findings.title: README is organised by linter; no reader can find themselves
findings.claim: README.md opens with the phrase, a 'what it is not' paragraph (line 16), then two install paths by linter (Stylelint 32-50, ESLint 52-74). The council's user, a design engineer whose scale lives in a token package (COUNCIL:63-65), gets one clause at line 91 and one Guides bullet (114); agents get one bullet (115). The words that persona searches for (DTCG, Style Dictionary, Figma, token package) never appear in README.md, although the first run finds and uses a DTCG file with provenance. No persona is named anywhere on the page, and the solo developer is never told what the tool does to their layout.
findings.evidence: README.md:7,16,18-74,91,114-115; `grep -n -i -E "dtcg|style dictionary|figma|token package" README.md` returns nothing; probe: `node src/cli/index.js` in /tmp/rg-review-positioning/ds-app (DTCG 2025.10 tokens/spacing.tokens.json) printed "Source  token-sources (tokens/spacing.tokens.json)" and scale 0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: A design engineer reading the first screen sees a 4px-default Stylelint rule and a hand-typed Tailwind scale array and files it as a solo-dev linter; the plan's own target cannot recognise the product built for them, and the other two personas have nothing addressed to them at all.
findings.proposal: Rewrite the top of README.md as a one-screen router: one promise sentence, then three doors by reader. "Your scale lives in a token file" (DTCG, Style Dictionary, @theme, Sass maps, 16 packages; embed config; CI gate). "You write CSS or Tailwind in a product repo" (npx rhythmguard, nearest-step finding, editor). "An agent writes your CSS" (init --agents, the AGENTS.md block, JSON contract). Each door: one command, one example finding, one link. Rules, Configs, Guides, Measured Type and Compatibility move below the fold or to docs. The door targets already exist: FOR_CONFIG_AUTHORS.md, FOR_AGENTS.md, CI_ADOPTION.md.
findings.truth_reason: Checked README.md lines 7, 16, 32-74, 91, 114-115; grep for DTCG, Style Dictionary, Figma and token package returns nothing. Re-ran the probe under /tmp/rg-verify-positioning/ds-app with a DTCG 2025.10 file: quickstart printed 'Source token-sources (tokens/spacing.tokens.json)' and scale 0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24. COUNCIL:63-65 user definition verified. The docs-and-onboarding map lists 'No persona router' as a gap; nothing in src or docs supplies one.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: README.md never mentions DTCG, Style Dictionary, Figma or token packages, names no persona, and gives the DS-team path one clause at line 91. Every persona meets this page first; the door targets (FOR_CONFIG_AUTHORS, FOR_AGENTS, CI_ADOPTION) exist, so a top-of-page router is cheap and stops the first-screen misread. Absorbs pos-12.
findings.relates_to: docs-and-onboarding map gap "No persona router"; docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:63-65 (user definition); docs/STRATEGY_2026-09.md 9.6

findings.title: Plan narrows to DS teams and bars the agent persona; goal needs both
findings.claim: The plan of record defines the user as a design engineer on a 1 to 6 person DS team with a token package (COUNCIL:63-65), records "the agent story has moved no human" (36), and stop-lists MCP, new agent-eval editions and a Figma bridge (98). #176 (MCP) can only be decided by an eval the stop list forbids running. The goal names any frontend developer and AI-assisted designers. The narrowing is unpublished (README never mentions team size or token packages), so the conflict is internal: the plan drops a persona the goal requires and leaves no way to re-admit it. The DS-team beachhead itself is sound: it is the only verified user and the only persona with a buyer.
findings.evidence: docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:36,63-65,98,160; ROADMAP.md:137; docs/AGENT_EVALS.md:25,39 (12-task hard suite never run); strategy-and-evidence map gaps 1 and 10
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: A #1 tool for AI-assisted designers cannot come from a plan that forbids the evidence needed to decide whether to serve them; and a beachhead that is never stated in public pulls no beachhead users either.
findings.proposal: Keep the beachhead and say it on the README (pos-01). Write COUNCIL Amendment 2 with one decision on the agent persona: (a) served through the same findings; deliverables are the AGENTS.md block, the three packs, the JSON contract and an agent setup page; MCP and evals wait for a named team; or (b) run one agent-eval edition with temptation prompts, five arms and five seeds (member C's design) before 2027-03-31 to settle #176 and the agent pitch. For the no-code designer (Lovable, v0, Figma Make) write the scope sentence: out of scope until those tools read a lint config. Either path is a decision, not code; the undecidable state is what must end.
findings.truth_reason: COUNCIL:36, 63-65, 98 (MCP, new agent-eval editions, Figma bridge stop-listed) and 160 verified; ROADMAP:137 ties #176 to an eval; AGENT_EVALS:25,39 describe the hard suite and docs/agent-evals/ holds only 2026-10-10. README has no team-size or token-package text. grep for lovable, v0, Figma Make, no-code across README, docs, packages and agents returns nothing, so no scope sentence exists. Strategy map gaps 1 and 10 agree.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified in COUNCIL: user narrowed to 1-6 person DS teams, 'the agent story has moved no human', MCP and eval editions stop-listed while #176 waits on an eval. A written decision moves no user directly, but it unblocks pos-06 and settles ai-assisted scope under the freeze; a prerequisite, not a deliverable.
findings.relates_to: Conflicts with docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:98 stop list (agent evals, MCP) under path (b); #176; #177

findings.title: Nearest-step messages no longer differentiate; the real wedge is unstated
findings.claim: README.md:14 and STRATEGY section 4 ("No competitor in either ecosystem does this") position scale-aware nearest-step reporting as the unique capability. oxlint-tailwindcss (1.19M downloads/month) prints "Closest in your theme: w-50.5 (202px) or w-51 (204px)" from the real @theme; @shadcn/lint suggests the equivalent step. What no competitor does: reject values against a restricted scale (p-13, p-3.25 off a 4px ladder), read that scale from a token file, and hold stylesheets and class strings to one scale. For Tailwind the ESLint rule checks only bracketed values and takes only a hand-typed array (ESLint README:35,93), so there the wedge is neither unique nor built; for CSS and SCSS it is real and under-sold.
findings.evidence: README.md:14,84; packages/eslint-plugin-rhythmguard/README.md:30-37,93; docs/STRATEGY_2026-09.md section 4 item 1; landscape map capability "oxlint-tailwindcss 1.17.1" (message text from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sergioazoc/oxlint-tailwindcss/main/packages/docs/rules/no-arbitrary-value.md); probe on /tmp/rg-review-positioning/tw-app: p-[13px] and gap-[18px] reported, p-3.25 not
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: A Tailwind developer already on oxlint-tailwindcss sees the same two-nearest-steps message and no reason for a second plugin; a design engineer is never told the scale can come from their token file, the one claim nobody else can make.
findings.proposal: Re-anchor the promise on the scale source: "reads the scale from your tokens; a value off it fails even when Tailwind can express it". Lead the ESLint README comparison with the p-3.25/p-13 row as the shared gap and state plainly: brackets today, v4 steps with a declared scale in 4.0 (or never, if the no-go stands; then say so). Date or delete "no competitor does this" in STRATEGY section 4. Add oxlint-tailwindcss with entryPoint as a column in the comparison table and in scripts/bench/tailwind-compare.mjs. Put the DTCG, Style Dictionary, @theme and Sass source list in the first paragraph of all three READMEs.
findings.correction: Nearest-step uniqueness is stale (oxlint-tailwindcss with entryPoint prints the closest theme steps) and the ESLint rule reads no token file, but the restricted-scale wedge is stated on README:14 and ESLint README:24-26. What is missing: the token-file sources (DTCG, Style Dictionary, @theme, Sass) in the root README's first paragraph (today only ESLint README:155 and rhythmguard README:42, below the fold), an oxlint-tailwindcss column in the table and compare script, and a date on STRATEGY section 4's claim.
findings.truth_reason: Verified STRATEGY:106 uniqueness claim, ESLint README:30-37 (no oxlint-tailwindcss column) and :93, the rule schema accepting only a scale array (src/eslint/rules/tailwind-class-use-scale.js:43-71), tailwind-compare.mjs covering three tools, and the probe (p-[13px], gap-[18px] reported; p-3.25, gap-4.5, p-13 not). But the restricted-scale wedge is already stated: README:14 'scale-aware rather than a blanket ban' and ESLint README:24-26 'is the value one of the steps your design system allows?'. 'Unstated' overreaches.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: STRATEGY:106 still claims no competitor reports nearest steps; oxlint-tailwindcss (1.19M/month) does from the real @theme. The true wedge (scale from a token file, restricted scale, one scale for CSS and classes) is absent from README.md and buried at ESLint README:155. Promise-level, all personas; overlaps pos-08 on wording and pos-04 on the oxlint column.
findings.relates_to: docs/ESLINT_PLAN.md:83-85 (items 1-3 not built after the no-go); #170; conflicts with Amendment 1's no-go if v4-step checking is built (M effort)

findings.title: COMPARISON.md compares complements and omits every substitute personas already run
findings.claim: docs/COMPARISON.md is titled "Defensive CSS vs Logical CSS vs Rhythmguard"; its matrix holds defensive-css, logical-css, stylelint-scales and @shadcn/lint. Missing: stylelint-declaration-strict-value (2.55M/month, listed three lines above Rhythmguard on awesome-stylelint), Stylelint 18's value-type-custom-property-required-list whose README says "length, so that spacing comes from your scale", declaration-property-custom-property-allowed-list, oxlint-tailwindcss, eslint-plugin-tailwindcss, better-tailwindcss, Biome's CSS rules and Terrazzo's token lint. The @shadcn/lint sentence ("reads the theme only for colors, radii and text sizes") is imprecise. The Tailwind recipe uses a v3 JS config path. The one page a buyer opens to justify a second plugin never mentions the free core rule.
findings.evidence: docs/COMPARISON.md:1,7-13,46,111-129; awesome-stylelint README lines 137-141 (strict-value, rhythmguard, stylelint-scales adjacent; fetched via gh api); https://github.com/stylelint/stylelint/blob/main/lib/rules/value-type-custom-property-required-list/README.md lines 14-17; landscape map quality notes 2 and 4; ecosystem map gap on strict-value (844 package.json repos)
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: Without a row that answers "why not the core rule, or the plugin we already run", a DS lead reads Rhythmguard as redundant with Stylelint 18 and removes it at the upgrade.
findings.proposal: Rewrite COMPARISON.md as "The tool you already have, and what Rhythmguard adds", one row per substitute with the same three inputs (padding: 13px; p-[13px]; --space-7: 26px): Stylelint 18 core (requires a var(); Rhythmguard says which value is off the scale, the two nearest steps and which token holds it; run both, pairing block included); strict-value (keep it, add use-scale); stylelint-scales (autofix, no tokens, no nearest step); oxlint-tailwindcss and @shadcn/lint (equivalent step from the theme, not a restricted scale from a token file); Terrazzo (lints the token file, not the CSS). Defensive and logical become a "pairs with" footnote. Add an oxlint-tailwindcss column to the ESLint README table.
findings.truth_reason: COMPARISON.md:1, 7-13, 46 and 111-129 verified as described. grep across README, docs/*.md, both package READMEs and docs/rules for strict-value, value-type-custom-property, oxlint-tailwindcss, better-tailwindcss, terrazzo and biome finds no user-facing coverage beyond the ESLint README's four-tool table. Fetched awesome-stylelint (strict-value line 137, rhythmguard 140, stylelint-scales 141) and the core rule README ('length, so that spacing comes from your scale'). Landscape and ecosystem maps agree.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: COMPARISON.md has no row for stylelint-declaration-strict-value (2.55M/month, 844 package.json repos), Stylelint 18 core, oxlint-tailwindcss or the Tailwind ESLint plugins, and its recipe uses a v3 config path. It is the buyer page linked from Guides; at the Stylelint 18 upgrade it decides keep-or-drop and names the cheapest acquisition channel.
findings.relates_to: #170; landscape map gap "Positioning against Stylelint 18 core"

findings.title: Stylelint 18 is the predicted positioning test; the front page fails it
findings.claim: Stylelint 18.0.0 shipped 2026-11-03 with a core rule pitched as "length, so that spacing comes from your scale"; stylelint-config-standard 41 peers on ^18. README.md:147 still says "Stylelint 16 and 17 ... 18.0.0-next.0 passes" and package.json:163 excludes 18. The council's kill clause (COUNCIL:113: "if Stylelint core ships a nearest-scale-step rule, deprecate use-scale") is close enough to the new rule that a reader will ask whether it tripped; no public text answers. 4.0 was pinned to "the week Stylelint 18.0.0 ships" (COUNCIL:75) and nothing of 4.0 exists. Every substitute plugin is also stuck on ^17, so the first to ship 18 support with the one-sentence split owns the slot.
findings.evidence: README.md:147; package.json:163; https://stylelint.io/migration-guide/to-18/; core rule README lines 14-17; docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:75,113; ecosystem-signals map gaps 1-2 (stylelint-scales, strict-value, defensive-css, logical-css all peer ^17)
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: A DS team upgrading to Stylelint 18 this month hits a peer conflict and meets a free core rule with a spacing pitch; if Rhythmguard's page cannot say in one sentence what it adds, the team drops it.
findings.proposal: Ship #168 (peer ^16||^17||^18, one CI row on Node 22/24/26 x Stylelint 18) as 3.18 now, decoupled from 4.0. Add a README "Stylelint 18" paragraph: core value-type-custom-property-required-list says "use a custom property"; use-scale says which value is off the scale and the two nearest steps; prefer-token says which token holds it; both read DTCG and Style Dictionary files core cannot; with a pairing config block. Add one dated line to COUNCIL stating the kill clause has not tripped (core has no scale and no nearest step) and what would trip it. Re-date 4.0 against the real Stylelint 18 release.
findings.correction: Three of the four substitute plugins are stuck on ^17 (stylelint-declaration-strict-value >=16 <=17, stylelint-plugin-defensive-css and stylelint-plugin-logical-css ^14 through ^17); stylelint-scales 6.0.0 declares no stylelint peer and installs under 18 without a conflict. The rest of the claim holds.
findings.truth_reason: README:147, package.json:163, ci.yml matrix (no Stylelint 18 row), COUNCIL:75,113 verified; stylelint-config-standard 41.0.0 peers ^18.0.0; #166 and #168 open per gh; no MIGRATING_TO_4.md, exported findingKey or message snapshot test. One error: stylelint-scales 6.0.0 declares no peerDependencies at all (registry JSON), so it installs under 18; strict-value (>=16 <=17), defensive-css and logical-css (^14 through ^17) are stuck. COUNCIL:21,89,162 note the v18 rules but give no dated kill-clause verdict.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: peer range ^16||^17, README:147 says 'Stylelint 16 and 17', #168 open, 4.0 pinned to a Stylelint 18 release that shipped 2026-11-03 with nothing of 4.0 built. A peer conflict is a hard install bounce for anyone on config-standard 41; the one-sentence split against the free core rule is the credibility test. Engines must rise to 22.22 too.
findings.relates_to: #168 (open); #172; docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:75 (4.0 date tied to a release that has now happened with 4.0 unbuilt)

findings.title: No agent-first front door while the agent-first competitor's quickstart is a prompt
findings.claim: @shadcn/lint's README quickstart is "Give your coding agent this prompt: Read SETUP.md and set up @shadcn/lint in this project"; oxlint-tailwindcss ships `npx skills add`. Rhythmguard has the ingredients (drift-tested SKILL.md, Cursor rule, Copilot block, JSON 2.0 contract, init --agents) but README.md gives agents one Guides bullet (115), no agent-readable setup page, and the pack's first instruction (`npx rhythmguard audit . --format json`) throws in an ESLint-only project. The README's own evidence line says findings made no difference in edition 1 (118). For the designer half of the persona (Lovable, v0, Figma Make) no surface exists and no page says so.
findings.evidence: README.md:115,118; docs/FOR_AGENTS.md:1-37; agents/claude-code/SKILL.md; `grep -rn -i -E "give your (coding )?agent|SETUP.md" README.md docs/*.md packages/*/README.md` returns nothing; https://github.com/shadcn-ui/lint README "Quickstart" (fetched via gh api); docs-and-onboarding map gap "agent pack throws without Stylelint"; landscape map gap "AI builders' guardrail files"
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The ai-assisted persona installs tools by asking the agent; a README with no prompt to paste, and a null-result eval on its first screen, loses to @shadcn/lint before any rule runs.
findings.proposal: Add docs/SETUP.md (about 20 lines) written for an agent: detect stack, install the right package, run quickstart, paste config, run init --agents, add the CI gate, with the ESLint-only branch. Put "Give your agent this prompt: read SETUP.md" as the second block of "Start here". Move the eval sentence from README to docs/AGENT_EVALS.md. State on the README which agent surfaces are served (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, any AGENTS.md reader) and that Lovable, v0 and Figma Make are out of scope until they read a lint config. Publish the skill on skills.sh once the repo rename lands. Needs no MCP and no eval.
findings.truth_reason: README:115,118 and FOR_AGENTS.md verified: paste block, pack install and command table, but no install or setup steps for the linters. grep for 'give your agent' and SETUP.md across README, docs and package READMEs returns nothing. agents/claude-code/SKILL.md:10 starts with the audit command; src/audit/scan/stylesheets.js:40-48 throws 'Auditing stylesheets needs Stylelint' and src/cli/audit.js:50-52 exits 1 (ESLint README:45 documents it). shadcn README lines 25-32 carry the exact agent prompt. No Lovable, v0 or Figma Make text anywhere.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: FOR_AGENTS.md:12 and SKILL.md tell agents to run `audit . --format json` first, which throws without Stylelint; README gives agents one bullet and puts the null eval result on the first screen. The ai-assisted persona installs by prompt and @shadcn/lint's quickstart is one. Small docs change, no MCP or eval, plan-compatible.
findings.relates_to: docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:98 (no MCP, no new evals; this needs neither); #176; docs-and-onboarding map gap "agent pack ESLint-only"

findings.title: Equal billing for an ESLint companion whose differentiators were never built
findings.claim: Amendment 1 item 8 (ESLINT_PLAN.md:90) gave ESLint equal billing on the repository README; README.md:14,52-74 deliver it. Phase 0 returned no-go on 2026-11-01, so items 1-4 (token-file scale, @theme reading, v4 steps, suggestion-only fixes) were not built. The ESLint rule still takes only a hand-typed scale array (README.md:69; ESLint README:93); the quickstart prints a different import (`stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard/eslint`, warn) than the README (`eslint-plugin-rhythmguard`, error); the 2027-03-31 demand test (400 aged weekly downloads, about 3 today) will be read as a verdict on distribution for a product half that never shipped.
findings.evidence: docs/ESLINT_PLAN.md:83-90,118-134,136-146; README.md:14,52-74; packages/eslint-plugin-rhythmguard/README.md:93; probe: quickstart on /tmp/rg-review-positioning/tw-app printed `import rhythmguard from 'stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard/eslint'` with severity 'warn'; strategy-and-evidence map gap on the demand test
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The largest persona by market (Tailwind with ESLint or Oxlint, about 66% of Tailwind package.json files) meets a front door that promises parity and hands them a scale array to maintain by hand; there is no second visit.
findings.proposal: Make billing match the build, one of two: (a) build `scale: "auto"`, `scaleSources` and `@theme` reading for the ESLint rule before 2027-03-31 so "one scale, two linters" is true for the reference user, then keep equal billing; or (b) demote the ESLint section to one paragraph under "Tailwind class strings" that states scope (bracketed arbitrary values, scale array, v4 steps unchecked) and keeps the comparison table as the pitch. Either way: one canonical import (`eslint-plugin-rhythmguard`), one severity, printed by the quickstart; and reword the demand test to name what was measured.
findings.truth_reason: ESLINT_PLAN:90 (item 8), :127-134 (no-go, items 1-4 unbuilt), :136-146 (demand test, about 3 of 400) and :28 verified; README:14, 52-74, 69 and ESLint README:93 verified; the rule schema accepts only a scale array. Probe quickstart on /tmp/rg-verify-positioning/tw-app printed `import rhythmguard from 'stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard/eslint'` with severity 'warn' (src/cli/quickstart.js:111-126) against README:62,69's `eslint-plugin-rhythmguard` at 'error'. README:54 says either import works, which does not remove the mismatch.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: ESLINT_PLAN item 8 gave equal billing, Phase 0 no-go left items 1-4 unbuilt, ESLint README:93 says the rule does not read the theme, quickstart prints `stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard/eslint` at warn while README prints `eslint-plugin-rhythmguard` at error. Largest persona by market meets a hand-typed array. Option (a) conflicts with the no-go; (b) is plan-consistent.
findings.relates_to: docs/ESLINT_PLAN.md Phase 0 no-go (option (a) reopens items 1-3); Amendment 1 item 8; docs-and-onboarding map gap "two import paths"; option (b) is S

findings.title: Six second sentences after the phrase; GitHub about carries council jargon
findings.claim: "Nobody chose 13px" is consistent; what follows differs on every surface: README.md:7, package.json:4, the live GitHub about (which appends STRATEGY section 4's "deterministic scale and token drift governance ... for measurement and ratcheting"; DISTRIBUTION.md:9 records a shorter text), the banner alt ("stable local evidence for design system drift"), both companion READMEs, awesome-stylelint and the playground meta. "Governance", "deterministic", "token opps" and "cleanliness" are on public surfaces. No maintainer reply in the outreach log uses "drift", "ratchet" or "governance"; they say scale, tokens, grid-unit, spacer, off-scale. "Ratchet" appears in one hand-rolled team's issue (quasar#370); "scale ratchet" only in COUNCIL. "8pt grid" appears nowhere, though stylelint-8-point-grid draws 26,680 downloads/month on that phrase.
findings.evidence: README.md:2,7; package.json:4; `gh api repos/PetriLahdelma/stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard --jq .description` (live two-sentence about); docs/DISTRIBUTION.md:9; packages/rhythmguard/README.md:7; packages/eslint-plugin-rhythmguard/README.md:7; docs/index.html:6-9; awesome-stylelint line 140; docs/outreach/embed-log.md:19,79,85,96,100; quickstart output "Token opps", "Cleanliness 0%"; https://github.com/accreleus/quasar/issues/370; api.npmjs.org last-month stylelint-8-point-grid 26,680 vs stylelint-scales 5,997; grep for "8pt|8-point|grid" on README, companions, index.html, package.json returns nothing
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: A tool found through eight channels should sound like one product; "drift governance for measurement and ratcheting" is the council's language, and it is the first sentence GitHub search shows.
findings.proposal: Fix one promise sentence and use it verbatim on all eight surfaces, for example: "Nobody chose 13px. Rhythmguard reads the spacing scale from your tokens and holds your CSS, your Tailwind classes and your coding agent to it: nearest step in the editor, only new drift fails CI." Replace the GitHub about with it; make DISTRIBUTION.md match the live text. Keep "drift" (OverlayQA, Supernova, Knapsack use it) and "off-scale" (maintainers use it); retire "governance", "deterministic" and "token opps" from user-facing text and rename "cleanliness" in 4.0 under the message freeze. Add "4px grid" and "8pt grid" to the README body and npm keywords.
findings.correction: 'Scale ratchet' appears in COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:57,130 and in ROADMAP.md:9 and :77 ('Rhythmguard is the scale ratchet for CSS, SCSS and Tailwind'), all internal planning text; it is still absent from every user-facing surface and every maintainer reply. The rest of the claim holds.
findings.truth_reason: gh api returns the live about: the DISTRIBUTION.md:9 text plus STRATEGY:102's 'deterministic scale and token drift governance ... measurement and ratcheting'. README:2,7, package.json:4, both companion READMEs, index.html:6-9 and awesome-stylelint line 140 all differ. Probe output shows 'Token opps' and 'Cleanliness 0%'. No 8pt or 8-point text anywhere; stylelint-8-point-grid 26,680 vs stylelint-scales 5,997 confirmed. No maintainer row in embed-log uses drift, ratchet or governance. One slip: 'scale ratchet' also appears in ROADMAP.md:9,77.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: the live GitHub about appends 'deterministic scale and token drift governance... measurement and ratcheting', unlike DISTRIBUTION.md; package.json, banner alt and companion READMEs each differ; '8pt grid' and '4px grid' appear nowhere though stylelint-8-point-grid draws about 30k/month on that phrase. Cheap and discovery-facing; take the sentence from pos-03.
findings.relates_to: docs/STRATEGY_2026-09.md 9.6 ("one phrase, everywhere"); docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:71 (message text frozen in patches; CLI label changes wait for a minor or 4.0)

findings.title: README leads with the fix buyers reject and buries the ratchet
findings.claim: README.md:7 promises "snaps to them or to your tokens when you ask"; section order is Start here, Rules, Configs, then Audit (93). The council records "the ratchet and baseline are the core value; teams will not accept fixes that move layout" (COUNCIL:41); USWDS closed the audit issue because token replacements moved spacing (embed-log:96) and Materialize asked for before/after screenshots (100); #166 --preserve is unbuilt. The Action, badge, baselines and --fail-on-new-drift, the ds-team's buying reasons, sit in the fourth section after a rule table. Nothing on the first screen answers "will it change my layout".
findings.evidence: README.md:7,76-106; docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:41,77; docs/outreach/embed-log.md:96,100; https://github.com/PetriLahdelma/stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard/issues/166 (open; strategy map: grep of src/cli for preserve returns nothing)
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The buyer approving a blocking CI gate asks first whether the tool will move pixels; the first sentence says it snaps, and the answer they want (report, baseline, gate, one reviewed fix at a time) is below the fold.
findings.proposal: Reorder the README: promise; "In CI" as the second block (Action one-liner, `--since-baseline --fail-on-new-drift`, badge); editor rules third; `fix` last as "one decision, one reviewable change" (the line 106 sentence promoted). Reword the promise so the fix is opt-in. Until #166 ships, state the layout guarantee honestly on the first screen: fixes are off by default; `fix` changes one value per run and shows the diff; output-preserving token swaps (--preserve, #166) are planned.

findings.title: Seven identifiers for one product, named after the host most users skip
findings.claim: A README reader meets stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard (repo, package, H1), rhythmguard (command, package), eslint-plugin-rhythmguard, stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard/eslint, rhythmguard/ (Stylelint rule prefix), rhythmguard-tailwind/ (ESLint plugin key) and rhythmguard-action. The GIF and playground say `npx stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard`; the text says `npx rhythmguard`. The rhythmguard package hard-depends on stylelint, so `npx rhythmguard` in an ESLint-only project installs Stylelint. GitHub search for "rhythmguard" returns 12 repos, 8 unrelated (empty RhythmGuard repos, an ESP32 alarm, a readmission model, a Godot game); npm search returns only the three packages; rhythmguard.dev/.com/.io are unregistered. The 4.0 rename to `rhythmguard` is planned; unifying the two rule namespaces is not.
findings.evidence: README.md:5,21,27,62,68,80,84,104 (grep count: 10 stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard, 6 eslint-plugin-rhythmguard, 3 rhythmguard-tailwind/); src/eslint/index.js:18; packages/rhythmguard/package.json dependencies (stylelint, stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard); docs/index.html:439,515; `gh api "search/repositories?q=rhythmguard"` total_count 12; `dig +short rhythmguard.dev A` empty (same for .com, .io)
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: A first-choice tool has one name people say and one command they type; the name a Tailwind or Oxlint developer sees first is "stylelint", the thing they do not run, and an agent told to "add rhythmguard" has four plausible package names to guess.
findings.proposal: Treat the 4.0 engine split (ESLINT_PLAN.md:96-102) as the naming release: product and repo `rhythmguard`; stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard and eslint-plugin-rhythmguard as adapters; one rule namespace `rhythmguard/` in both linters with `rhythmguard-tailwind/` kept as an alias through 4.x; README H1 "Rhythmguard". Before 4.0: register rhythmguard.dev and point it at the playground (STRATEGY 9.6's "one home"); re-record the GIF and fix the playground strip to `npx rhythmguard`; make the rhythmguard wrapper's stylelint dependency optional. Do not rename the product: the npm namespace is clean and the GitHub collisions are empty repos.
findings.correction: rhythmguard.dev is unregistered (RDAP 404) and remains the domain to register; rhythmguard.com has been registered since 2015 (GoDaddy, expires 2027-03-06, AWS nameservers, no A record), and rhythmguard.io could not be verified (dig empty; .io RDAP unreachable). An empty `dig +short` shows no A record, not an unregistered name. README mentions: 22 stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard (14 lines, mostly URLs), 6 eslint-plugin-rhythmguard, 3 rhythmguard-tailwind/.
findings.truth_reason: All seven identifiers found at README:5,21,27,62,68,80,84,104 and src/eslint/index.js:18; packages/rhythmguard/package.json hard-depends on stylelint; index.html:439,515 say npx stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard; gh search returns 12 repos; npm search returns the three packages; ESLINT_PLAN:96-102 plans the rename, nothing plans one rule namespace. Two errors: RDAP shows rhythmguard.com registered (GoDaddy, 2015-03-06 to 2027-03-06, AWS nameservers, no A record); only rhythmguard.dev is confirmed free, .io unverifiable. README counts are 22/6/3 occurrences, not 10/6/3.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: seven identifiers, playground strip and GIF alt say `npx stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard`, the rhythmguard wrapper hard-depends on stylelint, 8 of 12 GitHub name hits are unrelated. The rename is already planned for 4.0 (ESLINT_PLAN:96-102) and the pre-4.0 pieces are small; an agent guessing package names is real friction, but pos-06's SETUP.md removes most of it.
findings.relates_to: docs/ESLINT_PLAN.md:96-102 (rename planned for 4.0); ROADMAP.md:100; docs-and-onboarding map gap "two command names"; namespace alias at 4.0 is M

findings.title: Quickstart pastes configs that need packages it never says to install
findings.claim: The no-arg run ends with "Paste this into .stylelintrc.json" and "Lint with the config above: npx stylelint \"**/*.css\"" but prints no install line. Following doctor's fix line instead (`npm install --save-dev stylelint`) installs Stylelint 18.0.0, outside the plugin's ^16||^17 peer range, so the next `npm install --save-dev stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard` dies with ERESOLVE. The pasted `configs/tailwind` needs stylelint-config-tailwindcss, which no CLI output names; the ESLint snippet imports `stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard/eslint` without an install line. README.md:35 happens to resolve 17.16.0 because both packages are installed in one command; the CLI never prints that command.
findings.evidence: p1: `npm install --save-dev stylelint` -> stylelint 18.0.0; `npx stylelint "src/**/*.css"` -> `ConfigurationError: Could not find "stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard/configs/recommended"` exit 78; `npm install --save-dev stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard` -> `npm error ERESOLVE ... Found: stylelint@18.0.0 ... peerOptional stylelint@"^16.0.0 || ^17.0.0" from stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard@3.17.0`. p3: `npx stylelint "**/*.css"` with init's tailwind config -> `ConfigurationError: Could not find "stylelint-config-tailwindcss"` exit 78. src/cli/quickstart.js:138-146 (nextCommands, no install line); src/cli/doctor.js:67; src/audit/scan/stylesheets.js:47; src/configs/tailwind.js:6; package.json peerDependencies stylelint ^16||^17.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The pitch is "no install, no config"; the first command after the pitch ends in a Stylelint stack trace or an npm ERESOLVE. A developer who has to reverse-engineer the dependency list from an error never reaches the findings, and an agent following the printed steps loops on the same error.
findings.proposal: Quickstart prints one install line computed from what it scanned, directly above the paste block: `npm install --save-dev stylelint@17 stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard`, plus `postcss-scss` when .scss files were seen, `stylelint-config-tailwindcss` when the tailwind profile is pasted, and `eslint eslint-plugin-rhythmguard typescript-eslint` when the ESLint snippet is printed. The range comes from package.json peerDependencies, not a literal. doctor.js:67 and stylesheets.js:47 name both packages with the pinned range. Add a contract test: every package referenced by a pasted config or snippet appears in the printed install line. Separately decide whether 4.0 supports Stylelint 18 (landscape map), since `npm install stylelint` now defaults to it.
findings.truth_reason: Reproduced on clean installs: `npm install --save-dev stylelint` gave 18.0.0, then installing the plugin failed ERESOLVE (Found: stylelint@18.0.0); README:35 one-command install resolved 17.16.0. Tailwind paste on a clean stylelint 17 + plugin install: `Could not find "stylelint-config-tailwindcss"` exit 78. quickstart.js:138-146 prints no install line; doctor.js:67 and stylesheets.js:47 name only stylelint; ESLint snippet imports the subpath (quickstart.js:115) with no install line.
findings.materiality_reason: First command every Stylelint-path user runs after the pitch; verified: quickstart prints no install line, doctor's fix line now resolves Stylelint 18 (outside ^16||^17, ERESOLVE), tailwind config hard-extends stylelint-config-tailwindcss. Blocks all three personas before any finding is seen. Compounds with dx-04, dx-05, dx-07. Touches #168 (Stylelint 18 range).
findings.relates_to: docs-and-onboarding gap (quickstart omits stylelint-config-tailwindcss); landscape map (Stylelint 18.0.0 shipped 2026-11-03 outside the peer range); ecosystem-signals; no issue

findings.title: Pasted scale auto config does not reproduce the report it came from
findings.claim: Quickstart found the scale in src/tokens.css (p1) and src/styles/_variables.scss (p2) yet printed "Token files none found" and pasted `scale: "auto"` without `scaleSources`, because its token-file search matches only `*tokens*.json`. The Stylelint rule infers per linted file, so every file that does not itself define the tokens falls back to rhythmic-4: 40px passes in the editor and fails in the audit, and each file carries a fallback note. Writing `scaleSources` to the file the audit already reports as `scale.files` made the editor show the audit's exact findings (8 of 8 in p1, 10 of 10 in p2).
findings.evidence: p1 quickstart: `Token files     none found` then `Source          scanned-css (src/tokens.css)`. `npx stylelint "**/*.css"` with the pasted config: `src/app.css 9:12 ✖ Unexpected off-scale value "13px" ... No spacing tokens were found for scale "auto"; using preset "rhythmic-4"`, `✖ 7 problems` vs audit 8 (missing `src/app.css:15 padding 40px`). With `"scaleSources": ["./src/tokens.css"]`: `✖ 8 problems` incl. `15:12 ✖ "40px" ... (nearest: 32px)`. p2 with postcss-scss: three files print the fallback note, 9 problems vs audit 10; with `scaleSources: ["./src/styles/_variables.scss"]`: 10 problems, 0 fallback notes, `17:12 ✖ "40px"`. src/cli/quickstart.js:29 (TOKEN_FILE_PATTERN), 97-101, 182; comment at 91-96 promises reproduction.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The quickstart's contract is "the pasted config reproduces this report". When editor and CI disagree on the same file within ten minutes, the solo dev reads the tool as flaky, the DS team cannot ratchet, and an agent's fix loop chases two scales.
findings.proposal: In suggestedStylelintConfig, set `scaleSources` from `report.scale.files` whenever `scale.source` is `scanned-css` or `token-sources` (CSS, SCSS and JSON paths all work as scaleSources, verified), and list those files under "Token files". Pass the same files as `--token-source` in the Next commands so audit, Stylelint and the baseline share one scale. Add a quickstart test that lints each fixture with the pasted config through Stylelint and asserts the problem count equals the audit's off-scale count.
findings.truth_reason: p1 (tokens in src/tokens.css): quickstart printed `Token files none found` yet `Source scanned-css (src/tokens.css)` and pasted `scale: "auto"` without scaleSources. Stylelint: 6 problems with the rhythmic-4 fallback note vs audit 7 (40px missing); with scaleSources ./src/tokens.css: 7 incl. 40px, no note. p2 SCSS: 9 problems, 3 notes vs audit 10; with _variables.scss: 10, 0 notes. TOKEN_FILE_PATTERN quickstart.js:29 matches JSON only. Counts are fixture-dependent.
findings.materiality_reason: Token-file search is /(^|[.-])tokens?\.json$/, so CSS, SCSS and @theme sources (the common case) never reach scaleSources; editor and audit disagree on the same file within minutes. Breaks the quickstart's core contract for all three personas: ds-team cannot ratchet, agents chase two scales. Small fix; compounds with dx-06 and dx-10.
findings.relates_to: scale-and-tokens gap (rule infers from the linted file only); #246; #196; #172

findings.title: Installing the ESLint plugin breaks npx rhythmguard and the agent pack
findings.claim: `npm install --save-dev eslint eslint-plugin-rhythmguard` (README.md:57) pulls stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard and its `rhythmguard` bin into node_modules/.bin, which npx prefers over the wrapper package. From then on `npx rhythmguard` (README.md:21), the agent pack's `npx rhythmguard audit . --format json`, and doctor's own quickstart all exit 1 with "Auditing stylesheets needs Stylelint" because one .css file exists, which every Tailwind v4 app has. doctor's ESLint-only mode prints "All checks passed" in the same state. The pack never mentions `npx eslint`.
findings.evidence: p3c (clean package.json): `npm install --save-dev eslint eslint-plugin-rhythmguard` -> `added 116 packages`; `ls node_modules/.bin | grep rhythm` -> rhythmguard; no node_modules/stylelint. `npx rhythmguard` -> `Quickstart could not audit /private/tmp/rg-review-first-run/p3c-eslint-only: Auditing stylesheets needs Stylelint, which this project does not have. Install it with: npm install --save-dev stylelint` exit 1. `npx rhythmguard audit . --format json` -> same, exit 1. `npx rhythmguard doctor` -> `✓ eslint installed (v10.14.0) / ✓ ESLint config references rhythmguard (eslint.config.js) / All checks passed.` exit 0. src/audit/scan/stylesheets.js:44-48; agents/claude-code/SKILL.md:10; packages/rhythmguard/README.md:46; packages/eslint-plugin-rhythmguard/README.md:45.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The ESLint plugin is first-class per Amendment 1 and the ai-assisted persona's entry point. The moment it is installed, the headline command and the installed agent instructions stop working, while doctor says everything is fine; an agent cannot recover from that.
findings.proposal: Make the audit degrade instead of throw: when Stylelint cannot be loaded, still scan class strings (no Stylelint needed), count stylesheets under `scanned.stylesheetsSkipped` with the reason and install command (the existing SCSS-skip pattern), and exit 0 unless a gate flag is set. In that state quickstart prints the ESLint snippet first and the Stylelint path as optional, with the install line from dx-01. The agent pack gains one bullet: in an ESLint-only project run `npx eslint .`. doctor's ESLint-only mode states what `npx rhythmguard` will and will not audit. Test: the p3c sequence ends with exit 0 and 4 class-string findings.
findings.truth_reason: Clean dir, `npm install --save-dev eslint eslint-plugin-rhythmguard`: node_modules/.bin/rhythmguard present, no stylelint. `npx rhythmguard` and `npx rhythmguard audit . --format json` both exit 1 with `Auditing stylesheets needs Stylelint`; `npx rhythmguard doctor` prints `All checks passed` exit 0. SKILL.md:10 has the audit command, no `npx eslint`. Minor: CHANGELOG.md:32 is the 3.16.1 entry, not 3.17.0.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: the root package ships bin rhythmguard and eslint-plugin-rhythmguard depends on it, so a local .bin shadows the wrapper and the audit throws without Stylelint on any .css file. The README's ESLint install, the ai-assisted entry, breaks the headline command and the agent pack while doctor says passed. Degrade-not-throw is small.
findings.relates_to: docs-and-onboarding gap (agent pack's audit command throws without Stylelint); CHANGELOG.md:32 (3.17.0 chose the message over the behaviour); docs/ESLINT_PLAN.md Amendment 1

findings.title: Tailwind v4 TSX project: the pasted ESLint snippet lints nothing
findings.claim: The quickstart scanned 3 .tsx files and found 4 class-string findings, then pasted an eslint.config.js with `files: ['**/*.{js,jsx,mjs,cjs}']` and an import from `stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard/eslint`. With eslint and that package installed, `npx eslint .` exits 0 and prints nothing; `npx eslint "src/**/*.tsx"` says every file is ignored. Reaching the 4 warnings took installing @typescript-eslint/parser and hand-writing a block. README.md:66 has the same glob. `p-3.25`, `mt-13` and `gap-4.5` in Card.tsx were reported by no surface at all.
findings.evidence: p3: `npx eslint .` -> exit 0, empty output. `npx eslint "src/**/*.tsx"` -> `You are linting "src/**/*.tsx", but all of the files matching the glob pattern "src/**/*.tsx" are ignored.` exit 2. With `files: ['**/*.{ts,tsx}']` and `parser: tsParser`: `src/components/Button.tsx 5:23 warning Unexpected Tailwind arbitrary spacing value "p-[13px]". Use "p-3" (12px) or "p-3.5" (14px)` and 3 more, `✖ 4 problems (0 errors, 4 warnings)`; Card.tsx `p-3.25 mt-13 gap-4.5` absent from quickstart, audit and ESLint output. src/cli/quickstart.js:111-129 (eslintSnippet hard-codes the glob and the subpath import); README.md:54-74; packages/eslint-plugin-rhythmguard/README.md:84-88.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: Tailwind v4 plus TSX is the default output of v0, Lovable, Figma Make and Claude Code, the exact generated code the ai-assisted persona wants gated. A snippet that silently lints nothing is zero enforcement with a green exit code.
findings.proposal: Quickstart already knows which template extensions it scanned; emit the matching block: for .ts/.tsx, `files: ['**/*.{ts,tsx}']`, `import tseslint from 'typescript-eslint'`, `languageOptions: { parser: tseslint.parser }`, import from `eslint-plugin-rhythmguard` (the README's name) at the README's severity, and the install line `npm install --save-dev eslint eslint-plugin-rhythmguard typescript-eslint`. Add `Lint class strings: npx eslint .` to Next. Test: run ESLint with the pasted snippet on the TSX fixture and assert 4 findings. v4 step classes (p-3.25, mt-13) are a separate decision that Phase 0 declined; record it in relates_to rather than bundling it here.
findings.correction: The pasted snippet lints nothing in a TSX project (verified), but the quickstart is not silent about it: lines 267-268 print "TypeScript, Vue, Svelte and Astro files need their parser in a block of their own; see the eslint-plugin-rhythmguard README, 'Other file types'". The gap is that it prints that caveat instead of the TS block even though it counted 3 .tsx template files and 0 .jsx; `npx eslint .` with the snippet alone still exits 0 with no output.
findings.truth_reason: Reproduced: quickstart scanned 3 .tsx files, pasted `files: ['**/*.{js,jsx,mjs,cjs}']`; `npx eslint .` exit 0, empty; `npx eslint "src/**/*.tsx"` says all files ignored, exit 2; a typescript-eslint parser block gives the warnings; p-3.25/mt-13/gap-4.5 reported nowhere. But the claim omits that quickstart.js:267-268 prints a two-line caveat pointing at the README's TS block.
findings.materiality_reason: Quickstart knows it scanned .tsx yet pastes a js/jsx-only block importing the Stylelint subpath; npx eslint . exits 0 on a Tailwind v4 TSX app, the default output of v0, Lovable and Claude Code. A prose pointer to Other file types exists, but an agent pastes the snippet and sees green. v4 step classes stay with Phase 0.
findings.relates_to: docs-and-onboarding gap (two ESLint import paths); eslint-and-tailwind map (v4 step classes never checked); docs/ESLINT_PLAN.md Phase 0 no-go conflicts with the v4-step part only

findings.title: SCSS projects get an empty first run and a lint command that finds nothing
findings.claim: The published `npx rhythmguard` (103 packages, no postcss-scss) in an SCSS-only project reports 0 CSS files, 5 skipped, cleanliness 100%, yet pastes a config without `customSyntax` and says `npx stylelint "**/*.css"`, which throws NoFilesFoundError. No output names postcss-scss as something to install; init writes no customSyntax; doctor checks postcss-scss only after customSyntax is already in the config. The README's own showcase project (Bootstrap) is Sass.
findings.evidence: p2 cold `npx --yes rhythmguard@3.17.0` (fresh cache, 2.94 s): `CSS files       0 / Skipped         5 not audited (5 SCSS without postcss-scss) / Cleanliness     100%` then `Lint with the config above: npx stylelint "**/*.css"`; `ls npm-cache/_npx/*/node_modules/postcss-scss` -> No such file or directory. After installing stylelint@17 and the plugin: `npx stylelint "**/*.css"` -> `NoFilesFoundError: No files matching the pattern "**/*.css" were found.` exit 1; with `"customSyntax": "postcss-scss"` uninstalled -> `Error: Cannot resolve custom syntax module "postcss-scss"` exit 1. packages/rhythmguard/package.json:27-30; src/cli/quickstart.js:142, 229-235; src/cli/init.js:375; src/cli/doctor.js:258.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: Bootstrap, Angular Material, GOV.UK and most established design systems are Sass. A DS engineer whose first run says 100% clean on zero files, then whose lint command finds no files, has no reason to run a second command.
findings.proposal: Add `postcss-scss` to the `rhythmguard` wrapper's dependencies (one package, 181 ms install) so the published quickstart audits SCSS. When `scanned.scssFiles > 0`, quickstart and init write `"customSyntax": "postcss-scss"`, use the glob `"**/*.{css,scss}"`, and include `postcss-scss` in the install line (dx-01); the Skipped line names the install command. doctor warns when .scss files exist and no customSyntax is configured. Test: the p2 fixture through the published wrapper reports 10 off-scale values, not 0.
findings.correction: Replace "No output names postcss-scss as something to install" with: the quickstart's Skipped line names it only as the reason ("5 SCSS without postcss-scss") and `rhythmguard audit` text prints "(install postcss-scss to audit them)" (render-text.js:23); neither prints an install command, and the pasted config and lint glob still ignore SCSS. Rest of the claim holds; docs-and-onboarding open question 1 is answered yes.
findings.truth_reason: Cold `npx --yes rhythmguard@3.17.0` (fresh cache, 103 packages, no postcss-scss) on SCSS-only p2: CSS files 0, Skipped 5, Cleanliness 100%, config without customSyntax, `npx stylelint "**/*.css"` then NoFilesFoundError exit 1; unresolvable customSyntax errors exit 1; init writes no customSyntax; doctor skips the check unless configured. One sentence overstates: output does name postcss-scss.
findings.materiality_reason: Published wrapper lacks postcss-scss, so an SCSS-only project (Bootstrap, GOV.UK, half the quiet benchmark) gets 0 files, 100% clean, then NoFilesFoundError; init and doctor never mention customSyntax. First run, large population, one dependency fix. Compounds with dx-09 and dx-12. #196 covers inference, not the parser.
findings.relates_to: docs-and-onboarding open question 1 (now answered: yes, every .scss is skipped); #196; packages/rhythmguard/README.md:50

(nearest: 32px)`. p4 `printf 'y\ny\n' | node cli init` -> `⚠ Existing Stylelint config found. Overwrite? (y/n)` then the file holds only extends + ignoreFiles, `scaleSources` gone. src/configs/recommended.js:10 ([0..64]); src/audit/shared.js:7 ([0..32]); src/core/scale-inference.js:33 (rhythmic-4); src/cli/init.js:327-331, 352-363.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: 40px reported by one command and accepted by the next reads as a broken tool, not a misconfigured one. It is the fastest way a first-day user decides the findings are noise and uninstalls.
findings.proposal: init stops owning a scale: it runs the same detection and inference as quickstart (createAuditReport with scale auto) and writes exactly the config quickstart would paste, scale or scaleSources included; quickstart gains `--write` to do both in one step. Export one DEFAULT_SCALE used by the audit, the ESLint rule and the recommended config until #172 fixes the 4.0 value. When a config exists, init prints the diff before asking. Contract test: init's file equals quickstart's paste on every fixture.
findings.correction: On a fallback project (p5b) quickstart pastes the literal DEFAULT_SCALE, not `scale: "auto"`, so its paste reproduces the audit (6 of 6) and the split there is audit/quickstart (0..32) vs init's recommended (0..64). The `scale: "auto"` falling back to rhythmic-4 in Stylelint happens on a scanned-css project (p1: 6 problems with the fallback note vs audit 7), which is dx-02's case. The init overwrite losing scaleSources is confirmed.
findings.truth_reason: p5b reproduced: audit 6 off-scale (10,13,20,40,48,64, source default); init config (extends recommended only) 3 problems; quickstart config 6. init on an existing config with scaleSources: two y answers overwrote it to extends-only, no diff shown. recommended.js:10, shared.js:7, scale-inference.js:33, init.js:327-331/352-371 cited correctly. One clause misstates what quickstart pastes on a fallback project.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: audit DEFAULT_SCALE 0..32, recommended 0..64, init writes extends only and overwrites a quickstart config without a diff; 40px flips between commands on day one. Making init write quickstart's paste is small and clean. Unifying DEFAULT_SCALE into the recommended config before 4.0 changes existing findings and conflicts with #172 and the freeze.

findings.title: Doctor says all checks passed on a setup Stylelint cannot load
findings.claim: doctor checks that `stylelint` resolves and that the config text contains "rhythmguard". It never resolves stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard, the `extends` targets, or the Stylelint peer range, and never runs Stylelint. With Stylelint 18.0.0 installed, init's config present and the plugin absent, doctor exits 0 with "All checks passed" while `npx stylelint` exits 78. It says nothing about which scale the config will use or where it comes from.
findings.evidence: p1b: `node cli doctor` -> `✓ stylelint installed (v18.0.0) / ✓ config found (.stylelintrc.json) / ✓ config references rhythmguard / ... / All checks passed.` exit 0; `npx stylelint "src/**/*.css"` -> `ConfigurationError: Could not find "stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard/configs/recommended"` exit 78. `grep -n "installedVersion(" src/cli/doctor.js` -> only lines 60 (stylelint), 413, 421 (eslint); no plugin resolution. src/cli/doctor.js:58-70, 160-170. p4 after a correct setup: doctor passes but never prints the scale or tokens/tokens.json.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: doctor is the last line of every quickstart ("Check the setup"). A green doctor on a red setup teaches the newcomer that the tool's own diagnostics lie, and an agent that reads exit 0 moves on with nothing enforced.
findings.proposal: doctor resolves `stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard` from cwd and checks the installed Stylelint against the plugin's peerDependencies range; resolves every `extends` entry and `customSyntax` through Stylelint's resolver; warns when .scss files exist without a customSyntax; then lints one scanned stylesheet through `stylelint.lint` with the active config to prove it loads, and prints the scale and its source from the same inference the rule will use. Fail lines keep exact `npm install` commands with the pinned range. Test: the p1b state exits 1 with the plugin named.
findings.truth_reason: p1b (Stylelint 17.16.0 resolvable, init config, plugin absent): doctor printed `All checks passed`, exit 0; `stylelint` gave `ConfigurationError: Could not find "stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard/configs/recommended"` exit 78. installedVersion call sites are 60, 413, 421; no plugin resolution, no peer-range check, no stylelint.lint call anywhere in doctor.js. p4 with a correct scaleSources config: doctor passes without printing the scale or the token file.
findings.materiality_reason: Doctor only checks that stylelint resolves and the config text mentions rhythmguard; it never resolves the plugin, extends targets or peer range, and never lints. Trust hit on the last quickstart step, compounding with dx-01, but Stylelint then fails loudly (exit 78), so nobody is stranded. Fewer users reach doctor than the install step; effort M.
findings.relates_to: audit-and-cli gap (doctor cannot say whether the setup will produce the right findings); dx-01

findings.title: The CI gate fails the fix the finding recommends
findings.claim: Quickstart's last steps are `--write-baseline` then "gate only new drift". Changing `padding: 13px` to `12px`, exactly what "nearest: 12px or 16px" says, yields "2 resolved, 1 new" and exit 1, because prefer-token now reports `12px` as a raw scale value. Writing `var(--space-3)` passes although no CSS in the DTCG project defines `--space-3`. In the same report prefer-token says "No known token holds this value" for 24px while `rawValueMatches` lists 24px as `--space-6` from tokens.json: the audit never passes its token sources to prefer-token.
findings.evidence: p4: `audit . --scale auto --token-source ./tokens/tokens.json --since-baseline .rhythmguard-baseline.json --fail-on-new-drift` after 13px->12px: `Since baseline 2 resolved, 1 new / Audit failed: new drift found: 1 finding(s) not present in baseline` exit 1; newFindings[0]: `"rule": "rhythmguard/prefer-token", "text": "Unexpected raw scale value \"12px\". No known token holds this value; use the nearest token or add one."`; after 12px->var(--space-3): `2 resolved, 0 new` exit 0. JSON: `app/page.module.css:2 ... "24px". No known token holds this value` vs `rawValueMatches: [{"value":"24px","tokens":["--space-6"]}]`. src/audit/scan/stylesheets.js:79-88 (prefer-token gets tokenMapFromCssCustomProperties only); src/audit/baseline.js:233-239.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: "Fix loops that converge" is the ai-assisted persona's whole ask. A gate that rejects the recommended fix and accepts a reference to a token no CSS defines trains agents to cheat or loop, and a DS team sees the ratchet block the right change.
findings.proposal: (1) `--fail-on-new-drift` counts only `off-scale` and `tailwind` findings as drift; token-opportunity findings stay in the report and out of the gate, with an opt-in `--fail-on-new-token-debt`. (2) In the audit, feed the token definitions resolved from token sources into prefer-token's token map so the message names the token (`use --space-3`) and `fixWith: "token"` can act. (3) When a token exists only in a token file, say so: "defined in tokens/tokens.json, not emitted to CSS". Test: the p4 sequence (13px -> 12px) exits 0 and names --space-3.
findings.truth_reason: p4 (DTCG tokens/tokens.json) reproduced exactly: after 13px to 12px, `Since baseline 2 resolved, 1 new`, exit 1, the new finding is prefer-token `Unexpected raw scale value "12px". No known token holds this value`; 12px to var(--space-3) gives 2 resolved, 0 new, exit 0 though no CSS defines it; 24px reported as no known token while rawValueMatches lists --space-6. stylesheets.js:79-88 passes only tokenMapFromCssCustomProperties; baseline.js:233-239 counts all findings; test line 942 locks it.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: the baseline counts every css finding including prefer-token twins, and the audit passes no token sources to prefer-token. The ratchet rejects the exact fix the finding recommends and says no token exists for a value tokens.json defines. That is the 4.0 thesis (CI ratchet) and the ai-assisted convergence ask failing together.
findings.relates_to: audit-and-cli gaps (ratchet counts an on-scale literal as new drift; every literal reported twice); test/cli/audit-cli.test.js:942 locks the double report; docs/FOR_AGENTS.md:13

findings.title: Zero files scanned reports 100% clean and passes every gate
findings.claim: In an empty project the quickstart suggests `npx rhythmguard audit ./src`, which fails with "Directory not found: ./src"; `audit .` prints "No issues found. Your design-system rhythm is clean." with cleanliness 100% on 0 files, and `--min-cleanliness 100` exits 0. A typo in a CI path, the wrong workspace, or every SCSS file skipped (dx-05) looks like a clean design system.
findings.evidence: p5: `node cli audit ./src` -> `Directory not found: ./src` exit 1; `node cli audit . --min-cleanliness 100 --format json` -> `"scaleCleanliness":100,"totalFindings":0 ... "scanned":{"cssFiles":0,...,"totalFiles":0}` exit 0; text output: `✓ No issues found. Your design-system rhythm is clean.` p2 cold wrapper run: `CSS files 0 ... Cleanliness 100%`. src/cli/quickstart.js:201-204; src/audit/render-text.js:78; src/audit/contract.js:364-372.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The 4.0 thesis is a ratchet DS teams put in CI. A gate that goes green on nothing is the one failure a DS lead cannot forgive, and it is reachable from a single wrong path.
findings.proposal: When `scanned.totalFiles === 0` or every stylesheet was skipped, print "Nothing was audited" with the reasons (skipped SCSS, ignores, directory) instead of the clean message; report cleanliness as `null`, not 100; exit 1 whenever any gate flag (`--min-cleanliness`, `--max-findings`, `--fail-on-new-drift`) is present. Quickstart's empty-project hint lists directories that exist and contain stylesheets instead of a hard-coded `./src`. Test: `audit . --min-cleanliness 100` on an empty dir exits 1.
findings.truth_reason: Empty p5: quickstart suggests `npx rhythmguard audit ./src` (quickstart.js:206-207, not 201-204); that exits 1 `Directory not found`; `audit . --min-cleanliness 100 --format json` returns scaleCleanliness 100 with totalFiles 0, exit 0; text prints `No issues found`; `--max-findings 0` exit 0. Cold SCSS run showed 0 CSS files, 5 skipped, 100%. contract.js:364-372 returns 100 when auditedFiles <= 0.
findings.materiality_reason: computeScaleCleanliness returns 100 on zero audited files, so a wrong CI path or an all-SCSS-skipped run passes --min-cleanliness. Trust failure for the ds-team gate, reachable today through dx-05, but the setup-time report shows 0 files and few hit it afterwards. Tiny fix: cleanliness null, exit 1 under gate flags.
findings.relates_to: audit-and-cli gap (missing --token-source is a warning and exit 0; same trust class); none

findings.title: Next-step commands are hard-coded and do not fit the scanned project
findings.claim: init always prints `npx stylelint "src/**/*.css"`: NoFilesFoundError in a Next.js app-router project (app/, components/) and in an SCSS project. Quickstart always prints `npx stylelint "**/*.css"`. The audit footer always prints `npx rhythmguard audit ./src --format markdown`, dropping `--scale auto` and `--token-source`, so the PR report uses a different scale than the run above it (p3: 6 class-string findings on the default scale vs 4 on the @theme ladder; p4: "Scale source fallback" without the token file). The audit just walked the tree and knows the directories, extensions and sources.
findings.evidence: p4: `npx stylelint "src/**/*.css"` -> `NoFilesFoundError: No files matching the pattern "src/**/*.css" were found.` exit 1; p2: `npx stylelint "**/*.css"` -> same. p3: `node cli audit .` -> `TAILWIND CLASS-STRING DRIFT  6 total ... Scale source default` vs `audit . --scale auto` -> 4 class-string findings on the 35-step scale; p4: `audit . --scale auto` without --token-source -> `Scale source             fallback`. src/cli/init.js:375; src/cli/quickstart.js:142; src/audit/render-text.js:80-81.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: Each wrong command costs a newcomer a stack trace and a guess; three in a row in the first five minutes is where the solo dev leaves, and a report built on the wrong scale is what the DS team pastes into the PR.
findings.proposal: Derive the lint glob from `scanned` (directories that held stylesheets, the .css/.scss extensions found) in init and quickstart; the audit footer repeats the exact flags of the current run (`--scale auto --token-source ...`) and the directory that was audited, as quickstart's nextCommands already does. One shared helper renders the next commands for all three; a test asserts the printed glob matches at least one scanned file and the footer command reproduces the run's scale source.
findings.truth_reason: init.js:375 and quickstart.js:142 hard-code the globs: `npx stylelint "src/**/*.css"` gave NoFilesFoundError on the Next.js app-router fixture and `"**/*.css"` on the SCSS fixture. render-text.js:80-81 footer always prints `audit ./src --format markdown` without flags; p3 `audit .` gave 5 class-string findings on the default scale vs 3 with --scale auto; p4 `--scale auto` without --token-source printed `Scale source fallback`. Counts fixture-dependent.
findings.materiality_reason: init hard-codes src/**/*.css (fails on Next.js app-router and SCSS) and the text footer drops --scale auto and --token-source, so the PR markdown runs on a different scale than the report above it. Real friction for solo-dev and ds-team, but each is a one-line derivation from scanned; overlaps dx-02's next-command sharing and dx-05's glob.

findings.title: Audit footer recommends npx stylelint --fix; the agent pack forbids it
findings.claim: Every text report ends with "→ Run \"npx stylelint --fix\" for CSS declaration fixes." The pack written by `init --agents` says "Do not use --fix on spacing findings unless the task says so. Snapping a value can change layout." Running the footer's command on p1 rewrote 13px to 12px, 18px to 16px, 10px to 8px, 7px to 8px and 6px to 4px with no token suggested, while the reviewable path the rhythmguard README positions (`--plan`, `fix --value --to`) is absent from the footer.
findings.evidence: src/audit/render-text.js:80; agents/claude-code/SKILL.md:12 (`Do not use \`--fix\` on spacing findings unless the task says so. Snapping a value can change layout`). p1 `npx stylelint "src/**/*.css" --fix` diff: `-  padding: 13px 18px; +  padding: 12px 16px;`, `-  margin-bottom: 10px; +  margin-bottom: 8px;`, `-  margin: 7px auto; +  margin: 8px auto;`, `-  margin-bottom: 6px; +  margin-bottom: 4px;`. packages/rhythmguard/README.md:32-33 (`audit ./src --plan`, `fix ./src --value 10px --to "var(--space-sm)"`).
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: "Trustworthy autofix" and "no visual regressions" are explicit persona asks. The tool's own footer sends a newcomer to the one command its agent guidance says changes layout, and the first `git diff` after autofix decides whether the tool stays installed.
findings.proposal: Replace the footer with the reviewable path: `npx rhythmguard audit <dir> --plan` to propose one decision per value, then `npx rhythmguard fix <dir> --value 13px --to 12px` (or a token) per decision; mention `--fix` only together with `fixWith: "token"` when tokens were found. Derive the footer line and FOR_AGENTS bullet 3 from one shared string so they cannot disagree, and add the same guidance to quickstart's Next block. Test: no renderer output contains `stylelint --fix` without `fixWith`.
findings.truth_reason: render-text.js:80 prints `Run "npx stylelint --fix"`; SKILL.md:12 and FOR_AGENTS.md:14 say not to use --fix unless the task says so. Running the footer command on p1 rewrote 13px to 12px, 18px to 16px, 10px to 8px, 7px to 8px, 6px to 4px (also 40px to 32px) with no token suggested. The footer never mentions --plan or fix --value --to, which packages/rhythmguard/README.md:32-33 positions as the reviewable path.
findings.materiality_reason: The footer sends every reader to npx stylelint --fix while the shipped agent pack forbids it; the first git diff after autofix moves layout with no token suggested. Hits the solo-dev trustworthy-autofix ask and the ds-team no-regression ask; one string plus a shared constant. #166 --preserve is the deeper fix.
findings.relates_to: audit-and-cli gap (fix rewrites literals inside clamp/min/max); docs/FOR_AGENTS.md:14; none

findings.title: Sass token contract calls used tokens unused and Bootstrap's idiom a conflict
findings.claim: In the SCSS project every `$spacing.*` entry and `$spacer` is listed under "Defined but unused" (usedTokens: []) although main.scss, _mixins.scss and _button.scss use them through `map.get(v.$spacing, 4)`, `map-get(v.$spacing, 2)` and `v.$spacer * 0.75`; and `$spacer: 1rem` next to `$spacing.4: 16px` is reported as a conflict, which is Bootstrap's own pattern. The first TOKEN CONTRACT a Sass design-system team sees is wrong on three of its four lines.
findings.evidence: p2 `node cli audit .` -> `Defined but unused     8 / $spacer / $spacing.0 / $spacing.1 ... / Conflicting tokens     1 / 16px           $spacer, $spacing.4`; JSON `usedTokens: []`, `unusedTokens` holds all 8. `grep -n "v\.\$spac\|map-get\|map.get" src` -> `src/styles/main.scss:7:  padding: map.get(v.$spacing, 4);`, `main.scss:13: gap: map.get(v.$spacing, 2);`, `src/styles/_mixins.scss:5`, `src/components/_button.scss:5:  margin-right: map-get(v.$spacing, 2);`. rules-core map: "Sass @use namespaces, map.get() and interpolation pass unseen"; scale-and-tokens capability reads the same map for the scale, so the names are known.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: A design-system team on Sass judges the tool by whether it understands their token layer; "all your tokens are unused" on the first report ends the evaluation before the drift numbers are read.
findings.proposal: In the token contract's usage pass, count `map.get(<ns.>$map, key)`, `map-get($map, key)`, `<ns.>$var` and `#{...}` interpolation as uses of the map entry or variable, reporting `usedTokens` with file:line; treat two Sass tokens with equal values as aliases rather than conflicts when one is a scalar base and the other a map step. Leave cross-file arithmetic evaluation to #196. Test: the p2 fixture reports $spacing.2, $spacing.4 and $spacer as used and no conflict.
findings.truth_reason: p2 reproduced: usedTokens [], unusedTokens lists $spacer and $spacing.0 to .6, conflictingTokens [{16px: [$spacer, $spacing.4]}], while main.scss, _mixins.scss and _button.scss use map.get(v.$spacing, 4), map.get(v.$spacing, 2), map-get(v.$spacing, 2) and v.$spacer * 0.75. contract.js:102-104 collectTokenUses matches only `var(--…)`, so Sass uses are never counted; collectConflictingTokens (194-208) flags any two tokens sharing a value. Scale inference did read the same map.
findings.materiality_reason: collectTokenUses matches only var(--...), so Sass $spacing, map.get and interpolation never count as uses, and any two equal values are a conflict (Bootstrap's $spacer idiom). Credibility hit for Sass ds-teams, but only visible once dx-05 lands and the drift numbers above it are right. Effort M; #196 adjacent.
findings.relates_to: #196; rules-core quality note on Sass namespaces and map.get(); scale-and-tokens capability "SCSS variables and maps as token sources"

findings.title: Shipped tailwind config rejects Tailwind's own steps and misadvises v4
findings.claim: configs/tailwind extends strict, so use-scale runs with the rhythmic-4 list [0,4,8,12,16,24,32,40,48,64]. Tailwind's spacing ladder also has 6, 10, 14, 20, 28, 36, 44, 56, 80, 96px. Probe: padding: 20px (p-5), margin: 28px, inset: 44px, padding-inline: 14px, padding: 1.25rem are all reported off-scale and --fix rewrites them to 16px, 24px, 40px, 12px, 1rem. On a real v4 app.css (bare --spacing: 0.25rem) prefer-token with ^--spacing- reports every literal, on-scale 16px and 8px included, as 'No known token holds this value; use the nearest token or add one'; v4 has no --spacing-N tokens. docs/TAILWIND.md's example is a v3-style @theme. No Tailwind ladder preset exists.

No known token holds this value'. src/configs/tailwind.js:5-8 (extends strict), src/configs/strict.js:22 (scale), docs/CONFIGS.md:10 ('Tailwind v3 or v4 project'), docs/TAILWIND.md:11-30, listScalePresetNames() has no tailwind entry.

The first thing the documented config does on their stylesheet is flag p-5 and rewrite 20px to 16px; a destructive wrong fix ends adoption on day one, and an agent in a fix loop keeps 'fixing' legitimate Tailwind values.

In prefer-token, when the only spacing token is a bare --spacing, either drop the rule from this config or write --spacing(N) / calc(var(--spacing) * N) for on-ladder literals. Rewrite docs/TAILWIND.md around a real v4 @theme. Add a test that lints Tailwind's default ladder under the config with zero findings.
findings.truth_reason: src/configs/tailwind.js:5-8 extends strict; strict.js:22 is the rhythmic-4 list. Re-ran probe 5: 5a gives 22 warnings and rewrites 20px to 16px, 28px to 24px, 44px to 40px, 14px to 12px, 1.25rem to 1rem; 5b/5d report on-scale 16px/8px as 'No known token'. node_modules/tailwindcss/theme.css holds only --spacing: 0.25rem, zero --spacing-N. No tailwind preset in listScalePresetNames(). Only nit: TAILWIND.md's named @theme tokens are valid v4 syntax, not 'v3-style'.

README and quickstart auto-select this config, so the largest persona hits a destructive wrong fix at step one. Changes findings for existing config users, which the freeze should accept.
findings.relates_to: docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md stop list (presets, Tailwind class-name features) conflicts with a new ladder preset; docs/ESLINT_PLAN.md Phase 0 no-go covers class strings, not this config; landscape map (oxlint-tailwindcss reads @theme); README.md:44-48

findings.title: Physical offsets top/right/bottom/left unchecked and cannot be opted in
findings.claim: top, right, bottom, left belong to no property group, and the properties validator accepts only names matching a group pattern, so properties: ["top"] is an invalid option that switches the rule off for the whole file; only an undocumented RegExp form works. Corpus (58 benchmark repos, 8,705 css/scss files): 2,023 offset declarations with a px/rem literal, 1,112 off the rhythmic-4 scale, in 42 of 58 repos (ghost-admin 225, mattermost 151, zulip 140, discourse 109). That is one hidden finding for every six the rule reports (6,768 spacing literals off-scale). docs/rules/use-scale.md:60 cites top: -1px as a hairline the rule exempts, implying coverage that does not exist.
findings.evidence: probe-1-modern-css.js 1i: top/right/bottom/left 0 warnings while 10 sibling declarations reported; probe-6-hidden-drift.js 6i: 'Invalid value "top" for option "properties"', 0 findings; probe-7-props.js 7a: /^(top|right|bottom|left)$/ works. /tmp/rg-review-css/corpus-stats.json offsetsLiteralOff=1112, reposWithOffsetDrift=42. src/core/css-vocabulary.js:4-16; src/core/options.js:30-37,166-181.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: Absolute-positioning offsets are the second-largest off-scale channel in real CSS; a ratchet that cannot see them under-reports every repo and prints a flattering cleanliness score the ds-team cannot trust.
findings.proposal: 3.x: let properties accept any known-css-properties length property (keep the known-name check, drop the group-pattern filter) and document the RegExp form; add an opt-in offsets group (top|right|bottom|left, kind spacing). 4.0: fold offsets into the default spacing group as a documented new finding class, with the audit histogram keyed per property so a baseline absorbs the jump.
findings.correction: The RegExp form of `properties` is documented (docs/rules/use-scale.md:173, 'regex-like strings (/pattern/flags)'). What is undocumented is that plain names outside the five groups are rejected, so top/right/bottom/left can only be reached through the regex form; docs/AGENT_EVALS.md:39 already records physical offsets as unchecked by design.
findings.truth_reason: Offsets absent from css-vocabulary.js:4-16; options.js:30-37,166-181 accept only group-pattern names; probe 6i reproduces invalid option and zero findings; 7a/7b show RegExp works; use-scale.md:60 cites top: -1px. corpus-stats.json confirms 1112 off-scale offsets in 42 of 58 repos, hairlines excluded. But the RegExp form is documented at docs/rules/use-scale.md:173, and AGENT_EVALS.md:39 records offsets as unchecked by design.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: properties ["top"] turns the rule off for the file (margin silent too); default groups skip top/left/bottom. 1,112 hidden off-scale offsets in 42 of 58 repos means every ratchet score is flattering, and the undocumented RegExp form is the only workaround. All three personas; S effort; compounds with css-12.
findings.relates_to: Council stop list 'new rule options, property groups' (conflict); rules-core map gap; #172 (4.0 defaults)

findings.title: Component-scoped custom properties hide off-scale values from every rule
findings.claim: use-scale and prefer-token skip every --x: declaration, and a var(--x) whose name misses tokenPattern is walked only for its fallback. So .card { --card-gap: 13px; gap: var(--card-gap) }, and even :root { --space-3: 13px } under an explicit scale, produce zero findings; the audit is silent on the same file. Corpus: 2,568 component-scoped custom properties hold a length, 1,050 off the rhythmic-4 scale, in 35 of 58 repos (Mantine 300, fundamental-styles 184, PatternFly 143); 9,228 spacing declarations consume a var() with a non-token name. Inference drops component-scoped tokens by design, so scale: "auto" does not help.
findings.evidence: node /tmp/rg-review-css/probe-6-hidden-drift.js 6a, 6b, 6e: 0 warnings each; audit JSON on /tmp/rg-review-css/fx-audit: no finding for --card-gap: 13px (rawValueCandidates []). corpus-stats.json customPropLengthComponentOff=1050, reposWithLocalCustomDrift=35, spacingVarLocalName=9228. src/rules/use-scale/index.js:320-323; src/core/scale-inference.js:257-272.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: Modern design systems route spacing through component-local custom properties and AI agents write --card-gap: 13px locals freely; a scale gate that cannot see the definition or the consumer is not a gate.
findings.proposal: Check custom-property declarations whose value is a plain length (or a static calc of lengths) when the property is consumed by a spacing, size or radius declaration in the same file, resolving var() chains one level as src/audit/token-chains.js does; report on the definition naming the consumer ('--card-gap: 13px feeds gap'); never autofix a definition (many consumers) unless fixDefinitions: true. Under scale: "auto", root-scoped tokens remain the scale and only component-scoped definitions are checked. Add the same pass to the audit's CSS run.
findings.correction: The Stylelint rules are blind to every custom-property definition and non-token var() consumer. The audit is not fully silent: its token-chains contract (contracts.tokens.chains, src/audit/token-chains.js:27) classifies component-local properties whose name carries a spacing segment (space, spacing, spacer, padding, margin, gap, inset, --size- prefix), so --card-gap: 13px appears as an off-scale chain. Names without such a segment (--card-pad, --btn-x, --sp-3) and calc chains ('computed') stay unseen, and chain outcomes never feed findings.css, totalFindings, scaleCleanliness (100% on the fixture) or the exit gates.
findings.truth_reason: Rules part holds: use-scale/index.js:320-323 and prefer-token/index.js:183-185 skip --x declarations; probes 6a/6b/6e give zero warnings; scale-inference.js:257-272 drops component scope. Audit part is wrong: I ran `rhythmguard audit --format json` on the reviewer's fx-audit fixture and the token-chains pass (#110, docs/AUDIT.md:114-127) reports --card-gap as an off-scale chain entry. Coverage is name-based (--card-pad, --btn-x, --sp-3 produce nothing) and never enters findings, cleanliness or gates.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: --card-gap: 13px with gap: var(--card-gap), and :root --space-3: 13px under an explicit scale, produce nothing. 1,050 off-scale local definitions in 35 repos plus 9,228 non-token var() consumers is the design-system idiom and the way agents write CSS; no competitor checks definitions. Noise risk needs the consumer-scoped design.
findings.relates_to: Council stop list (new rule option); scale-and-tokens map gap on var()/calc chains; src/audit/token-chains.js

findings.title: SCSS blind spots: @include args, namespaced vars, interpolation, map.get
findings.claim: The rules visit declarations only, so @include pad(13px) is never checked; the Sass tokenizer has no namespace form, so t.$space-3 * 2 after @use "./tokens" as t is silent; #{13px}, -#{$s13}, calc(-1 * #{$s13}) and map.get($spacers, 13) are silent. Corpus (6,684 .scss files): 677 @include calls with px/rem arguments, 1,658 ns.$var references in spacing or offset declarations, 2,521 interpolated values, 131 map.get, against 8,330 spacing declarations that use $ at all. Same-file and token-file $vars with * / + - and math.div do work.
findings.evidence: node /tmp/rg-review-css/probe-3-preprocessors.js 3a: only '$spacer * .8', the literal 13px and '$spacer + 13px' reported; map.get, t.$space-3, #{...} silent. probe-6 6d: '@include pad(13px)' silent, '-$s13', '$s13 * -1', '- $s13' evaluated. corpus-stats.json includeWithPx=677, sassNamespacedVar=1658, sassInterp=2521, sassMapGet=131. src/core/token-sources.js:851-1007; src/rules/use-scale/index.js:319.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: Bootstrap, GOV.UK, Carbon and PatternFly are module Sass with mixins and maps; for them the rule sees a fraction of spacing, so the ratchet number is wrong in the flattering direction and the team cannot gate on it.
findings.proposal: (a) Walk @include params with the existing value walker; literal arguments are fixable like declarations. (b) Resolve #{$x} to $x before evaluation and treat #{<literal>} as the literal.
