(c) Resolve ns.$x by reading @use "path" as ns partials with the token-source collector already used for scaleSources (#196), plus map.get/map-get on maps the collector already parses. Report evaluated terms with 'Evaluates to Npx', never rewrite (the #234 guard). Ship (a)+(b) in 3.x, (c) with #196.
findings.truth_reason: Re-ran probes 3a and 6d: @include pad(13px), t.$space-3 * 2, #{13px}, -#{$s13}, calc(-1 * #{$s13}) and map.get silent while $spacer * .8 and $spacer + 13px evaluate. token-sources.js:851 SCSS_TOKEN_PATTERN has no namespace form; only math.div and px-to-rem calls at :941-944. Rules use walkDecls only (use-scale/index.js:319); no walkAtRules anywhere in src/rules. AUDIT.md:90 confirms at-rule positions get property null. Corpus counts match corpus-stats.json; #196 tracks @use partials.
findings.materiality_reason: Map-verified: namespaced, map.get and interpolated terms silent. ds-team only, but half the benchmark corpus is SCSS and Bootstrap/GOV.UK/Carbon are exactly the module-Sass systems the 4.0 thesis targets, so the ratchet under-reports where it matters. Partly tracked under #196; (a)+(b) are cheap.
findings.relates_to: #196; rules-core map gap; council 'small, stable' thesis (conflict on (c))

findings.title: calc() skipped by default and var-multiplier chains never evaluated
findings.claim: shouldLintMathArgument returns false inside calc/clamp/min/max unless enforceInsideMathFunctions, and no shipped config enables it, so calc(100% - 13px), calc(-1 * 13px) and calc(env(safe-area-inset-bottom) + 13px) pass under recommended, strict and tailwind. Static chains like calc(var(--unit) * 3.25), or --sp-3: calc(var(--unit) * 3.25) with --unit: 4px in the same file, are never evaluated. Corpus: 3,462 spacing declarations use calc(); 201 carry a plain literal, 97 of them off-scale in 26 repos; the rest are var()-based arithmetic. Tailwind v4 compiles every spacing utility to calc(var(--spacing) * N).
findings.evidence: probe-1-modern-css.js 1d: 0 warnings on five calc declarations; 1e: 4 warnings with enforceInsideMathFunctions; probe-4-configs.js: '.safe { padding-bottom: calc(env(safe-area-inset-bottom) + 13px) }' unreported under all four configs; probe-6 6e: 0 warnings. corpus-stats.json spacingCalc=3462, spacingCalcWithLiteralOff=97, reposWithCalcDrift=26. src/core/value-nodes.js:185-208; src/rules/use-scale/index.js:364-369.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: An agent told '13px is off-scale' rewrites it as calc(var(--spacing) * 3.25) and the lint passes; the fix loop converges on evasion, not on the scale, which is the opposite of what the ai-assisted persona needs.
findings.proposal: Evaluate calc() statically when every term is a length literal, a unitless number or a same-file custom property that resolves to one (reuse evaluateScssValueList, which already handles * / + - and parentheses), then check the result as an evaluated term ('Evaluates to 13px'), report-only inside the expression. On by default only when the whole expression resolves; percentages or unresolved var() leave it alone. Keep enforceInsideMathFunctions for per-term checks. Teach the audit the same so CI and editor agree.
findings.truth_reason: value-nodes.js:185-208 returns false inside math functions unless enforceInsideMathFunctions; use-scale/index.js:364-369 skips math children. None of src/configs/* sets enforceInsideMathFunctions or checkMathBounds. Probe 1d zero warnings versus 1e four; probe 4 leaves the .safe calc line unreported under all four configs; 6e zero. Audit inherits it (fx-audit calc(100% - 13px) absent from findings; chains mark calc as 'computed'). AGENT_EVALS.md:39 records calc() as unchecked by design. Corpus figures match.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: calc(100% - 13px), calc(-1 * 13px) and calc(var(--spacing) * 3.25) pass by default. Evasion by agents is plausible and the audit/editor split matters, but only 97 off-scale plain-literal calc declarations in 26 repos and Tailwind's calc output is compiled, not authored. Shares one case with css-09 without duplicating it.
findings.relates_to: #232 (motion skips math), #172, rules-core map; council stop list (new default behaviour)

findings.title: Vue, Svelte, Astro style blocks invisible to rules, audit and quickstart
findings.claim: postcss-html is in neither node_modules nor devDependencies and no test exercises it; a .vue file through the default parser throws CssSyntaxError 'Unknown word </style>'. The audit scans .css and .scss only: on a fixture with App.vue (padding: 13px in <style scoped>), Other.svelte and base.css it reports base.css alone, and the quickstart prints a config with no overrides and the command npx stylelint "**/*.css". Corpus: 219 of 362 Vue files have <style> blocks; 19 Vue and 9 Astro files carry spacing literals (57 declarations) that no rule saw. FRAMEWORKS.md documents the postcss-html path as if supported.
findings.evidence: probe-3-preprocessors.js 3i (require.resolve('postcss-html') fails), 3j (CssSyntaxError). Audit and quickstart runs on /tmp/rg-review-css/fx-vue: css findings only 'src/base.css:1 padding 13px'; printed 'npx stylelint "**/*.css"'. package.json devDependencies list (no postcss-html); docs/FRAMEWORKS.md:50-62,102-140; src/audit/args.js:93; src/cli/quickstart.js:267.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: Nuxt, SvelteKit and Astro developers are a large share of 'any frontend developer'; for them the zero-config path measures 0% of component CSS and reports a clean score, so Rhythmguard looks useless on first contact.
findings.proposal: Add postcss-html as a devDependency and optional peer; one test per flavour (Vue, Svelte, Astro) through stylelint.lint with customSyntax, including --fix. Make the audit lint <style> blocks of .vue/.svelte/.astro through postcss-html when installed and count them as 'skipped, install postcss-html' otherwise, as it does for SCSS today. Make quickstart detect those files and print the overrides block and a glob that includes them.
findings.truth_reason: postcss-html absent from node_modules and from package.json dev/peer deps; zero test files mention it; probe 3j reproduces CssSyntaxError. src/audit/scan/files.js:465-476 treats only .css/.scss as stylesheets; .vue/.svelte/.astro are TEMPLATE_EXTENSIONS scanned for class strings. My audit run on fx-vue: cssFiles 1, findings base.css only. Quickstart printed a config with no overrides and 'npx stylelint "**/*.css"' (quickstart.js:142); init.js detect() has no SFC detection. FRAMEWORKS.md:50-140 documents the path. Vue corpus counts are not in corpus-stats.json, so unverified.
findings.materiality_reason: postcss-html absent and untested; audit and quickstart lint .css/.scss only, so a Nuxt, SvelteKit or Astro developer's first command prints a clean score and a glob excluding every component. That is a day-one bounce for a large slice of 'any frontend developer', and the manual FRAMEWORKS.md path is unverified by any test.
findings.relates_to: rules-core map 'Declared syntax boundary' (maturity unknown); #175 (Less decision, separate); docs-and-onboarding map

findings.title: Typography group autofixes letter-spacing and word-spacing onto font-size ladder
findings.claim: propertyGroups: ["typography"] puts font-size, line-height, letter-spacing and word-spacing on one scale. With scales.typography [12,14,16,20,24], letter-spacing: 0.1em is reported 'off-scale (nearest: 12px)' and --fix writes 0.75em; letter-spacing: 2px becomes 12px; word-spacing: 3px becomes 12px. Tracking values never sit on a font-size ladder, so every non-hairline tracking value is a finding with a destructive fix. The font shorthand (145 uses in the corpus) is outside the group. Corpus: 544 letter-spacing declarations among 10,918 typography declarations.
findings.evidence: node /tmp/rg-review-css/probe-2-values.js 2a: fixed output 'letter-spacing: 0.75em; ... letter-spacing: 12px; word-spacing: 12px;'. src/core/css-vocabulary.js:32-37; corpus-stats.json letterSpacing=544, fontShorthand=145.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: A design-system team that turns on the documented typography group gets a --fix that changes tracking by 7x; that is exactly the 'visual regression from a linter' the ds-team persona will not forgive.
findings.proposal: Split tracking out of typography: typography = font-size, line-height (plus the first length of the font shorthand); new kind tracking = letter-spacing, word-spacing, checked only against scales.tracking when given, otherwise skipped, never autofixed. Patch-safe because it only removes findings and fixes; no message text changes.
findings.truth_reason: css-vocabulary.js:32-37 puts letter-spacing and word-spacing in typography; probe 2a reproduces fixed output 'letter-spacing: 0.75em', 'letter-spacing: 12px', 'word-spacing: 12px' against scales.typography [12,14,16,20,24], and the font shorthand is untouched. Corpus letterSpacing 544 and fontShorthand 145 match. Note test/rules/group-scales.test.js:52-57 asserts letter-spacing: 3px is reported on the typography scale, so the split would also change that test.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: letter-spacing 0.1em to 0.75em, 2px to 12px, word-spacing 3px to 12px. A 7x tracking change from --fix is the visual regression the ds-team persona will not forgive, but the typography group is opt-in and fixToScale can be disabled, which bounds exposure. S effort, patch-safe.
findings.relates_to: rules-core map gap; council 'message changes in patches' (none needed)

findings.title: prefer-token map path silently picks the last of two same-valued tokens
findings.claim: tokenMapFromCssCustomProperties, enabled in the shipped tailwind config, builds map[value] = token, so a later token overwrites an earlier one. Probe: --spacing-3: 12px; --spacing-gutter: 12px gives 'Use var(--spacing-gutter)' and --fix writes it into padding: 12px, while the index path on the same stylesheet says 'Use one of the tokens that hold it: var(--space-3) or var(--space-gutter)' with no fix. docs/rules/prefer-token.md promises the rule never guesses.
findings.evidence: node /tmp/rg-review-css/probe-2-values.js 2k (index path: two candidates, no fix) versus 2l (map path: fixed 'padding: var(--spacing-gutter)'). src/core/token-map.js:77-83; src/configs/tailwind.js:13-14.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: Semantic tokens sharing a primitive value are the norm in design systems; writing the wrong meaning into source is a fix the team must revert by hand, inside the config they were told to use.
findings.proposal: Build the custom-property map as value to Set of tokens; when a value has more than one token, leave it out of the map so the index path emits the multi-candidate message with no fix. Add a test with two same-valued tokens under tokenMapFromCssCustomProperties and under the tailwind config.
findings.truth_reason: token-map.js:77-83 writes map[normalizedRaw] = token and map[px] = token, so a later token overwrites; mergeTokenMapFromCssCustomProperties guards only one token with several values (#231), not several tokens with one value. tailwind.js:13-14 enables the map path. Probe 2k (index path) names both tokens with no fix; 2l (map path) writes var(--spacing-gutter) into padding: 12px. prefer-token.md:36-42 promises no guessing. The existing test at prefer-token-config-sources.test.js:80-90 covers the index path only.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: tailwind config writes var(--spacing-gutter) for 12px while the index path on the same tokens correctly refuses to choose. Wrong-meaning fixes inside the shipped config break the 'never guesses' promise for ds-teams with semantic aliases; S fix with an existing correct path to defer to.
findings.relates_to: rules-core map gap; docs/rules/prefer-token.md:42

findings.title: @apply arbitrary values and --spacing()/theme() multipliers pass unseen in CSS
findings.claim: In a Tailwind CSS file, @apply p-[13px] is an at-rule the rules never visit, and --spacing(3.25), theme(spacing.13) and calc(var(--spacing) * 3.25) produce no finding: theme() is skipped as a token function whatever its argument, --spacing(3.25) is walked but its argument is unitless, calc is skipped. Corpus: 215 @apply lines with arbitrary px/rem values. The ESLint plugin and the audit scan class strings in templates but never CSS at-rules.
findings.evidence: node /tmp/rg-review-css/probe-3-preprocessors.js 3h: 2 warnings, both for plain 13px literals; '@apply p-[13px]', '--spacing(3.25)', 'theme(spacing.13)', 'calc(var(--spacing) * 3.25)' unreported. corpus-stats.json applyArbitrary=215. src/core/value-nodes.js:28-53; src/rules/use-scale/index.js:319.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: Tailwind users keep component CSS in @apply and v4 functions; an agent that learns p-[13px] is flagged in JSX moves it into @apply or --spacing(3.25) in CSS and passes, so enforcement has a hole exactly where generated code lands.
findings.proposal: In use-scale, visit @apply params with the existing src/core/tailwind-class-analysis.js and report arbitrary spacing values as the ESLint rule does (fix to the nearest utility); check --spacing(N) and theme(spacing.N) arguments by multiplying N by the inferred bare --spacing base when the scale came from it. The audit gets both through its CSS pass.
findings.truth_reason: Probe 3h and my own probe: @apply p-[13px] unreported (walkDecls only, no walkAtRules in src/rules), --spacing(3.25) unreported while --spacing(13px) is reported, so 'walked but unitless' is exact; theme(spacing.13) and theme(--spacing-13) skipped whole per value-nodes.js:28-53; calc(var(--spacing) * 3.25) skipped. No 'apply' or 'spacing(' handling in src/ or packages/eslint-plugin-rhythmguard; audit templates.js scans string literals, not CSS at-rules. corpus applyArbitrary 215 matches.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: @apply p-[13px], --spacing(3.25), theme(spacing.13) and calc(var(--spacing) * 3.25) all pass in CSS. Real hole for ai-assisted fix loops where generated code lands, and a competitor gap, but 215 @apply arbitrary lines corpus-wide is modest and @apply checking sits next to the ESLint Phase 0 no-go on scale-aware Tailwind work.
findings.relates_to: docs/ESLINT_PLAN.md Phase 0 no-go (class-string work paused; this is the CSS side, conflict in spirit); council stop list 'Tailwind class-name features'

findings.title: env()/attr()/anchor() fallbacks are snapped like spacing decisions
findings.claim: Any non-token, non-math function is descended into, so padding-top: env(safe-area-inset-top, 13px), margin: attr(data-gap px, 13px), inset-block-start: anchor(--tip bottom, 13px) and margin-left: anchor-size(--tip width, 13px) are reported and --fix rewrites the fallback to 12px. A safe-area fallback is a device measurement, not a rhythm decision. Corpus: 35 spacing declarations use env/attr/anchor, so the class is rare today, but anchor positioning is new and growing.
findings.evidence: node /tmp/rg-review-css/probe-1-modern-css.js 1h: 5 warnings, fixed 'env(safe-area-inset-top, 12px)', 'anchor(--tip bottom, 12px)'. src/core/value-nodes.js:105-119; corpus-stats.json spacingEnvAttrAnchor=35.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: Low volume, but each one is a visible wrong fix on mobile safe areas; it feeds the 'noisy linter' impression the solo-dev persona rejects outright.
findings.proposal: Treat the fallback argument of env(), attr(), anchor() and anchor-size() like a var() fallback (#240): report, never fix; and skip env() entirely by default through a new ignoreFunctions option defaulting to ["env"]. Patch-safe since it only removes fixes and findings.
findings.truth_reason: value-nodes.js:105-119 descends into any function that is neither a token function nor skipped math, so env(), attr(), anchor(), anchor-size() fallbacks are checked. Probe 1h reproduces five warnings and fixes env(safe-area-inset-top, 12px) and anchor(--tip bottom, 12px); my probe shows env() without a fallback yields nothing. No ignoreFunctions option exists (zero hits in src/ and docs/). Corpus spacingEnvAttrAnchor 35 matches. Rules-core map lists it as a gap.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: env(safe-area-inset-top, 13px) fixed to 12px. Each case is a visible wrong fix on mobile safe areas, but 35 declarations corpus-wide; keep as a cheap patch-safe noise cut, not a priority.
findings.relates_to: #240; rules-core map gap; council stop list (new option)

findings.title: Length grammar and unit allowlist miss lh, rlh, cap, ic, Q, pt and +13px
findings.claim: LENGTH_RE accepts only -?digits[.digits]unit, so +13px and 1.3e1px pass silently. lh, rlh, cap, ic, Q, pt, cm, mm, in, pc are absent from SUPPORTED_SCALE_UNITS, so units: ["px","lh"] is an invalid option that switches the rule off for the whole file behind one warning, and margin: 1lh can never be checked even with unitStrategy: "exact". Absolute units convert to px exactly, yet toPx returns null for them. Corpus: 5 spacing declarations in these units and 1 with a plus sign, so rare today.
findings.evidence: node /tmp/rg-review-css/probe-2-values.js 2b ('+13px', '1.3e1px' unchanged), 2d (0 warnings on 16 exotic-unit declarations), 2e/2f ('Invalid value "lh"', 'Invalid value "Q"', 0 findings for the on-file 13px). src/core/length.js:3,43-53; src/core/css-vocabulary.js:92-123; corpus-stats.json exoticUnitSpacing=5, plusSignOrExp=1.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: lh-based rhythm is the idiom typographic systems are moving to; rejecting the unit in options and then switching the rule off is a silent CI failure that a ds-team discovers only when drift ships.
findings.proposal: Accept every CSS <length> unit in units; convert absolute units in toPx (1in=96px, 1pt=96/72px, 1pc=16px, 1cm=37.8px, 1mm=3.78px, 1Q=0.945px); keep lh, rlh, cap, ic as exact-strategy units; extend LENGTH_RE with an optional + sign and exponent. Make an invalid units entry a warning that drops the entry rather than the rule.
findings.truth_reason: length.js:3 LENGTH_RE is ^(-?(?:\d+|\d*\.\d+))(?:([a-zA-Z%]+))?$ with no plus sign or exponent; toPx at :43-53 returns null for anything but px/rem/em. css-vocabulary.js:92-123 lacks lh, rlh, cap, ic, Q, pt, cm, mm, in, pc; options.js:75-80 isSupportedUnit rejects them for units and :130 for scale entries. Probe 2b leaves +13px and 1.3e1px unchanged; 2d zero warnings; 2e/2f show the invalid option silences the on-file 13px. Corpus 5 and 1 match.
findings.materiality_reason: units: ["lh"] silently disabling the rule is a quiet CI failure, but only 5 corpus declarations use these units and one uses a plus sign. The 'invalid entry drops the entry, not the rule' part matters more and compounds with css-02's validator change; rate low on volume.
findings.relates_to: rules-core map gap; rules-core quality note on invalid options silencing a file

findings.title: Small coverage misses: grid-gap aliases, translate3d z, font shorthand, non-group lengths
findings.claim: grid-gap, grid-row-gap, grid-column-gap (23 literal uses in the corpus) match no pattern; translate3d(12px, 0, 2px) reports the z offset and fixes it to 0px; the font shorthand (145 uses) sits outside the typography group; border-width, text-indent, box-shadow and stroke-width (254, 29, 1,027 and 56 literal uses) cannot be named in properties because the validator only accepts group-pattern names, so a team cannot extend coverage without a RegExp.
findings.evidence: probe-6-hidden-drift.js 6h: only 'gap' reported of four; probe-1 1l: fixed 'translate3d(12px, 0, 0px)'; probe-7-props.js 7c: 'Invalid value "border-width"', 'Invalid value "text-indent"', 'Invalid value "box-shadow"'. corpus-stats.json legacyGap=23, fontShorthand=145, otherLen. src/core/options.js:30-37.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: Each is small, but together they are the 'why did it miss this and flag that' questions a developer asks in week one, and the answer today is a hidden RegExp form.
findings.proposal: Add grid-(row-|column-)?gap to the spacing group as aliases of gap; skip the third argument of translate3d; let properties accept any known CSS length property (shared with css-02) and document the RegExp form; leave font shorthand and box-shadow out but say so in docs/rules/use-scale.md.
findings.truth_reason: css-vocabulary.js gap patterns are exact (^gap$, ^row-gap$, ^column-gap$) and grid-gap appears nowhere in src/; probe 6h reports only gap. Probe 1l fixes translate3d(12px, 0, 2px) to 0px. Probe 7c: border-width, text-indent, box-shadow rejected by the validator (options.js:30-37 filters known properties by group patterns); stroke-width takes the same path; RegExp entries bypass it (options.js:346-349). Font shorthand outside typography (probe 2a). Corpus legacyGap 23, fontShorthand 145, otherLen match.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: grid-gap aliases silent, gap reported. The valuable half (properties accepting any known length property) is css-02's proposal; the remainder (23 grid-gap uses, translate3d z, docs for font shorthand and box-shadow) is week-one polish that removes 'why did it miss this' questions but would not move a persona alone.
findings.relates_to: css-02; rules-core map gap on shorthand side semantics

findings.title: No fix says whether it moves layout; no preserve-only mode
findings.claim: Every surface snaps silently. The Stylelint message is `Unexpected off-scale value "13px". Use scale values (nearest: 12px or 16px).` with no delta. Far-off values snap to the top step: `margin: 100px; gap: 200px` became `64px`; the ESLint rule fixed `p-[13rem]` (208px) to `p-8` (32px). On-scale `p-[12px]` is never canonicalised, so every ESLint fix moves layout. The agent packs' only guidance is `Do not use --fix` (docs/FOR_AGENTS.md:14). #166 (--preserve), which the strategy map calls the most important item, is unbuilt and #177 waits on it.
findings.evidence: probe-stylelint.js A2 (message), A14 output `.a { margin: 64px; padding: 4px; gap: 64px; width: 13px; }`; /tmp/rg-review-fix/eslint probe.jsx line 8 `--fix-dry-run`: `p-[13rem]` -> `p-8`, `p-[12px]` unchanged; src/rules/use-scale/index.js:54-55; src/core/tailwind-class-analysis.js:221-235; gh issue 166 and 177 open with 0 comments; docs/FOR_AGENTS.md:14.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The solo developer wants a trustworthy autofix; one that can shrink 208px to 32px without a word is not. USWDS and Bootstrap said output-preserving changes are the only ones they accept. The AI-assisted persona needs a fix loop that converges, and the tool's own agent packs say never to autofix.
findings.proposal: Classify every finding as `preserving` (literal to an in-scope token holding exactly that value in the same unit; bracket to utility for an on-scale value) or `moving` (a snap, with its px delta). Suffix messages accordingly (`writes var(--space-3); no visual change` versus `snaps 13px to 12px (-1px)`). Add `fixOnly: "preserving"` to the rules, `--preserve` to `rhythmguard fix` and `audit --plan`, and a `maxSnapPx` guard (default 8px or half the value) above which a finding is report-only. Split report and PR-comment counts into the two classes.
findings.truth_reason: Reproduced A2 (no delta in the message), A14 (100px and 200px -> 64px), ESLint p-[13rem] -> p-8 with p-[12px] never reported. FOR_AGENTS.md:14 says do not use --fix; #166 and #177 open with 0 comments; COUNCIL:77 and ESLINT_PLAN:134 as cited; grep of src for preserve, maxSnap, fixOnly is empty. Nuance: prefer-token's fix is output-preserving by construction and fixToScale/disableFix turn fixes off, but nothing classifies or labels a fix.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: 100px and 200px snap to 64px, p-[13rem] to p-8, no delta in any message. #166 is the plan's 'most important item' and unbuilt. All three personas hit it on the first --fix; oxlint-tailwindcss chose report-only and Tailwind canonicalizers rewrite only exact equivalents, so competitors already avoid this. Compounds with fix-02, 04, 06, 10.
findings.relates_to: #166, #177; docs/ESLINT_PLAN.md item 4 (dropped after the no-go); docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md dates --preserve as the last 3.x feature

findings.title: fixWith token writes var() of tokens that are not in scope
findings.claim: `use-scale` with `fixWith: "token"` wrote `var(--space-local)` into `.other` when `--space-local` is declared only inside `.card`. All three token paths wrote `var(--space-3)` when the token exists only under `@media (min-width: 768px)`. A fallback literal became a token: `margin: var(--space-4, 13px)` -> `var(--space-4, var(--space-3))`. Wherever the token is undefined the property is invalid at computed-value time, so the padding renders as 0. The token index never consults definition scopes (the root filter at scale-inference.js:260 serves inference only) and @media is a transparent scope.
findings.evidence: /tmp/rg-review-fix/probe-scope.js outputs I1 (`.other { padding: var(--space-local); }`), J1/J2/J3 (`.a { padding: var(--space-3); ... }` with the token only under @media); probe-stylelint.js A13; src/core/token-index.js:45-77 and 141-156 (no scope check); src/core/scale-inference.js:257-263 (root filter only in inferScaleFromDefinitions), :328 (media transparent); src/rules/use-scale/index.js:266-277.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: A fix that turns 13px of padding into 0 below 768px is exactly the visual regression the design-system persona runs CI to prevent; one such incident ends the rollout and the tool's reputation with it.
findings.proposal: Carry `scopes` and the enclosing conditional at-rules into the token index. A token qualifies for a fix only when it is root-scoped and declared outside @media/@supports/@container, or when the fixed declaration sits inside the token's own scope block. Never write a token into a var() fallback; write the literal. Add tests for component-scoped, media-only and fallback cases on use-scale, no-offscale-transform and both prefer-token paths.
findings.truth_reason: Reproduced I1 (var(--space-local) written into .other), J1/J2/J3 (a token defined only under @media written by all three paths) and A13 (fallback 13px -> var(--space-3)). token-index.js:45-77 and 141-156 read values, files and token, never scopes; scale-inference.js:257-263 applies the root filter only inside inferScaleFromDefinitions; :328 lists media as transparent. #231 (closed) covers multi-valued tokens only.
findings.materiality_reason: Reproduced on use-scale fixWith token, prefer-token's index path and a var() fallback: component-scoped and @media-only tokens are written where they are undefined, so the padding computes to 0. Reachable from the shipped strict and tailwind configs. Trigger frequency is moderate, but it is exactly the silent visual regression the design-system persona runs CI to prevent; S effort.
findings.relates_to: #231 (multi-valued tokens), #240 (fallback of its own token); no issue for scope

findings.title: rhythmguard fix rewrites what the plan never showed and breaks Sass
findings.claim: The codemod walks every word. `--plan` listed 10px with count 9; `fix --value 10px` made 10 replacements, two inside `clamp()`/`calc()` the plan never showed, and skipped the `var(--x, 10px)` fallback the plan counted. In SCSS it rewrote operands: `margin: 2 * 10px` -> `2 * var(--space-2)` (Dart Sass 1.103.1: `Error: Undefined operation "2 * var(--space-2)"`) and `math.div(10px, 2)` -> `math.div(var(--space-2), 2)`, which compiles to the invalid `padding-left: var(--space-2)/2`. It drops comments inside values (`margin: 10px /* top */ 0` -> `var(--space-2)  0`; SCSS `// top` deleted) and writes px into rem files (`0.625rem -> 12px` under `--decided`).
findings.evidence: /tmp/rg-review-fix/cli: `audit ./src --plan` (10px count 9) versus `fix ./src --value 10px --to 'var(--space-2)' --write` git diff (clamp, calc and math.div rewritten, inset fallback untouched); /tmp/rg-review-fix/sass-check.scss and sass-check2.scss compiled with core-web-components/node_modules/sass 1.103.1; /tmp/rg-review-fix/cli3/src/m.scss after `--write`; src/audit/codemod.js:48-83 (no math skip, no Sass guard, `decl.value = parsed.toString()` at :81); docs/AUDIT.md:190 promise.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: `--plan` then `fix --decided` is the CI story sold to design-system teams. A codemod that breaks the Sass build, edits fluid bounds the plan hid and deletes comments cannot be run by a PR bot, so the ratchet stays a report.
findings.proposal: Reuse the rules' walk in the codemod: skip math functions unless `--check-math-bounds` (matching the audit's default), apply `sassOperandNodes` and skip operands, read and write through `declarationValueSource`/`writeValueEdits` so comments survive, and when `--to` is a length write it in the literal's unit (`0.625rem` -> `0.75rem`). Make the dry run list skipped literals with a reason so plan and fix agree one to one.
findings.truth_reason: Rebuilt the fixture from its init commit: audit JSON counts nine 10px findings including the inset fallback and excluding the clamp/calc bounds; fix made 10 replacements, the reverse. Dart Sass 1.103.1: '2 * var(--space-2)' is 'Undefined operation', math.div(var(--space-2), 2) compiles to var(--space-2)/2. CSS and SCSS comments inside values dropped; --decided wrote 0.625rem -> 12px. codemod.js:48-83 has no math or Sass guard. Note AUDIT.md:190's promise is about files, not literals.
findings.materiality_reason: Reproduced: --plan counted 10px seven times, fix made eight replacements (clamp, calc, 0.625rem) and skipped the counted var() fallback; SCSS became `2 * var(--space-2)` and `math.div(var(--space-2), 2)`; both comment styles were deleted. Breaks AUDIT.md's plan-never-rewrites-unshown promise, so the CI ratchet the 4.0 thesis sells cannot be bot-run. Single persona, small CLI usage today.
findings.relates_to: #233, #234, #256, #331; audit-and-cli map gap (clamp half)

findings.title: em values are snapped through the root font size on both surfaces
findings.claim: `.btn { font-size: 20px; padding: 0.6em 0.7em; }` renders 12px and 14px, so 0.6em is on scale. use-scale converted through baseFontSize 16 (9.6px, 11.2px) and fixed it to `0.5em 0.75em`, which renders 10px and 15px: an on-scale value moved off scale. The ESLint rule keeps the unit but snaps the same way (`p-[0.8em]` -> `p-[0.75em]`). The docs present the em conversion as deliberate, but an em length depends on the element's font-size, which static analysis cannot know.
findings.evidence: probe-stylelint.js A3 output `.btn { font-size: 20px; padding: 0.5em 0.75em; }`; /tmp/rg-review-fix/eslint probe.jsx line 8 `p-[0.8em]` -> `p-[0.75em]`; src/core/length.js:43-53 and 212-225; src/core/tailwind-class-analysis.js:221-230; docs/rules/use-scale.md:70; docs/rules/tailwind-class-use-scale.md:52 and 91.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: em padding is the standard idiom for buttons and form controls (Bootstrap, USWDS, GOV.UK). A fix that silently breaks a correct component is the regression that gets a linter removed from a repo.
findings.proposal: Never autofix em: report only, with the note `em follows the element's font size`. Check em only when `unitStrategy: "exact"` supplies an em scale. Apply the same in the ESLint rule (no `p-[0.75em]` rewrite) and in the audit's findings, and update both Autofix doc sections.
findings.correction: By default both rules snap em through baseFontSize (confirmed), but `units: ['px','rem']` already removes em from checking and fixing on the Stylelint and ESLint rules, and `unitStrategy: 'exact'` with em entries already checks em in its own unit. The ask reduces to changing the default (em report-only unless an exact em scale is supplied) and documenting the existing opt-out, not adding mechanisms.
findings.truth_reason: Reproduced A3 (0.5em 0.75em) and ESLint p-[0.8em] -> p-[0.75em]; length.js:43-53 converts em through baseFontSize and both rule docs present it as deliberate. But units: ['px','rem'] already excludes em from checking and fixing on the Stylelint and ESLint rules (verified on both), and unitStrategy: 'exact' with em steps already checks em in its own unit (0.7em -> 0.75em, 0.6em kept). The gap is the default, not missing options.
findings.materiality_reason: Reproduced: 0.6em 0.7em on a 20px button became 0.5em 0.75em, moving an on-scale value off scale. A real regression on a standard button idiom, but em spacing is a minority of declarations and rare in Tailwind-era code, and the report itself is equally wrong, so report-only is only a partial remedy. S effort, two personas.
findings.relates_to: #247 (closed; kept em arbitrary but still snaps it)

findings.title: stylelint --fix is a silent no-op on Stylelint 16.0 to 16.6
findings.claim: The rules fix through the `fix` callback of `utils.report()`, which Stylelint 16.0.0's report() never reads. With the plugin installed next to each Stylelint, 16.0.0, 16.2.0, 16.4.0 and 16.6.0 return the input unchanged with all warnings still present; 16.7.0, 16.8.0 and 16.8.2 fix. The peer range is `^16.0.0 || ^17.0.0`, the floor suite asserts reports only, and the only mention is CONTRIBUTING.md:122 `known autofix differences`.
findings.evidence: /tmp/rg-review-fix/sl16/probe16b.mjs: `stylelint 16.0.0: warnings after --fix = 3; output = ".a { padding: 13px; margin: 12px; }"; FIX APPLIED = false` (identical for 16.2.0, 16.4.0, 16.6.0); `stylelint 16.7.0 ... FIX APPLIED = true`; raw.githubusercontent.com/stylelint/stylelint/16.0.0/lib/utils/report.mjs reads no `fix`; src/rules/report.js:48-54; test/compat/floor-compat.test.js:16-25; package.json peerDependencies.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: A solo developer on Stylelint 16.3 reads `autofixes to the nearest on-scale value`, runs `--fix`, sees nothing change and concludes the plugin is broken. Stylelint 16 is still 29% of installs.
findings.proposal: Raise the Stylelint peer floor to `^16.7.0` in the release that widens the range to 18 (#168), add a `fix: true` assertion to test/compat/floor-compat.test.js and the CI matrix, and state the fix floor in each rule's Autofix section and the README install step.
findings.truth_reason: Reproduced with my own plugin copies: 16.0.0, 16.2.0, 16.4.0 and 16.6.0 return the input unchanged with 3 warnings; 16.7.0, 16.8.0 and 16.8.2 fix. 16.0.0's report.mjs has no fix handling, 16.7.0's does. report.js:48-54 only sets payload.fix and no rule reads context.fix. ci.yml:75-80 runs only test:compat-floor on 16.0.0, which asserts reports only. CONTRIBUTING.md:122 is the sole autofix mention; peer range ^16.0.0 || ^17.0.0.
findings.materiality_reason: Reproduced with the plugin installed beside each version: 16.6.0 returns the input unchanged with warnings intact (its report() has no fix handling), 16.7.0 fixes. npm per-version data: 16.0 to 16.6 is 3.04% of last week's Stylelint downloads (427k). Small population, but a silent failure at the first --fix, and a peer floor plus one compat test removes it.
findings.relates_to: #168; CONTRIBUTING.md:122; landscape map (Stylelint 18 removed context.fix)

findings.title: Shipped tailwind config and playground autofix a guessed token
findings.claim: With `tokenMapFromCssCustomProperties: true` (the `tailwind` config and the playground) two tokens holding 24px collapse to the last declared: `margin: 24px` -> `var(--space-layout)` with no mention of `--space-gutter`, while the index path names both and writes nothing. A chained `--fix` run (use-scale then prefer-token) launders a safe literal snap into the guess: `padding: 23px` -> `24px` -> `var(--space-layout)`. The browser bundle reproduces it: `gap: 24px` -> `var(--space-layout)`.
findings.evidence: probe-stylelint.js A5a (literal 24px written), A5b (`var(--space-layout)` written, no candidate list), A5c (`Use one of the tokens that hold it: var(--space-gutter) or var(--space-layout)`), A5d (chain); /tmp/rg-review-fix/probe-playground.js output; src/core/token-map.js:75-83 (`map[normalizedRaw] = token` overwrite); src/rules/prefer-token/index.js:202-211 (map consulted first); src/configs/tailwind.js:9-15; docs/index.html:554; docs/rules/prefer-token.md:42 and 56.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: Semantic tokens sharing a primitive value are the norm in token packages. A CI bot that rewrites gutters to layout tokens destroys the token contract the design-system persona adopted the tool to protect, and the public playground demonstrates the guess.
findings.proposal: Build the custom-property map as value to set of tokens; when a value has several, emit the multi-candidate message and no fix, exactly as the index path does. Apply the same to `tokenMapFile` and the Tailwind map. Add a regression test with two same-valued tokens for every map source and for the use-scale plus prefer-token chain.
findings.truth_reason: Reproduced A5b (var(--space-layout) written, no candidates), A5c (index names both, writes nothing), A5d (23px -> 24px -> var(--space-layout)) and the playground bundle (gap: 24px -> var(--space-layout)). token-map.js:77-82 overwrites map[normalizedRaw]; every map source goes through addLengthValueMapping (:112-192, :244). prefer-token/index.js:201-211 consults the map before the index. configs/tailwind.js:13-14, index.html:554 and prefer-token.md:42/56 as cited; the rules-core map lists this as a gap.
findings.materiality_reason: Reproduced: the custom-property map writes var(--space-layout) for 24px while --space-gutter holds the same value; the index path correctly names both and writes nothing. The shipped tailwind config and the public playground take the map path. Semantic tokens sharing a primitive value are standard, so the fix silently breaks the token contract design-system teams adopt the tool to protect. S effort.
findings.relates_to: rules-core map gap (never-guesses promise); no issue filed

findings.title: Two rules still rewrite Sass operands
findings.claim: `no-offscale-transform` and `use-motion-scale` lack the #234 guard: `transform: translateX($n * 13px)` -> `$n * 12px`, `translate: $n * 13px 0` -> `$n * 12px 0`, `transition-duration: $d + 25ms` -> `$d + 0ms`, `animation-delay: 25ms * 2` -> `0ms * 2` (a 50ms delay becomes 0). The visit, bounds and report scaffolding is copied per rule, which is how the guard landed in two rules out of four.
findings.evidence: probe-stylelint.js A6a and A6b outputs; `sassOperandNodes` is imported only in src/rules/use-scale/index.js:28 and src/rules/prefer-token/index.js:24; import lists at src/rules/no-offscale-transform/index.js:20-30 and src/rules/use-motion-scale/index.js:10-15 lack it.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: SCSS is half the quiet-benchmark corpus and the idiom of Bootstrap, GOV.UK and Carbon. A fix that zeroes a delay or halves a translate changes animation and layout math with no warning.
findings.proposal: Extract one `visitLengthValue({ decl, options, check })` helper in src/core (walk, math bounds, Sass operands, fallback context, write-back) used by all four rules, and delete the three copies. Add an SCSS operand fixture to each rule's test file so a missing guard fails.
findings.truth_reason: Reproduced A6a (translateX($n * 13px) -> $n * 12px; translate: $n * 12px 0) and A6b ($d + 25ms -> $d + 0ms; 25ms * 2 -> 0ms * 2). sassOperandNodes is imported only in use-scale/index.js:28 and prefer-token/index.js:24; the import lists of no-offscale-transform (20-30) and use-motion-scale (10-15) lack it. The rules-core map lists this as a gap, not a capability.
findings.materiality_reason: Map-verified operand rewrites in no-offscale-transform (in strict) and use-motion-scale (opt-in, experimental). SCSS arithmetic on transforms and delays is rarer than on spacing, which already carries the guard, so fewer users hit it. The shared visitor is the durable fix and stops the next copy-paste omission; distinct from fix-03, which is the CLI codemod.
findings.relates_to: #234; rules-core quality note on duplicated scaffolding

findings.title: Decisions drive fixes differently on each surface
findings.claim: A snap with `to` is executed only by `rhythmguard fix --decided`. `stylelint --fix` wrote `gap: 16px` for `{ value: "18px", decision: "snap", to: "24px" }` and `padding: 12px` where `to` was `var(--space-3)`. `adopt` with `as` ("the token it should become") has no execution path: src/cli/fix.js:109-125 runs only snaps with `to`, and `decision.as` is read nowhere but the plan echo. `--plan` prints `nearest` yet the user hand-types `to`, and a snap on a negative literal writes `calc(-1 * 12px)`.
findings.evidence: probe-stylelint.js A10 and A10b outputs; /tmp/rg-review-fix/cli2 `fix ./src --decided` dry run (`margin-left: -10px -> calc(-1 * 12px)`, `padding-bottom: 0.625rem -> 12px`); src/rules/use-scale/index.js:135-139 (adopt/allow only); src/cli/fix.js:109-125; grep: `decision.as` used only in src/audit/decisions.js:110; docs/AUDIT.md:175-177.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The rc file is sold as the single source of truth. A team whose editor writes 16px while CI writes 24px stops trusting both, and the adopt path, the common outcome of a plan, never produces the token it names.
findings.proposal: Rules honour `snap.to`: write `to` when the literal matches by px, else the nearest step, also under `fixWith: "token"`. `fix --decided` executes `adopt` with `as` by writing `var(as)` and, with `--define <tokens-file>`, appends the missing definition. `audit --plan --fill-to` prefills `to` with the nearest step in the literal's unit. A length `to` on a negative literal writes `-12px`, not `calc(-1 * 12px)`.
findings.truth_reason: Reproduced A10 (gap: 16px for snap to 24px; padding: 12px) and A10b. fix.js:109-125 executes only snap decisions with a to; `as` is read only by core/decisions.js validation and the --plan echo at audit/decisions.js:110; --plan prints nearest. fix --decided dry run wrote margin-left: -10px -> calc(-1 * 12px) and 0.625rem -> 12px. use-scale:135-139 consults adopt/allow only. AUDIT.md:175-177 documents to as CLI-only, so the split is documented, not hidden.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: rules ignore snap.to (map), adopt.as is read nowhere but the plan echo, and a negative length snap writes calc(-1 * 12px). Only teams deep in the decisions workflow hit it, late in the journey, after fix-03 blocks the same path. Honouring `to` in rules is a bug fix; --define and --fill-to are new features that conflict with the freeze.
findings.relates_to: rules-core map gap (snap `to`); #256; docs/AUDIT.md:175

findings.title: eslint --fix rewrites any string and emits classes Tailwind lacks
findings.claim: The JS/TS path visits every Literal. `--fix-dry-run` rewrote an enum-like `Object.freeze({ Tight: 'p-3' })`, `title="p-3"`, `data-x="p-3"`, `id="m-2"`, `aria-label="use p-3 here"` and the prose `{'release p-3 notes'}`; the map saw a TS `type Size = 'p-3' | ...`. Negative padding and gap are fixed to `-p-3` and `-gap-3` and recommended in messages, but tailwindcss 4.1.18 generates neither (`-mt-3`, `-space-x-3`, `-inset-3` are generated).
findings.evidence: /tmp/rg-review-fix/eslint/probe.jsx `--fix-dry-run` output lines 3, 7, 16, 17; /tmp/rg-review-fix/tw/gen.mjs with the repo's tailwindcss 4.1.18: `-p-3 NOT generated`, `-gap-3 NOT generated`; src/eslint/rules/tailwind-class-use-scale.js:81-83 (Literal and TemplateElement unconditionally); src/core/tailwind-class-analysis.js:25 (`-?` on every utility) and :147-159.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The ESLint path is the only path for generated Tailwind code. An agent loop that runs `eslint --fix` corrupts data attributes, prop contracts and copy, and the dead classes it writes pass the linter while nothing renders.
findings.proposal: Gate JS/TS scanning to class contexts: JSX `className`/`class`, arguments of cn/clsx/classnames/cva/tv/twMerge and object keys inside them, template literals in those positions, plus any string with two or more utility-shaped tokens; expose `classFunctions` for others. Drop the leading `-` from the `p*` and `gap*` alternatives and report `p-[-13px]` as invalid without a fix. Port the Phase 0 class-context rule into tests.
findings.truth_reason: Reproduced --fix-dry-run: line 3 Object.freeze values, line 7 -p-3 and -gap-3, line 16 title, data-x, id and aria-label, line 17 prose, all rewritten. tailwindcss 4.1.18 candidatesToCss: -p-3 and -gap-3 not generated; -mt-3, -inset-3, -space-x-3 generated. The rule registers Literal and TemplateElement unconditionally (:81-83); the regex allows -? on every utility (:25); messages recommend -p-3. No class-context or classFunctions option exists; the eslint-and-tailwind map lists both as gaps.
findings.materiality_reason: Reproduced: --fix rewrote title, data-x, prose text and an Object.freeze value, and wrote -p-3, which Tailwind does not generate. The ESLint path is the only path for agent-generated Tailwind and agent loops run --fix; oxlint-tailwindcss already gates on class contexts across 14 helpers. A correctness fix to the existing rule, so it does not reopen the Phase 0 no-go.
findings.relates_to: eslint-and-tailwind map gaps; conflicts with docs/ESLINT_PLAN.md Phase 0 no-go on rule work, but these are defects, not features

findings.title: ESLint fix UX: no messageIds, no suggestions, whole-literal locations
findings.claim: All 26 diagnostics on the probe carry no `messageId`; `meta.hasSuggestions` is absent; each finding spans the whole literal (`6:6-6:57` for four classes in one string); template-literal chunks are reported but never fixed, so two findings remain after `--fix`; and every fix is a layout-moving snap that `--fix` applies silently. Oxlint runs the same rule object.
findings.evidence: eslint `--format json` on /tmp/rg-review-fix/eslint/probe.jsx: `(no messageId)` on every message, `remaining messages after fix: 2` (lines 10 template chunks); src/eslint/rules/tailwind-class-use-scale.js:25-31 and 35-74; src/eslint/literal-spans.js:300-311.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: Editors and agents act on per-token ranges and suggestions. A squiggle across a 400-character className and a fix that must be hand-applied for template literals make the `fix loop converges` promise false for the agent persona.
findings.proposal: Add `meta.messages` with ids (`offScale`, `negative`), per-token `loc` computed from `segment.start`, `hasSuggestions: true` with one suggestion per nearest utility (lower and upper), autofix only for exact equivalents (ties to fix-01), and a fix for static `TemplateElement` chunks when `cooked === raw`. Keep message text unchanged so the audit's regexes hold.
findings.correction: 27 diagnostics on the probe (not 26), all without messageId; every other statement holds as written.
findings.truth_reason: eslint --format json on the probe gives 27 diagnostics, not 26: all without messageId, none with suggestions; meta has no hasSuggestions or messages (rule file :35-74); four findings share 6:6-6:57; --fix-dry-run leaves exactly 2 messages, the template chunks at 10:6-10:18 and 10:28-10:39 with no fix; on-scale p-[12px] is never reported, so every fix is a snap. Oxlint uses the same rule object per the map.
findings.materiality_reason: Reproduced: no messageId, no hasSuggestions, four findings sharing one 1:26-1:67 span. Degrades editor and agent ergonomics but corrupts nothing, and the plugin has one external user. Overlaps fix-01 on exact-equivalent-only autofix, but per-token loc, suggestions and template-literal fixes are distinct deliverables that make the agent fix loop converge, so not a duplicate.
findings.relates_to: docs/ESLINT_PLAN.md item 4; #278

findings.title: Typography group autofixes tracking onto the font-size ladder
findings.claim: With `propertyGroups: ["typography"]` and `scales.typography [12,14,16,20,24]`, `letter-spacing: 0.1em` became `0.75em`, `word-spacing: 3px` became `12px` and `font-size: 15px` became `14px`. Tracking values are small fractions of an em and never belong on a type-size ladder, yet the group shares one scale and one fix path.
findings.evidence: probe-stylelint.js A8 output `.a { font-size: 14px; letter-spacing: 0.75em; line-height: 1.5; word-spacing: 12px; }`; src/core/css-vocabulary.js:32-37 (group patterns); src/core/options.js:810-816 (one scale per group).
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: A documented, typed option that destroys letter-spacing on the first `--fix` is the surprise that ends adoption in a design-system team that owns typography.
findings.proposal: Remove letter-spacing and word-spacing from the shared typography scale: report-only by default, with an optional `scales.tracking` key (em or px) for teams that have one; keep font-size and line-height on the type ladder. Document it in use-scale.md and ship the message change as a minor bump.
findings.correction: The default typography group does snap tracking onto the font-size ladder, but `propertyScales: { 'letter-spacing': [...], 'word-spacing': [...] }` already supplies a per-property tracking scale inside the group, so the open ask is only the default: make letter-spacing and word-spacing report-only (or drop them from the shared group scale) rather than adding a new scales.tracking key.
findings.truth_reason: Reproduced A8 (letter-spacing 0.1em -> 0.75em, word-spacing 3px -> 12px); css-vocabulary.js:32-37 and options.js:810-816 as cited. But propertyScales (use-scale.md:129/175, tested in group-scales.test.js:52-58) already gives letter-spacing and word-spacing their own scale inside the typography group; verified that 0.1em and 3px are kept with per-property scales. The proposal's scales.tracking key duplicates it; only the default is missing.
findings.materiality_reason: Reproduced: letter-spacing 0.1em became 0.75em, word-spacing 3px became 12px. Destructive, but the typography group is opt-in and absent from every shipped config, so only teams that enable it are exposed; for those (design-system teams owning type) it ends adoption on the first --fix. S effort; the message change needs a minor release.
findings.relates_to: rules-core map gap (typography group); no issue filed

findings.title: env() and attr() fallbacks are snapped like spacing
findings.claim: `padding-top: env(safe-area-inset-top, 13px)` is reported and fixed to `env(safe-area-inset-top, 12px)` because any function that is not a token or math function is descended into. A safe-area fallback is a device measurement that no shipping browser renders, so the finding is noise and the fix changes nothing useful.
findings.evidence: probe-stylelint.js A1 output line `padding-top: env(safe-area-inset-top, 12px);`; src/core/value-nodes.js:105-119 (walkNodes descends into any non-skipped function).
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: Low-value findings that carry fixes are the noise the solo-dev persona leaves a linter over, and each one erodes trust in the fixes that matter.
findings.proposal: Treat env(), attr(), anchor() and anchor-size() like calc(): skipped unless `enforceInsideMathFunctions`, or add them to a default `ignoreFunctions` list shared by the three length rules and the audit; one test per function.
findings.correction: By default env()/attr() fallbacks are reported and snapped (confirmed), but adding env to `tokenFunctions` already suppresses them per config today; the ask is a default skip list for env/attr/anchor (or documenting the tokenFunctions route), not a new mechanism.
findings.truth_reason: Reproduced A1 (env(safe-area-inset-top, 13px) -> 12px); value-nodes.js:105-119 descends into every non-token, non-math function; no ignoreFunctions option exists. However tokenFunctions: ['var','theme','token','env'] already skips env() and its fallback per config (verified: no finding, padding still fixed). tokenFunctions is documented as 'Functions treated as tokenized values', so this is a workaround that suppresses rather than reports.
findings.materiality_reason: Reproduced: env(safe-area-inset-top, 13px) became 12px. Off-scale safe-area fallbacks are rare (fallbacks are usually 0 or on-scale), so this is marginal noise for the solo developer; a low-cost addition to a shared ignoreFunctions list, but it barely moves any persona on its own.
findings.relates_to: rules-core map gap (env); no issue filed

findings.title: Spacing tokens are chosen by a case-sensitive name regex; $type ignored
findings.claim: Token selection is one regex (space|spacing|spacer with a `-` boundary, case-sensitive). A DTCG file whose group carries `$type: dimension` but names tokens by role (gap, inset, stack) or as `dimension.100` yields zero tokens; so do camelCase names (`--spacingXs`, the default output of @tokens-studio/sd-transforms), `--Space-1`, and PascalCase `Space1` (Style Dictionary json/flat). Terrazzo validates all of these as dimensions and Style Dictionary emits them, because neither selects by name. The only remedy is a hand-written `tokenPattern`; the Stylelint rule never shows that hint because warnWhenEmpty is set only by the audit and doctor.
findings.evidence: src/core/token-sources.js:42 (TOKEN_KIND_PATTERNS.spacing), :1052-1065 ($type used only for inheritance and $ref checks); warnWhenEmpty set only in src/audit/report.js:63 and src/cli/doctor.js:373. Probes: `node src/cli/index.js audit . --scale auto --no-config --token-source tokens.json` in /tmp/rg-review-tokens/dtcg-roles -> source=fallback, tokenCount=0, "yielded no spacing tokens; ... set a tokenPattern"; /tmp/rg-review-tokens/tokens-studio/build/tokens.css (`--spacingXs: 4px`) -> tokenCount=0; /tmp/rg-review-tokens/case.css (`--Space-1`) -> 0; `tz check dtcg-roles/tokens.json` -> "No errors"; Stylelint note on the same file: "No spacing tokens were found for scale \"auto\"; using preset \"rhythmic-4\"." with no hint; tokenPattern "^--dimension-" gives [0,4,8,12,16,24,32].
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The ds-team's token package is DTCG typed by $type and named by role, and every Figma or Tokens Studio export is too. Their first run falls back to a guessed scale and tells them to write a regex; in the editor it says nothing. An agent reading "No spacing tokens were found" has no move except inventing a scale.
findings.proposal: In walkJsonTokenGroup, when the requested kind is spacing and the token's own or inherited `$type` is `dimension` (or legacy `type` is spacing, dimension or sizing), accept it whatever its name unless the name matches the typography, radius or motion patterns; keep name selection for CSS, SCSS and flat JSON. Make the name regex case-insensitive and accept a camelCase boundary (`spacing(?=[A-Z0-9])`). Record `selectedBy: "type" | "name"` per source in provenance. Pass warnWhenEmpty from the rule path so the lint note carries the same hint. Add role-named, camelCase and PascalCase files to the vendored conformance tests.
findings.truth_reason: Regex at token-sources.js:42 is case-sensitive with a `-|$` boundary; `$type` reaches only leafTokenValue (1052-1065) for inheritance and the `$ref` number check. Probes: dtcg-roles tokenCount=0 with the tokenPattern hint; `--Space-1` and `--spacingXs` files tokenCount=0; tokenPattern `^--dimension-` gives [0,4,8,12,16,24,32]; `tz check` passes dtcg-roles. warnWhenEmpty is set only at report.js:63 and doctor.js:373; scale-inference.js:177 omits it, and the lint note carried no hint while a missing-file control did.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: role-named $type:dimension and --spacingXs both read as nothing; the editor shows no hint. Every DTCG, Tokens Studio and sd-transforms export hits it on first run; Terrazzo and Style Dictionary select by type. Council line 61 names the silent DTCG fallback as the one gap real usage shows. Prerequisite for tf-08.
findings.relates_to: scale-and-tokens map gap 5 (untracked); tf-08; docs/AUDIT.md:219 documents the name rule as a feature; feature freeze until 4.0 (docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md)

findings.title: A source with tokens but no lengths falls back silently everywhere
findings.claim: Only a zero-token source warns. A source whose tokens are aliases into another file, `var()`/`calc(var())` chains, Tokens Studio unitless strings ("4", "{spacing.sm} * 2") or unitless numbers (`value: 4, type: spacing`; DTCG `$value: 4`) parses, counts its tokens, and the audit falls to the default scale with `rejected: null` and `warnings: []`; text prints only "Scale source fallback"; `doctor` prints "token source found"; the Stylelint note says "No spacing tokens were found", which is false. Terrazzo stops with "Could not resolve alias {space.100}" or "Invalid alias syntax" on the same files.
findings.evidence: src/core/token-sources.js:185-189 (warning only when tokens.length === 0); src/audit/report.js:242-252 (no `rejected` on the token-sources path); src/core/scale-inference.js:659-668 (note text). Probes (/tmp/rg-review-tokens, generator at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-petrilahdelma-SAPDevelop-stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard--claude-worktrees-dreamy-torvalds-c5c0c8/bb2bb07d-7002-475e-acc8-17e1f07d4fe9/scratchpad/review/make-token-fixtures.js): dtcg-crossfile semantic.tokens.json alone -> tokenCount=6, source=fallback, warnings=[]; calc-ladder/tokens.css -> 6 tokens, fallback, silent; tokens-studio/tokens.json -> 6, fallback, silent; sd-source/tokens/space-numbers.json and dtcg-numbers.json -> 5, fallback, silent; `rhythmguard doctor` in tokens-studio -> "token source found (./tokens.json)"; `tz check tokens/semantic.tokens.json` -> "parser:init: Could not resolve alias {space.100}".
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: Every persona is told the tool found nothing when it found their tokens and could not read them. The solo dev concludes the tool does not work, the ds-team ships a CI gate against a guessed scale, and the agent in a fix loop has no signal. Silent wrong-source and silent success are indistinguishable.
findings.proposal: In parseTokenSources, count definitions that carry a px key. When tokens > 0 and px-bearing = 0, push a per-source warning with the count, three example tokens with their raw values and the diagnosed cause: "tokens.json: 6 spacing tokens found, none carries a length ({space.100} is an alias to a file not in this source list; use var() chains or unitless values)". Set `contracts.scale.rejected = { source: "token-sources", values: [], reasons }`, print it in text and Markdown like the scanned-css rejection, make doctor repeat it, and change the lint note to "6 spacing tokens found in tokens.json, none carried a length".
findings.truth_reason: token-sources.js:185 warns only when tokens.length is 0; report.js:242-252 sets no `rejected` on the token-sources path. Probes: semantic-only 6 tokens, calc-ladder 6, tokens-studio 6, space-numbers 5, dtcg-numbers 5: all source=fallback, rejected null, warnings []; text prints only "Scale source fallback", Markdown warnings "none"; doctor on tokens-studio prints just "token source found"; lint note says "No spacing tokens were found". Terrazzo errors loudly on both files (alias message text differed: "space already exists").
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: alias-only and raw Tokens Studio files count 4 tokens, rejected null, warnings empty, text says fallback. Smallest effort, all three personas, first run; the agent's only convergence signal, and it makes tf-03/05/08 failures diagnosable before they are fixed. Lint-note wording belongs in a minor (council: no message changes in patches).
findings.relates_to: #270 (closed; same class for missing file and parse error); 4.0 message freeze (new strings, not changed ones); causes in tf-03, tf-05, tf-08

findings.title: DTCG and Style Dictionary aliases never resolve across files
findings.claim: References resolve against the single parsed file (`context.root`). A semantic file aliasing a primitives file contributes no lengths even when both are configured; when the primitives are named `dimension.*` the pair yields fallback. With a tokenPattern on the primitives the scale is right, but the six semantic tokens are reported as `non-length` in the token contract, so chains and prefer-token cannot name `--spacing-gap-sm` as holding 4px. Style Dictionary and Terrazzo merge all sources before resolving, which is why every multi-file token package is split this way.
findings.evidence: src/core/token-sources.js:1028 (root = the one parsed file), :1173-1182 (lookupJsonReference), :1270-1289. Probes: dtcg-crossfile semantic alone -> fallback, 6 tokens; dtcg-crossfile-dimension both files -> fallback, primitives warned; with /tmp/rg-review-tokens/dtcg-crossfile-dimension/rc.json (tokenPattern on primitives) -> scale [0,4,8,12,16,24,32] but chains summary {"total":6,"non-length":6}; `style-dictionary build` on /tmp/rg-review-tokens/sd-build emits `--gap-sm: 4px` from the same alias; `tz check` -> "Could not resolve alias {space.100}".
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The council's own Q2 item names this as what lets a design-system team delete its glue. Today the team must rename primitives to "space" or run Style Dictionary first and point Rhythmguard at the build, so the ratchet reads a derivative, not the file the designer owns.
findings.proposal: Parse all configured JSON sources into one merged tree (later files override, as Style Dictionary does) before resolving `{a.b}` and `$ref`; keep the defining file per token for provenance; resolve aliases in token chains and prefer-token through the same tree so `--spacing-gap-sm` reports as holding 4px from primitives.tokens.json. An alias that still does not resolve becomes the tf-02 warning naming the target path. Add a two-file case to the DTCG conformance tests.
findings.truth_reason: context.root is the one parsed file (1028) and lookupJsonReference walks only it (1173-1182). Probes: semantic alone falls back with 6 non-length chains; dimension.* primitives plus semantic fall back with primitives warned; with rc.json tokenPattern the scale is [0,4,8,12,16,24,32] but chains {total:6, non-length:6}; prefer-token on 4px names only var(--dimension-100) and fixWith token writes it, never --spacing-gap-sm; Style Dictionary built --gap-sm: 4px from the same alias. #267 closed; COUNCIL:88 lists the Q2 item.
findings.materiality_reason: Council Q2 2027 item verbatim: read Style Dictionary output and DTCG aliases so doctor-school-style teams delete glue; the reference user hand-derives its scale today. Every multi-file token package splits primitives from semantics; SD and Terrazzo merge first. Verified single-file resolution. Conflicts with the plan's timing (Q2 2027), not its content.
findings.relates_to: docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:88 (2027 Q2 item); #267 (closed, same-file only); tf-02

findings.title: Modes, density and brands collapse into one union scale
findings.claim: A token holding several values unions them all into the scale. Terrazzo's plugin-css output, the canonical DTCG-to-CSS path, declares `--space-1` as 4px in `:root` and 2px in `[data-density="compact"]`; Rhythmguard inferred [0,2,4,6,8,12,16,24], so each mode now accepts the other mode's steps. Two density files gave a 10-step ladder, two brand files an 11-step one; `$extensions.mode` values are ignored. Provenance never says values were merged, and `fixWith: "token"` already refuses multi-valued tokens, so these projects get neither a true scale nor token fixes.
findings.evidence: src/core/token-sources.js:1328-1355 (addDefinition unions values per token); src/core/scale-inference.js:257-272 (a token with root scope keeps every value). Probes: /tmp/rg-review-tokens/tz-build `tz build` then `audit . --scale auto --token-source build/tokens.css` -> source=token-sources values=[0,2,4,6,8,12,16,24] tokenCount=10, warnings=[]; dtcg-modes two files -> [0,2,4,6,8,12,16,18,24,32]; multi-brand two files -> [0,4,8,12,16,20,24,28,32,44,48]; dtcg-modes $extensions.mode -> [0,4,8,16,24].
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: Density modes and brands are how the multi-product design-system teams the 4.0 thesis targets ship tokens, and Terrazzo output is their build artifact. A union scale passes values off-scale in every mode, so the CI gate guards nothing, and the first report is wrong without saying so.
findings.proposal: Model a token as values-by-context: the default context is `:root`/`@theme`, the `$value`, or the first file; each other selector, file or `$extensions.mode` key is a named mode. The scale is the default context. Emit `contracts.scale.modes: { compact: [...] }` and a warning "5 tokens hold different values in [data-density=compact]; scale uses :root". Add a `scaleMode` option (`default`, `union`, or a mode name) to the rules and the audit, and let a token-source entry declare `mode`. Keep the union only when no default context exists.
findings.correction: The scale provenance (`contracts.scale.files`, no warning) never says values were merged and the lint says nothing; the audit's token-chains contract does list each such token as `ambiguous` with both terminals (`--space-1`: 4px, 2px), but nothing connects that to the inferred scale, which still unions every mode.
findings.truth_reason: addDefinition unions values per token (1328-1355) and a root-scoped token keeps every value (257-272). Probes reproduce: Terrazzo CSS [0,2,4,6,8,12,16,24] tokenCount=10 warnings []; density pair 10 steps; brands 11; $extensions ignored ([0,4,8,16,24]); lint on the Terrazzo CSS accepts 2px. token-index singleValuedLengths drops multi-valued tokens (#231). Partly off: the report is not wholly silent, since the token-chains contract marks every such token `ambiguous` with both terminals.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified on Terrazzo-style CSS: :root plus [data-density=compact] unions to [0,2,4,6,8,12,16,24], so 6px passes in default mode. But 13px is still caught; the gate weakens, it does not vanish. Council found mode demand rests on one SAP comment; effort L. Default-context selection plus a merged-values warning is the cheaper slice.
findings.relates_to: docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:158 (track B critique of the single scale); #231 (fixes exclude multi-valued tokens); conflicts with the feature freeze until 4.0

findings.title: Ladders built from var() and calc(var(--unit) * N) are unreadable
findings.claim: `--space-2: calc(var(--unit) * 2)` and `--space-md: var(--size-2)` are collected as spacing tokens but carry no length, so the source falls back silently and the lint says no tokens were found. Only literal `--spacing`/`--space` bases are expanded, and `calc(<length> * var(--factor))` needs the unit on the literal. The audit's token-chains code already follows `var()` to terminal lengths but is not used for inference. This is the most common hand-written token idiom after plain lengths, and what an agent writes when asked to put spacing on a 4px unit.
findings.evidence: src/core/scale-inference.js:23-29 (base names hard-coded); src/core/token-sources.js:1357-1384 (CALC_LENGTH_TIMES_VAR requires a unit on the literal); src/audit/token-chains.js:8-27 (var() resolution exists). Probes: /tmp/rg-review-tokens/calc-ladder `audit . --scale auto --token-source tokens.css` -> tokenCount=6 source=fallback warnings=[]; tokens-alias.css -> 4 tokens, fallback; Stylelint with scaleSources ./tokens.css -> "No spacing tokens were found for scale \"auto\"; using preset \"rhythmic-4\"."; quickstart -> "Token files none found".
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The solo dev's own hand-rolled tokens.css is the first thing they point the tool at; a silent fallback there ends the trial. An agent asked for a unit-based scale writes exactly this ladder and then lints its own output against a preset it never chose.
findings.proposal: After collecting a CSS/SCSS source set, resolve `var(--x)`, `var(--x, <length>)`, `calc(var(--x) * N)`, `calc(N * var(--x))` and `calc(var(--x) + <length>)` against definitions in the same source set plus installed packages, depth-capped as token chains are, by lifting the evaluator out of src/audit/token-chains.js into core. The terminal length becomes the token's normalized value and provenance names the base token (`--space-2 = 8px via --unit`). Apply the same resolver to the linted stylesheet route so editor and audit agree.
findings.truth_reason: scale-inference.js:23-29 expands only `--spacing` and a bare `--space`; CALC_LENGTH_TIMES_VAR (1357-1359) needs a unit on the literal, so calc(var(--unit) * 2) and var(--size-2) carry no length. Probes: tokens.css 6 tokens and tokens-alias.css 4 tokens, both fallback with warnings []; lint note "No spacing tokens were found"; quickstart "Token files none found". token-chains resolves the var() aliases on-scale (calc ones come out `computed`) and resolveAuditScale never calls it. #293 closed; map gap 2 untracked.
findings.materiality_reason: Map verified a --space-unit ladder yields null silently; #293 covers only bare --space/--spacing bases. Second most common hand-written idiom, the solo dev's first file and what agents write for a unit-based scale; audit token-chains already evaluates var(), so this lifts existing code. Compounds with tf-02 and tf-12.
findings.relates_to: #293 (bare --space base, closed); scale-and-tokens map gap 2 (untracked); tf-02

findings.title: Tailwind v3 configs and JS/TS themes: audit and quickstart read nothing
findings.claim: `--token-source tailwind.config.js|ts`, Mantine, Chakra, MUI and Panda theme files all fail with "is not valid JSON" because every non-.css/.scss file is parsed as JSON. The Stylelint rule reads `tailwindConfigPath` (verified on .js and .ts), but the audit has no Tailwind branch and the quickstart, which prints "Tailwind v3", still pastes a literal default scale with no `tailwindConfigPath`, so the solo dev's three surfaces disagree from the first run and the ESLint snippet gets the default array.
findings.evidence: src/core/token-sources.js:240-247 (detectSourceFormat: everything else is flat-json); src/audit/report.js:232-311 (no Tailwind branch); src/cli/quickstart.js:97-109, 172-179, 258-266 (detects the major, never writes tailwindConfigPath). Probes: /tmp/rg-review-tokens/tailwind-v3 `--token-source tailwind.config.js` -> "Unable to parse token source tailwind.config.js: Unexpected token 'm', \"module.exp\"... is not valid JSON"; quickstart there -> "Tailwind v3 ... Source fallback", pasted `scale: [0,4,8,12,16,24,32]`; Stylelint with tailwindConfigPath ./tailwind.config.ts -> 13px reported against the config's scale; /tmp/rg-review-tokens/js-themes/*.ts -> same JSON error.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: Tailwind v3 remains a large share of installs and Mantine, Chakra and Panda teams keep the scale in a TS object. For them the audit says fallback and the pasted config can never read their scale, while the rule could have. The first run contradicts itself.
findings.proposal: Two steps. (1) Quickstart writes `tailwindConfigPath` into the pasted config when it detects v3, and the audit honours `audit.tailwindConfigPath` through src/core/token-map.js, so lint, audit and the pasted config agree (S). (2) Add `format: "js"`, auto-selected for .js/.ts/.mjs/.cjs: a static reader that finds `spacing`/`space` object literals, string lengths, `rem(n)`/`px(n)` calls and numeric arrays (MUI) without executing the file, with a warning naming what it looked for when nothing matches; later, make tailwindConfigPath use the same reader so no project code runs at lint time (M).
findings.truth_reason: detectSourceFormat (240-247) sends every non-.css/.scss file to JSON.parse: tailwind.config.js, theme.js, mantine-theme.ts and chakra-theme.ts all fail "is not valid JSON". grep of src/audit finds no tailwindConfigPath and resolveAuditScale (232-311) has no Tailwind branch. quickstart.js:97-109 never writes tailwindConfigPath; the tailwind-v3 run printed "Tailwind v3", "Source fallback" and a literal scale under configs/tailwind. Lint with tailwindConfigPath .js and .ts both loaded the config (13px reported; 20px exempt via the .js gutter). #201 open.
findings.materiality_reason: Quickstart detects v3 then pastes a literal default and no tailwindConfigPath; the audit has no Tailwind branch (verified in code). Solo-dev only, Tailwind v3 declining, and only teams who customised theme.spacing are affected; the Stylelint rule already reads the config. Step 1 is a small first-run fix; step 2 is #201.
findings.relates_to: #201 (open); docs/COMPARISON.md:111-129 (tailwindConfigPath recipe); scale-and-tokens quality note on executing the config; audit-and-cli map gap 11

findings.title: Figma variables exports read as nothing; the hint cannot help
findings.claim: Both committed Figma export shapes, variables2json (`collections[].modes[].variables[]`) and the REST `meta.variables` shape (`resolvedType: FLOAT`, `valuesByMode`, `scopes`), yield zero tokens. Arrays are never walked, so the warning's advice to set a tokenPattern is wrong for variables2json, and for REST it only "works" with token names like `--meta-variables-VariableID:1:2-valuesByMode-1:0`. Terrazzo rejects the file loudly and ships `tz import` from Figma; Rhythmguard neither reads the export nor says what to use instead.
findings.evidence: src/core/token-sources.js:1048-1050 (non-object values skipped), :94-106 (hint text). Probes: /tmp/rg-review-tokens/figma-variables variables2json.json and rest-local-variables.json -> tokenCount=0, "yielded no spacing tokens; ... set a tokenPattern"; rc2.json (tokenPattern ".") on variables2json -> fallback; rc.json (tokenPattern "valuesByMode") on REST -> [0,4,8,12,16] with path-shaped names; `tz check variables2json.json` -> "Expected \"version\" to be \"2025.10\" / Unknown key \"collections\""; `tz --help` -> "import [path] Import from a Figma Design file"; quickstart -> "Token files none found".
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The scale designers set lives in Figma, and the committed export is the only Figma path that needs no Enterprise seat (ROADMAP.md:72). A team that exports variables and points Rhythmguard at the file gets a guessed scale and a misleading hint; nothing the designer decided is read.
findings.proposal: Add a `figma-variables` format auto-detected by shape: variables2json (`collections[].modes[].variables[]` with `type: "number"`) and REST (`meta.variables` with `resolvedType: "FLOAT"`). Read the collection's default mode as the scale and other modes as tf-04 modes; map `scopes` GAP and WIDTH_HEIGHT to the spacing and size kinds; turn `space/1` into `--space-1`. When the shape is unknown, the warning lists the formats read and points at `tz import` or Tokens Studio for a DTCG file. No API calls, no bridge.
findings.truth_reason: walkJsonTokenGroup skips non-object values (1048-1050), so collections[] is never walked. Probes: variables2json and REST exports tokenCount=0 with the tokenPattern hint; rc2 (tokenPattern ".") yields one ratio token (`--version`) and fallback; rc (tokenPattern "valuesByMode") yields 4 path-shaped tokens and [0,4,8,12,16]; quickstart "none found"; `tz check` rejects the file ("Expected version to be 2025.10") and `tz --help` lists `import` from Figma. Note: ROADMAP.md:72's file-based path is a committed DTCG export, not a raw variables file.
findings.materiality_reason: Persona lists Figma variables and the roadmap calls the committed export the path for everyone, but tz import and Tokens Studio already convert it to DTCG, which tf-01/tf-03 make readable. Two unspecified shapes are a moving target; the stop list names a Figma bridge. Fix the wrong tokenPattern hint and point at the DTCG route first.
findings.relates_to: docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:98 stop list ("Figma bridge"; this is a file reader, not an API bridge, but say so); ROADMAP.md:72; #176; tf-04

findings.title: Tokens Studio exports fall back; default sd-transforms output unreadable
findings.claim: The raw Tokens Studio export (sets, legacy `type`, unitless "4", math "{spacing.sm} * 2", `$themes`, `$metadata`) is detected as style-dictionary, yields 6 tokens with no lengths and falls back silently; its W3C-mode export does the same. The documented bridge, @tokens-studio/sd-transforms through Style Dictionary, resolves the math and adds px, but its default name transform emits camelCase (`--spacingXs`), which the name matcher rejects; only an added `name/kebab` transform makes the output readable. No doc tells a Tokens Studio user which of these to do.
findings.evidence: Probes in /tmp/rg-review-tokens/tokens-studio: tokens.json -> format=style-dictionary tokenCount=6 source=fallback warnings=[]; tokens-dtcg.json -> 4 tokens, fallback, silent; `style-dictionary build --config sd.config.mjs` with sd-transforms 2.0.3 (register + preprocessors tokens-studio) -> build/tokens.css `--spacingXs: 4px` -> tokenCount=0 with the tokenPattern hint; with transforms ts/size/px, ts/resolveMath, name/kebab -> `--spacing-xs` and scale [0,4,8,16,24,32]; `tz check tokens-dtcg.json` -> "parser:init: Invalid alias syntax" at the math string.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: Tokens Studio is the most common Figma-to-code bridge (818k sd-transforms downloads a month). A ds-team following its default pipeline gets fallback at both ends, raw export and built CSS, and the only message blames token names. They conclude Rhythmguard does not understand their system.
findings.proposal: Detect the Tokens Studio shape (`$metadata.tokenSetOrder` or `$themes` at the root, `type` on leaves). Read sets in `tokenSetOrder`, or the enabled sets of the first `$themes` entry; treat unitless `spacing`, `sizing` and `dimension` values as px; evaluate `+ - * /` over resolved aliases by reusing the Sass arithmetic evaluator in token-sources.js; apply tf-01's type-based selection so camelCase names pass. Document the sd-transforms path with `name/kebab` as the alternative, in docs/FOR_CONFIG_AUTHORS.md.
findings.truth_reason: tokens.json is detected style-dictionary, 6 tokens, fallback, warnings []; tokens-dtcg.json 4 tokens, fallback, silent. Rebuilt with sd-transforms 2.0.3 and Style Dictionary 5.8.0 (transformGroup tokens-studio, excludeParentKeys, no name/kebab): output is `--spacingXs: 4px` etc. and the audit reports tokenCount=0 with the tokenPattern hint; the kebab build reads as [0,4,8,16,24,32]. `tz check tokens-dtcg.json`: "Invalid alias syntax". No doc mentions Tokens Studio or sd-transforms except a Dev.to draft that claims support.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified raw export: 4 tokens, no lengths, silent fallback. sd-transforms is the common bridge, but tf-01 (camelCase, type selection) and tf-02 (the warning) remove most of the pain; the unique remainder is unitless strings, math and sets, plus a doc page that does not exist today. Not a duplicate; depends on tf-01.
findings.relates_to: tf-01, tf-02; landscape map (Tokens Studio, sd-transforms repo unpushed since 2025-12); scale-and-tokens map gap 6

findings.title: No globs, directories, YAML, JSON5 or JSONC token sources
findings.claim: `--token-source "tokens/*.tokens.json"` reports "Token source not found", a directory fails with EISDIR, and `.yaml`, `.json5` and `.jsonc` fail JSON parsing. Style Dictionary reads globs, JSON5 and JSONC natively; Terrazzo reads YAML and takes a file list in config; Node 22 ships `fs.globSync`. A multi-file token package must be enumerated by hand in three places (scaleSources, the rc file, the CLI), and the quickstart's next-commands line grows one `--token-source` per file.
findings.evidence: src/core/token-sources.js:136-153 (existsSync on the literal path), :164 (JSON.parse), :240-247. Probes in /tmp/rg-review-tokens: globs `tokens/*.tokens.json` -> "Token source not found: tokens/*.tokens.json"; `tokens/` -> "EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory, read"; yaml-json5/tokens.yaml, tokens.json5, tokens.jsonc -> "is not valid JSON" / "Expected property name or '}'"; `style-dictionary build` with source tokens.json5 and tokens.jsonc -> `--space-1: 4px`; `tz check tokens.yaml` -> "No errors"; `node -e "typeof require('node:fs').globSync"` -> function on v22.22.3.
