findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: A design-system team's source of truth is a directory of twenty files, often JSON5 or YAML, already listed as a glob in their Style Dictionary config. Hand-enumerating build outputs in three config files is the friction that ends an evaluation before the first useful report.
findings.proposal: Accept globs through `fs.globSync` (fall back to a small `*`/`**` matcher on Node 20.19) and directories (recursive `*.json`, `*.json5`, `*.jsonc`, `*.yaml`, `*.yml`, `*.tokens.*`, `*.css`, `*.scss`), expanding to one source report per file. Strip comments and trailing commas in-house for `.jsonc` and `.json5`. Read YAML through an optional `yaml` peer dependency and warn "install yaml to read tokens.yaml" when absent. Keep provenance per expanded file.
findings.truth_reason: Code: existsSync on the literal path (136-141), readFileSync on a directory (144-153), JSON.parse (164), extension-only detection (240-247); no glob, yaml, json5 or jsonc handling anywhere in src or docs. Probes: glob "Token source not found", directory "EISDIR", tokens.yaml/json5/jsonc parse errors, an explicit two-file list works; Style Dictionary built the json5 and jsonc sources; `tz check tokens.yaml` passes; fs.globSync is a function on v22.22.3 while engines say >=20.19.0; nextCommands emits one --token-source per file.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: a glob reports not found. Hand-listing files in three places is evaluation friction for ds-team, and globs become the natural input once tf-03 merges files. Effort S with Node 22 globSync; YAML and JSON5 are a minority. Does not bounce by itself; compounds with tf-03 and tf-10.
findings.relates_to: audit-and-cli map gap 12 (quickstart discovery); scale-and-tokens map gap 11; no issue

findings.title: A monorepo with two scales gets one union or the wrong rc
findings.claim: Auditing a workspace root with an 8px marketing package and a 4px app package and no root rc scans both token files and unions them to [0,4,8,12,16,24,32,48], so marketing's off-scale 12px passes. Auditing `packages/marketing` from the root ignores that package's `.rhythmguardrc.json`, because rc discovery, scaleSources and package discovery resolve from `process.cwd()`, not from the nearest package root. Only running inside each package gives the right scale, so a root CI job and a package-local editor lint disagree.
findings.evidence: src/core/scale-inference.js:158, 238, 487, 530 (cwd-keyed lookups). Probes in /tmp/rg-review-tokens/monorepo: `audit . --scale auto` -> source=scanned-css files=[packages/app/tokens.css, packages/marketing/tokens.css] values=[0,4,8,12,16,24,32,48] findings=6; `audit packages/marketing --scale auto` from the root -> scanned-css [0,8,16,24,32,48], rc not applied; inside packages/marketing -> source=token-sources [0,8,16,24,32,48] findings=4; inside packages/app -> [0,4,8,12,16,24] findings=3.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The ds-team persona is defined by apps in a monorepo, and one CI job at the root is how they gate. A union scale or a cwd-dependent result makes the ratchet non-reproducible between CI and the editor, which is the one property a design-system team buys a ratchet for.
findings.proposal: Resolve configuration per file: for each scanned or linted file walk up to the nearest `.rhythmguardrc.json` (or `package.json` with a `rhythmguard` key), resolve its tokenSources, Tailwind config and installed packages from that root, and group the audit by workspace. `contracts.scale` becomes a list of `{ workspace, source, values, files }` (one entry, current shape, for non-monorepos). Add `--workspace <dir>` to limit a run, and print "2 workspaces, 2 scales" in text.
findings.truth_reason: rc, scaleSources and package discovery key on process.cwd() (scale-inference.js:158, 238, 382-383, 487, 530; audit/config.js:37). Probes: root `audit .` gives scanned-css union [0,4,8,12,16,24,32,48] with 6 findings (20px only); `audit packages/marketing` from the root is scanned-css (rc ignored) [0,8,16,24,32,48]; inside marketing token-sources [0,8,16,24,32,48] with 4 findings including 12px; inside app [0,4,8,12,16,24] with 3; marketing's 12px disappears at the root. #174 open; COUNCIL:88 says only on request.
findings.materiality_reason: cwd anchoring verified in code; #174 open. Two-scale monorepos are rare; a single-scale monorepo with a root rc reproduces between CI and editor today, which is the reference user's shape. Council parked per-workspace scales 'only on request' and nobody has asked. Effort L for a small subset.
findings.relates_to: #174 (open); docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:88 ("per-workspace scales only on request"; the persona definition is that request); audit-and-cli map gap 20

findings.title: DTCG 2025.10 $root is dropped and $deprecated kept silently
findings.claim: `isMetadataKey` skips every `$`-prefixed key, so a group's `$root` token is not a token: `space.$root = 4px` is missing from the inferred scale [0,8,12,16,20,24], while a `$deprecated` token (20px) stays in it. Style Dictionary 5.8 emits `--space: 4px` for the same file. The vendored conformance suite has no `$root` or `$deprecated` case, so the gap is invisible to CI.
findings.evidence: src/core/token-sources.js:1300-1306 (isMetadataKey). Probe: /tmp/rg-review-tokens/dtcg-root `audit . --scale auto --token-source tokens.json` -> source=token-sources values=[0,8,12,16,20,24] tokenCount=5; `style-dictionary build --config sd.config.mjs` on the same file -> `--space: 4px` and `--space-5: 20px`; test/unit/dtcg-test-suite.test.js:50-115 (dimension and reference cases only); https://www.designtokens.org/TR/2025.10/format/ ($root group tokens, $deprecated).
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: "Token-file-native" is the 4.0 thesis; a reader that drops a spec-defined token shape produces a scale with a missing base step and tells no one. Teams moving to 2025.10 shapes through zeroheight, Terrazzo or Style Dictionary 5.5+ hit this on the step most often written as $root.
findings.proposal: Treat `$root` as the group's own token (`--space`, subject to the conditional-base rule from #293). Skip tokens with `$deprecated: true` or a string `$deprecated` from the scale and list them in provenance as `deprecated` (prefer-token should still recognise them but not suggest them). Add `$root` and `$deprecated` cases to the vendored suite and to the nested-under-spacing re-read.
findings.truth_reason: isMetadataKey (1300-1306) skips every `$` key. Probe: dtcg-root gives [0,8,12,16,20,24] tokenCount=5, the `$root` 4px dropped and the `$deprecated` 20px kept. DTCG 2025.10 §6.2 defines root tokens "using the reserved name $root"; §5.2.4 allows `$deprecated` true/false/string. Style Dictionary 5.8 drops a trailing `$root` segment (lib/common/transforms.js:53-60) and built `--space: 4px`, `--space-5: 20px`. The vendored suite holds only dimension and reference cases; upstream's `group-root-token` concerns tokens outside any group, not `$root`.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: $root dropped (scale missing 4px), $deprecated 20px kept. Spec-correct but $root files are rare today; when it bites it floods 4px findings loudly rather than silently, so teams notice. Effort S; conformance housekeeping for the token-file-native thesis, not a choice driver.
findings.relates_to: #163 (closed, dimension objects); test/fixtures/dtcg-test-suite/README.md; landscape map open question on $root

findings.title: Quickstart hides source warnings and misses non-JSON token files
findings.claim: Quickstart finds only `tokens.json`, `*.tokens.json` and `*-tokens.json` in five fixed directories, so `tokens.css`, Style Dictionary `build/css/variables.css`, `variables2json.json` and nested token directories are "none found". When a found file yields a warning (role-named DTCG, Tokens Studio, a semantic file), quickstart prints "Source fallback / No spacing tokens found" and pastes a literal default scale, dropping the audit's own `!` line that names the cause and the tokenPattern remedy.
findings.evidence: src/cli/quickstart.js:29-30 (TOKEN_FILE_PATTERN, TOKEN_DIRS), :97-109 (literal scale on fallback), :212-221 (Source line, no warnings). Probes: `node src/cli/index.js quickstart` in /tmp/rg-review-tokens/dtcg-roles and tokens-studio -> "Token files tokens.json ... Source fallback ... Note No spacing tokens found", pasted `scale: [0,4,8,12,16,24,32]`; audit text in sd-build prints "! Token source tokens/semantic.tokens.json (dtcg) yielded no spacing tokens" while quickstart on the same directory prints no `!` line; quickstart in calc-ladder and figma-variables -> "Token files none found".
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The README's first command is `npx rhythmguard`; it is the moment the tool must prove it can read the user's scale. Today it finds the file, fails to read it, hides why, and pastes a config that locks in the guess. An agent running quickstart to bootstrap a project inherits that guess.
findings.proposal: Print every `contracts.tokens.sources[].warnings` line (and tf-02's new warning) under Source. Extend discovery to `tokens.css`, `*.tokens.{json,json5,jsonc,yaml}`, and `variables.css`/`tokens.css` under `build/**`, `dist/**` and `packages/*/tokens*/**` to depth 4, excluding node_modules. When a found file yields nothing, paste `scaleSources` pointing at it with the warning as a comment line above, instead of a literal default, so the pasted config points at the truth and fails loudly until the source reads.
findings.correction: Quickstart never prints `contracts.tokens.sources[].warnings`, so for a zero-token source (role-named DTCG, a semantic file whose names are not spacing names) it drops the audit's `!` line and its tokenPattern remedy; a Tokens Studio raw export yields six tokens and no audit warning at all (tf-02), so there quickstart adds its own misleading "No spacing tokens found" note rather than dropping one.
findings.truth_reason: TOKEN_FILE_PATTERN `/(^|[.-])tokens?\.json$/` over cwd plus four fixed dirs (29-30); a literal scale is pasted on fallback (97-109); the Source block (212-221) prints no source warnings. Probes: calc-ladder and figma-variables "none found"; sd-build lists only tokens/*.tokens.json, not build/css/variables.css; dtcg-roles and tokens-studio print "Source fallback" plus a literal scale with zero "yielded" lines, while the audit text prints the `!` line for dtcg-roles and the sd-build semantic file. The Tokens Studio example is wrong: that export yields no audit warning (tf-02).
findings.materiality_reason: Verified in code: JSON-only discovery in five dirs, source warnings never printed, literal default pasted on fallback. It is the README's first command, but CSS token files in the tree are still read via scanned-css, so the discovery gap is mostly cosmetic. Standalone it surfaces an existing hint; the lift comes paired with tf-02.
findings.relates_to: audit-and-cli map gap 12; src/cli/quickstart.js:95 rationale (#246, literal scale on fallback); tf-02

findings.title: Default scale fights Tailwind's own theme: wrong advice, shrinking fixes
findings.claim: With no `scale` option the rule checks against [0,4,8,12,16,24,32], which is neither Tailwind's default theme nor the Stylelint default. On a stock Tailwind project `p-[20px]` is reported with 'Use p-4 (16px) or p-6 (24px)' although `p-5` is the standard 20px class; `p-[6px]` and `p-[10px]` get the same treatment while `p-1.5` and `p-2.5` exist. Anything above 32px snaps to the top step: `p-[40px]`, `p-[48px]` and `p-[64px]` all become `p-8`, and `p-[2px]` becomes `p-0` because ties round down. @shadcn/lint and oxlint-tailwindcss both answer 'p-5, same value'.
findings.evidence: cd /tmp/rg-review-classes && eslint --format json probe-steps.jsx (default options): 9:20 p-[20px] FIX='p-4' 'Use "p-4" (16px) or "p-6" (24px)'; 12:20 p-[40px] FIX='p-8'; 13:20 p-[48px] FIX='p-8'; 14:20 p-[64px] FIX='p-8' 'Use "p-8" (32px)'; 18:20 p-[2px] FIX='p-0'. Same file under eslint.config.shadcn.mjs: 'Use "p-5" instead (same value, on the scale)', 'p-16', 'p-0.5'; under oxlint-tailwindcss: 'Closest in your theme: p-5 (20px)'. src/core/tailwind-class-analysis.js:18 (DEFAULT_SCALE); src/core/length.js:189-190 (ties to lower).
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: A solo dev who installs the recommended config on a stock Tailwind project sees warnings on standard spacing and a `--fix` that halves a 64px padding in the first hour. The impression is 'this tool does not know Tailwind', and they switch to a canonicalizer that stays quiet.
findings.proposal: When `scale` is not set, default to Tailwind's default spacing ladder (the 34 steps quickstart already derives from `--spacing`, printed by `npx rhythmguard`) instead of [0..32]; keep a hand-written `scale` as the opt-in restriction. Never fix past the ends of the scale: when the value is above the top step or below the first non-zero step, report 'no step on your scale above 32px; add one or use a token' with no fix. Say in the message which scale was used ('against Tailwind's default scale; set `scale` to restrict it') so the first finding explains itself.
findings.truth_reason: DEFAULT_SCALE [0,4,8,12,16,24,32] at tailwind-class-analysis.js:18; Stylelint default is rhythmic-4 [0..64] (presets/scales.js:27). Reproduced: p-[20px] FIX p-4 'Use p-4 (16px) or p-6 (24px)'; p-[40px]/[48px]/[64px] FIX p-8; p-[2px] FIX p-0 (length.js:189-190 ties to lower). shadcn: p-5, p-16, p-0.5; oxlint-tailwindcss: 'Closest in your theme: p-5 (20px)'. Control run with the 34-step ladder leaves only p-[13px]. #246 closed; code comment says 'waits for a major'.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: p-[20px] gets p-4/p-6 while p-5 exists; 40, 48 and 64px all fix to p-8; 2px to p-0. Recommended config and audit default hit every stock Tailwind user in hour one, and Phase 0 found 19 of 20 apps on the default ladder. Conflicts with the #246 deferral and the freeze.
findings.relates_to: #246 (closed: unifying the defaults 'waits for a major'), #172 (4.0: one default scale). Changes default reports, so it conflicts with the freeze unless treated as a bug fix.

findings.title: Bare v4 step classes p-3.25, gap-4.5, p-13 are never checked
findings.claim: The matcher requires brackets, so `p-3.25` (13px), `gap-4.5` (18px), `p-13` (52px) and `px-0.75` (3px) pass under any scale. Tailwind 4.3.4's canonicalize rewrites `p-[0.8125rem]` to `p-3.25` and `gap-[1.125rem]` to `gap-4.5`; better-tailwindcss and IntelliSense do the same, and @shadcn/lint suggests `p-3.25` for `p-[13px]`. The off-scale value survives in a form no tool, including this one, questions. Phase 0 found 87 of 700 off-scale findings already in step form, and the package README itself calls this 'the gap every tool shares, this one included'.
findings.evidence: eslint probe-steps.jsx lines 3-6 (p-3.25, gap-4.5, p-13, px-0.75): no message with the default or an explicit scale. node benchmarks/tailwind-compare/node_modules/@tailwindcss/cli/dist/index.mjs canonicalize --format json --css app.css p-[0.8125rem] gap-[1.125rem]: output p-3.25, gap-4.5 (changed: true). src/core/tailwind-class-analysis.js:25 (regex ends in a bracketed value); benchmarks/tailwind-compare/RESULTS.md:17-19 (five tools, no finding); packages/eslint-plugin-rhythmguard/README.md:35-37; benchmarks/tailwind-v4/RESULTS.md ('613 bracketed, 87 v4 steps').
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The one check nobody else makes is the reason to pick Rhythmguard over a free canonicalizer. A design-system team that declares a 4px scale finds that `p-3.25` passes CI and concludes the ratchet has a hole the size of the whole v4 syntax; an agent that learns `p-[13px]` fails simply writes `p-3.25`.
findings.proposal: Parse `^(utility)-(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)$` for the spacing utilities already matched (plus ps/pe/ms/me, cs-07), convert with `spacingUnit`, and check against the scale. Gate it on a declared scale (`scale` option, rc file, or `@theme` `--spacing-*` tokens) so it is off on the Tailwind default ladder and `p-1.5` never fires. Message: '"p-3.25" is 13px, not on your scale. Use "p-3" (12px) or "p-4" (16px)'; offer the two steps as suggestions, no autofix. Option `checkSteps`, default true in 4.0. Add the four rows to the comparison script so the README table stops saying 'no finding' in the Rhythmguard column.
findings.truth_reason: Regex at tailwind-class-analysis.js:25 ends in -\[...\]; p-3.25, gap-4.5, p-13, px-0.75 produce no message under default or ladder scale. Tailwind CLI 4.3.4 canonicalize: p-[0.8125rem] -> p-3.25, gap-[1.125rem] -> gap-4.5, changed:true. shadcn suggests p-3.25 for p-[13px]. RESULTS.md:17-19 five blanks; package README:35-37 'gap every tool shares'; tailwind-v4/RESULTS.md:38 '613 bracketed, 87 v4 steps'; ESLINT_PLAN.md:134 item 3 not built.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified no finding for p-3.25, gap-4.5, p-13. The one check no competitor ships, and the reason a ds-team with a declared scale picks Rhythmguard over a free canonicalizer; agents launder p-[13px] into p-3.25. Needs cs-03 or cs-05 for the declared scale. Plan item 3, stopped by the no-go.
findings.relates_to: docs/ESLINT_PLAN.md item 3 (not built after the 2026-11-01 no-go, line 134), #172. Conflicts with the plan of record: Phase 0 measured drift prevalence in apps with no declared scale, not the value of this check for teams that have one.

findings.title: ESLint rule cannot read @theme, --spacing or token files
findings.claim: The option schema accepts only `scale`, `units`, `baseFontSize`, `allowHairlines`, `allowNegative`, `spacingUnit` and `note`; `scale: "auto"` or `scaleSources` fail config validation, so the readers the Stylelint side has (core/token-sources.js: `@theme` `--spacing-*`, DTCG, Style Dictionary) are unreachable from ESLint. `spacingUnit` defaults to 4px whatever `--spacing` says: under `@theme { --spacing: 0.125rem }` Tailwind compiles `p-3` to 6px, so the fix for 13px renders at half size. Named tokens are invisible: for `py-[15px]` beside `--spacing-md: 16px`, oxlint-tailwindcss says 'py-3.5 (14px) or py-md (16px)' and Tailwind canonicalizes `mt-[16px]` to `mt-md`; Rhythmguard says 'py-4'.
findings.evidence: eslint --config eslint.config.auto.mjs probe-steps.jsx: 'Unexpected property "scaleSources". Expected properties: "allowHairlines", "allowNegative", "baseFontSize", "note", "scale", "spacingUnit", "units"'. tailwindcss 4.3.4 -i theme-2px.css: '.p-3 { padding: calc(var(--spacing) * 3); }' with '--spacing: 0.125rem'. oxlint -c .oxlintrc.tw.json probe-forms.jsx:38: 'py-[15px] ... Closest in your theme: py-3.5 (14px) or py-md (16px). If none fits, add a token to app.css.'; canonicalize mt-[16px] -> mt-md. src/core/tailwind-class-analysis.js:20-23,39-43; packages/eslint-plugin-rhythmguard/README.md:93 ('The rule does not read your Tailwind theme').
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: 'One scale, two linters' is the design-system pitch, and the ESLint side needs a hand-copied array that goes stale (doctor-school reads allowed-tokens.json by hand). A Tailwind-first team puts the two messages side by side: oxlint-tailwindcss names their tokens and their theme file, Rhythmguard names a class that may be the wrong size.
findings.proposal: Add `entryPoint` (the Tailwind CSS entry), `scaleSources`, `preset` and `scale: "auto"` to the rule schema with the same meaning as `use-scale`, wired to core/token-sources with an mtime-keyed cache per process. Derive `spacingUnit` from `--spacing` and `baseFontSize` from the entry when present. When a `--spacing-*` token equals a nearest step, name it in the message and prefer it in the fix (`py-md`), as Tailwind's canonicalize does. End every message with 'If none fits, add a token to <entry>'. Done when doctor-school's config can drop its JSON read and report identical findings.
findings.truth_reason: Schema (rule lines 43-73) lists only seven options; scaleSources and entryPoint both fail validation ('Unexpected property'). spacingUnit defaults to baseFontSize*0.25 (lines 39-43). Tailwind 4.3.4 compile of --spacing 0.125rem: '.p-3 { padding: calc(var(--spacing) * 3) }' = 6px. oxlint-tailwindcss on py-[15px]: 'py-3.5 (14px) or py-md (16px). If none fits, add a token to app.css.' canonicalize mt-[16px] -> mt-md. README:93 states the rule does not read the theme. No token-sources import in src/eslint.
findings.materiality_reason: Schema confirmed: a hand-written scale only, and spacingUnit ignores --spacing so fixes can render at the wrong size. Breaks the 'one scale, two linters' pitch for ds-team and loses the token-naming comparison to oxlint-tailwindcss. Overlaps cs-05's shared resolver; keep both. Plan items 1 and 2, stopped by the no-go.
findings.relates_to: docs/ESLINT_PLAN.md items 1-2 (not built), #201 (JS/TS theme objects), #246. Conflicts with the freeze.

findings.title: Every string is a class string: --fix rewrites types, enums, aria-labels
findings.claim: The JS/TS path visits every Literal and TemplateElement with no notion of a class context, so `--fix` rewrote `type Size = 'p-[13px]'`, `enum Spacing { Tight = 'p-[13px]' }`, `interface Props { pad: 'p-[13px]' }`, `aria-label="p-[13px]"`, `title=`, `id=`, `data-size=`, a `<Box padding="p-[13px]">` prop and the prose string `'Error in p-[13px] string'`. Changing a type literal or enum member breaks the prop contract against callers the linter never sees. On the same helper file @shadcn/lint reports 12 findings, Rhythmguard 24; on the TS file shadcn reports none at type level, Rhythmguard four. The Vue and Svelte paths already restrict themselves to `class`.
findings.evidence: eslint --fix-dry-run --format json probe-types.tsx, output: "type Size = 'p-3' | 'p-[12px]'; enum Spacing { Tight = 'p-3' }; interface Props { pad: 'p-3' }". probe-helpers.jsx line 24 after fix: data-size="p-3" title="p-3" id="m-3" aria-label="p-3"; line 23: 'Error in p-3 string'. eslint --config eslint.config.shadcn.mjs: probe-helpers.jsx 12 messages vs 24; probe-types.tsx lines 1-4: 0 vs 4. src/eslint/rules/tailwind-class-use-scale.js:81-83 (Literal/TemplateElement unconditionally); src/eslint/literal-spans.js:274-292 (Vue/Svelte class gate); scripts/bench/tailwind-v4/measure.mjs:203-208 (Phase 0 needed a class-context rule to drop SVG path data).
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: A dev runs `eslint --fix` once, sees a TypeScript error or a changed accessible name in the diff, and stops trusting every fix the plugin offers. An agent in a fix loop gets findings on strings it cannot change (API prop values, enum members) and never converges.
findings.proposal: Gate the JS/TS path on class contexts, as Vue/Svelte already do: JSX attributes named `class`, `className` or `*ClassName`; arguments, array elements and object keys inside calls to `cn`, `clsx`, `classnames`, `cx`, `cva`, `tv`, `twMerge`, `twJoin` and a `tw` tagged template; `class`/`className` keys of object literals; plus any literal with two or more whitespace-separated tokens where one is a known utility. Always skip type positions (TSLiteralType, enum members). Options `classFunctions: string[]` to extend and `classContexts: "any"` to restore today's behaviour. Document the gate in the rule docs where 'every string literal' is currently sold as a feature.
findings.truth_reason: Rule lines 81-83 register Literal/TemplateElement with no context check. --fix-dry-run output matches verbatim: type Size = 'p-3', enum Tight = 'p-3', interface pad: 'p-3', data-size/title/id/aria-label rewritten, Box padding='p-3', 'Error in p-3 string'. shadcn: helpers 12 vs 24; types file lines 1-4 zero vs four. Vue/Svelte gate at literal-spans.js:274-292; measure.mjs:199-210 class-context amendment; rule doc line 43 and README:130 advertise 'every string literal'.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: --fix rewrote title, aria-label, id, data-size and a prose string, and the map's probe shows TS type literals. Severe when hit (broken prop contracts, changed accessible names), but Phase 0 found 4 of 704 hits outside class contexts, so few users meet it. cs-06 suggestions would limit the damage.
findings.relates_to: none tracked; #225 (escape safety) and #244 (Vue/Svelte class gate) are the same instinct applied elsewhere. Reduces findings, so it is arguably a bug fix inside the freeze.

findings.title: Quickstart, audit and ESLint judge the same class by three scales
findings.claim: On one Tailwind v4 directory with an `@theme`, quickstart infers a 34-step ladder from `--spacing` and pastes it into its ESLint snippet (75 class-string findings), while `rhythmguard audit .` uses the default [0..32] (85 findings, source 'default') and ESLint uses whatever array was pasted. `.rhythmguardrc.json` carries `audit.scale` and `audit.tokenSources` for the audit, but the ESLint rule cannot read the rc, and `doctor` never compares the ESLint `scale` with the audit's. The agent skill tells agents to run the audit before finishing, while CI runs ESLint.
findings.evidence: node src/cli/index.js (quickstart) in /tmp/rg-review-classes: 'Scale 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 20, 24, ... 384', 'Source scanned-css (app.css)', 'Off-scale 1 in CSS, 75 in class strings', ESLint snippet carrying that 34-value scale. node src/cli/index.js audit . --format json: contracts.scale.source 'default', values [0,4,8,12,16,24,32], findings.tailwind.length 85. src/audit/config.js:97-123 (audit.scale, audit.tokenSources); ESLint schema src/eslint/rules/tailwind-class-use-scale.js:43-73; node src/cli/index.js doctor in the same dir prints nothing about the ESLint scale; agents/claude-code/SKILL.md:10.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: An agent fixes to the audit's verdict, CI's ESLint disagrees on `p-[20px]`, and the human watches two Rhythmguard surfaces contradict each other and removes the one in CI. 'Fix loops that converge' needs one scale, not three.
findings.proposal: One scale resolver for all three surfaces: when `scale` is absent the ESLint rule reads `.rhythmguardrc.json` (`audit.scale`, `audit.tokenSources`, then `@theme` once cs-03 lands) through the resolver the audit uses, and the audit's class-string pass defaults to that resolver instead of [0..32] (#287 fixed the printed commands, not the default). Quickstart writes the rc (`scale`, `tokenSources`) and its ESLint snippet then omits `scale`. `doctor` fails when an explicit ESLint `scale` differs from the resolved one and prints both. The audit JSON and `eslint --format json` both state the scale and its source so an agent can see they agree.
findings.truth_reason: Quickstart in the probe dir: 34-step ladder, source scanned-css, '75 in class strings', ESLint snippet with that array (quickstart.js:111-127). audit . JSON: contracts.scale.source 'default', [0..32], 85 tailwind findings; report.js:232-240 infers only with --scale auto. config.js:96-124 reads audit.scale/tokenSources; no rc read in src/eslint; doctor output never mentions the ESLint scale. SKILL.md:10 runs audit without --scale auto. #287 changed printed commands only.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified on a Tailwind v4 fixture: quickstart infers 34 steps and pastes them into the ESLint snippet, plain `audit .` uses [0..32] (6 versus 2 findings), and the agent skill runs `audit .` without --scale auto, so agents and CI disagree by design; doctor never compares. Central to converging fix loops. Overlaps cs-03.
findings.relates_to: #287 (closed, quickstart next commands), #246 (closed), #172 (one default scale), docs/FOR_AGENTS.md:12-16. Conflicts with the freeze where it changes the audit default.

findings.title: Autofix moves layout; no suggestion path exists
findings.claim: `fixable: 'code'` with no `hasSuggestions`: every off-scale finding carries an autofix that changes rendered spacing (13px to 12px, 15px to 16px, 64px to 32px, 2px to 0 under the default scale), and no finding offers the two nearest steps as editor suggestions. @shadcn/lint ships 0 fixes and 34 suggestions on the same file; oxlint-tailwindcss refuses to autofix on purpose. The project's own agent skill says 'Do not use --fix on spacing findings... Snapping a value can change layout', which concedes the fix is not trustworthy, and plan item 4 ('fixes that never move layout') was dropped with the no-go.
findings.evidence: eslint --format json probe-forms.jsx line 38: py-[15px] FIX='py-4'; probe-steps.jsx 14:20 p-[64px] FIX='p-8', 18:20 p-[2px] FIX='p-0'; no message in any probe has a `suggestions` array. eslint --config eslint.config.shadcn.mjs probe-forms.jsx: 'fixable 0, with suggestions 34'. src/eslint/rules/tailwind-class-use-scale.js:28-30,42 (fix on every non-negative finding, no hasSuggestions); agents/claude-code/SKILL.md:12; docs/ESLINT_PLAN.md:86,134; src/core/length.js:189-190.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: 'Trustworthy autofix' and 'no visual regressions' are both in the goal. A fix that silently changes padding on a legacy codebase is the fastest route to a reverted PR and an uninstalled plugin, and the skill telling agents never to use it means the fix exists for nobody.
findings.proposal: Report exact equivalents (`p-[12px]` on a 12px step, `p-[0.75rem]`) as a separate fixable message ('same value, use p-3') and give off-scale values two ESLint suggestions ('Use p-3 (12px)', 'Use p-4 (16px)') with no autofix by default; `fixOffScale: "nearest"` restores today's behaviour, aligned with `--preserve` (#166). Under Oxlint the suggestions surface through the LSP. In the audit keep `fixedToken` but rename it `snapTo` and add `preservesLayout: false`, so agents reading JSON know which rewrites are safe.
findings.truth_reason: Rule meta has fixable:'code', no hasSuggestions, no messages (lines 35-74); every non-negative finding gets a fix (28-30). Probe: py-[15px] FIX py-4, p-[64px] FIX p-8, p-[2px] FIX p-0, no suggestions array anywhere. shadcn on probe-forms.jsx: fixable 0, 34 with suggestions. oxlint-tailwindcss --fix leaves probe-steps.jsx byte-identical. SKILL.md:12 forbids --fix; ESLINT_PLAN.md:86,134 item 4 dropped; length.js:189-190.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: fixable code, zero suggestions, and the project's own skill forbids --fix because snaps move layout. 'Trustworthy autofix' and 'no visual regressions' are in the goal, and shadcn and oxlint-tailwindcss already refuse layout-moving fixes. Compounds with cs-01 (fixes past the scale ends) and cs-09. Plan item 4, stopped by the no-go.
findings.relates_to: docs/ESLINT_PLAN.md item 4 (not built), #166 (--preserve), #177 (visual evidence). Conflicts with the freeze (changes fix behaviour).

findings.title: Logical utilities, arbitrary properties and v3 prefixes pass unseen
findings.claim: `ps-[13px]`, `pe-`, `ms-`, `me-`, `start-`, `end-` and `scroll-ps-` produce no finding, although Tailwind 4.3.4 generates `ps-3` and RTL codebases use them instead of `pl`/`pr`; the project's own Phase 0 regex counts them (`p[xytrblse]`). Arbitrary properties `[padding:13px]` and `[margin-top:13px]` pass. A Tailwind v3 project with `prefix: 'tw-'` (26% of tailwindcss downloads are still v3) gets zero findings on `tw-p-[13px]` and no warning. @shadcn/lint and oxlint-tailwindcss report every one of these.
findings.evidence: eslint probe-forms.jsx lines 3-8 (ps/pe/ms/me/start/end-[13px]), 25-26 ([padding:13px], [margin-top:13px]), 30 (tw-p-[13px]): no message. Same lines under @shadcn/lint: 'Use "ps-3.25"', '"[padding:13px]" hardcodes an off-token value', '"tw-p-[13px]" hardcodes...'; under oxlint-tailwindcss: 'ps-3 (12px) or ps-3.5 (14px)'. src/core/tailwind-class-analysis.js:25 (`p(?:[trblxy])?`, anchored, bracket only); scripts/bench/tailwind-v4/measure.mjs:31-32; /tmp/rg-review-classes/out-2px.css:547 '.ps-3'; api.npmjs.org versions/tailwindcss/last-week: v3 25.9%.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: A team that writes logical utilities (any product with RTL) or runs a prefixed v3 design system installs the rule, sees nothing, and concludes their code is clean or the rule is broken. Either way the ratchet never starts.
findings.proposal: Extend the matcher: sides `[trblxyse]` for `p`, `m`, `scroll-m`, `scroll-p`; `start`/`end`; `inset-(x|y|s|e)`. Add arbitrary properties `[(padding|margin|gap|row-gap|column-gap|inset|top|right|bottom|left|inset-inline|inset-block|translate)(-[a-z]+)?:<length>]`, fixed to the utility when one exists. Add a `prefix` option (the v3 `tw-` form; the v4 `tw:` form already works), stripped before matching and written back in fixes; `doctor` warns when `tailwind.config.*` sets `prefix` and the rule does not. Six fixtures each; the Phase 0 measurement regex is the reference.
findings.truth_reason: Regex line 25: p(?:[trblxy])?, anchored, brackets only. ps/pe/ms/me/start/end-[13px], [padding:13px], [margin-top:13px], tw-p-[13px]: no message; tw:p-[13px] fixed. shadcn reports all nine; oxlint-tailwindcss 'ps-3 (12px) or ps-3.5 (14px)' and reports tw-p-[13px]. Tailwind 4.3.4 compile emits .ps-3. measure.mjs:31-32 uses p[xytrblse]. npm last-week: v3 44.2M of 170.8M = 25.9%.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: ps/pe/ms, tw-p- and [padding:13px] are all silent. Silent zero findings for RTL and prefixed v3 teams, and competitors report every one, but these are minority codebases and the gap is coverage rather than a first-hour bounce. Effort S with no message change, so it fits under the freeze.
findings.relates_to: none tracked. The logical utilities need no option change and fit the freeze as a bug fix; the `prefix` option is a small addition.

findings.title: Fix writes classes Tailwind never generates: -p-3, -gap-3
findings.claim: The utility regex allows a leading `-` on every utility, so `-p-[13px]`, `p-[-13px]` and `-gap-[13px]` are reported with 'Use "-p-3" (12px)' and fixed to `-p-3` or `-gap-3`. Tailwind 4.3.4 generates no negative padding or gap: compiling with those candidates emits `.-m-3` and `.-inset-3` but no `.-p-3` or `.-gap-3`. oxlint-tailwindcss reports the input as 'not a valid Tailwind class'; Rhythmguard turns one dead class into another and calls it fixed.
findings.evidence: eslint probe-forms.jsx 11:20 -p-[13px] FIX='-p-3' 'Use "-p-3" (12px) or "-p-4" (16px)'; 12:20 p-[-13px] FIX='-p-3'; 13:20 -gap-[13px] FIX='-gap-3'. tailwindcss 4.3.4 -i theme-2px.css with @source inline("p-3 -p-3 -gap-3 -m-3 -inset-3"): out-2px.css contains .-m-3 and .-inset-3; grep for '.-p-3' and '.-gap-3' returns nothing. oxlint -c .oxlintrc.tw.json: '"-p-[13px]" is not a valid Tailwind class', '"-gap-[13px]" is not a valid Tailwind class'. src/core/tailwind-class-analysis.js:25,147-159.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: An agent told 'use -p-3' writes it, the lint passes, nothing renders, and the human blames the tool that suggested it. A message that names a nonexistent class is worse than no message.
findings.proposal: Keep the leading `-` only for utilities with negative forms (m*, inset*, top/right/bottom/left/start/end, translate*, scroll-m*, space-*). For `-p-*`, `p-[-N]`, `-gap-*` and `gap-[-N]` report 'Tailwind has no negative padding or gap; "-p-[13px]" produces no CSS' with no fix. Apply the same guard in `utilityClassFor` so `nearestUtilities` never names them, and in the audit's `fixedToken`.
findings.truth_reason: Regex line 25 allows leading - on every utility; utilityClassFor 147-159 re-signs. Probe: -p-[13px] and p-[-13px] FIX -p-3 'Use "-p-3" (12px) or "-p-4" (16px)'; -gap-[13px] FIX -gap-3; audit fixedToken identical. Tailwind 4.3.4 compile with @source inline: .-m-3 and .-inset-3 present, .-p-3 and .-gap-3 absent. oxlint-tailwindcss: '"-p-[13px]" is not a valid Tailwind class', same for -gap-. #241, #277 closed.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: -p-[13px] and -gap-[13px] fix to -p-3 and -gap-3, which Tailwind never generates. The input is already dead CSS (negative padding and gap do not exist), so few people write it; a wrong suggestion on nonsense input moves no persona much. Cheap bug-level guard.
findings.relates_to: #241 and #277 (closed) handled the sign of margins; none tracks this. Bug fix, inside the freeze.

findings.title: Findings in one className share one location; no messageIds
findings.claim: A finding is reported on the Literal node, so the five off-scale classes in `className="p-[13px] m-[13px] gap-[13px] px-[14px] py-[15px]"` are five diagnostics at 38:20-38:70. Editors underline the whole attribute, 'go to next problem' lands on the same spot five times, and an agent reading `eslint --format json` must regex the token out of the message text. The audit computes per-token columns (38:21, 38:30, 38:39, 38:50, 38:60) from the same analysis, and the span mapper the fixer uses already knows each token's raw range. The rule has no `meta.messages`, so consumers cannot key on a messageId.
findings.evidence: eslint --format json probe-forms.jsx: five messages at 38:20-38:70; probe-types.tsx two at 6:39-6:80. node src/cli/index.js audit . --format json: probe-forms.jsx:38:21, :38:30, :38:39, :38:50, :38:60. src/eslint/rules/tailwind-class-use-scale.js:25-31 (`node` only, no loc), 35-74 (no messages, no hasSuggestions); src/eslint/literal-spans.js:222-254 (raw range per token); src/audit/scan/templates.js:32.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: Editor feedback is in the solo-dev goal and agent-readable findings in the ai-assisted goal; a diagnostic that cannot point at the class is noise in both, and SARIF or PR annotations (#165) inherit the same blur.
findings.proposal: Compute `loc` from the span mapper: report `{ node, loc: { start, end } }` for the token's raw range in Literal, TemplateElement, VLiteral and SvelteLiteral, falling back to the node when the span cannot be aligned. Add `meta.messages` (`offScale`, `offScaleUtilities`, `negative`) with `data`, keeping the text identical, and expose `messageId` in the audit's `findings.tailwind`. Five tests: JSX attribute, template chunk, escaped literal, Vue, Svelte. Pair with cs-06's suggestions.
findings.truth_reason: context.report passes node only (rule 25-31); meta has no messages (35-74). Probe-forms.jsx line 38: five messages all 38:20-38:70; probe-types.tsx two at 6:39-6:80; messageId absent. Audit on the same line: 38:21, 38:30, 38:39, 38:50, 38:60 (templates.js:32 valueStart + segment.start). spanReplacer (literal-spans.js:222-254) already computes each token's raw range. #165 and #172 open.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: five findings at 8:92-142. Whole-attribute squiggles and regex-from-message parsing hurt the editor and agent paths on every multi-finding className, and the audit already computes per-token columns. Matters more once cs-06 adds suggestions. Bug-level with no message change, so it fits under the freeze.
findings.relates_to: docs/ESLINT_PLAN.md item 4 (messageIds), #165 (SARIF), #172 (structured findings). Fits the freeze as a quality fix.

findings.title: HTML class attributes and @apply have no path in any product
findings.claim: The audit scans nine template extensions and not `.html`: `probe.html` with `class="p-[13px] p-3.25 m-[13px]"` is not counted (templateFiles 11 of 12, four of them eslint configs). The ESLint route through eslint-plugin-html only lints `<script>`, so the class attribute is unreachable there too. In CSS, `@apply p-[13px] m-3.25 gap-4` and `@apply px-5 py-[18px]` are reported by neither `use-scale` nor the audit, which see only the `padding: 13px` declaration on the next line, although docs/TAILWIND.md tells users to lint their authored `@layer components` CSS, where `@apply` lives.
findings.evidence: node src/cli/index.js audit . --format json --ignore node_modules: scanned.templateFiles 11, no probe.html finding; src/audit/shared.js:38-48 (TEMPLATE_EXTENSIONS). eslint --config eslint.config.templates.mjs probe.html (eslint-plugin-html): 1 message at 5:25 (the <script> string), none for the class attribute on line 4. stylelint --config .stylelintrc.json app.css and the audit: only app.css:11:12 'padding 13px'; the @apply lines 10 and 14 are silent. docs/TAILWIND.md:97-101.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: Tailwind in plain HTML, Rails, Laravel, Django and component CSS with `@apply` is a large share of the solo-dev audience; a tool that promises 'CSS and class strings' and misses both forms sends them back to a grep script in CI.
findings.proposal: (a) Audit: add `.html`, `.htm`, `.php`, `.erb`, `.twig`, `.hbs`, `.mdx` with a `class="..."` / `class='...'` attribute scanner (the linear quote scanner already handles quoting) and keep the JS scanner for `<script>`. (b) `use-scale` and the audit's stylesheet pass: run the class analyzer over `@apply` params (postcss AtRule `apply`), report per token with the same message, fix the token in place. (c) Stop counting `eslint.config.*`, `*.config.*` and `.d.ts` as template files. Document the HTML path in the package README.
findings.truth_reason: TEMPLATE_EXTENSIONS (shared.js:38-48) has no .html; audit counts 12 template files (7 probes + 5 eslint.config.*), probe.html absent from findings. eslint-plugin-html: one message at 5:25 (script string), none for the class attribute. Stylelint use-scale and the audit on app.css report only 11:12 padding 13px; @apply lines 10 and 14 silent; grep src for @apply returns nothing. TAILWIND.md:97-101 recommends linting @layer components CSS.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: probe.html not counted, and @apply p-[13px] inside @layer components is reported by neither use-scale nor the audit, though TAILWIND.md sends users to that CSS. Widens reach to Rails, Laravel, Django and v3 @apply codebases rather than fixing the core personas' path; those users arrive through the audit, not ESLint.
findings.relates_to: none tracked; docs/TAILWIND.md:97-101 recommends linting the CSS where @apply lives. New coverage conflicts with the freeze.

findings.title: Svelte class: directives missed; Astro and audit report non-class attributes
findings.claim: With the real parsers, `class:gap-[13px]={on}` in Svelte is not reported by the rule or the audit. The Astro path has no class gate, so `title="p-[13px]"` is reported and fixed in `.astro` while Vue and Svelte skip it; the audit reports `title=` in all three. Vue, Svelte and Astro support is tested only against hand-written fake parsers, none of the three parsers is a devDependency, and the README lists Astro as supported with no code path and no test.
findings.evidence: eslint --config eslint.config.templates.mjs (vue-eslint-parser, svelte-eslint-parser, astro-eslint-parser installed in /tmp/rg-review-classes/node_modules): probe.svelte 4 messages, none for class:gap-[13px]; probe.astro 5:84 title FIX='p-3'; probe.vue and probe.svelte report no title finding. audit JSON: probe.vue:2:87, probe.svelte:5:82, probe.astro:5:85 are all title="p-[13px]". test/helpers/fake-template-parsers.js:1-15; repo node_modules: vue-eslint-parser, svelte-eslint-parser, astro-eslint-parser MISSING; packages/eslint-plugin-rhythmguard/README.md:91.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: A Svelte or Astro solo dev meets the two most visible inconsistencies in the first file they lint: a directive that passes and a tooltip that gets 'fixed'. Parser drift later turns a green CI into silence nobody notices.
findings.proposal: Add `SvelteDirective` with `kind: 'Class'` (the key text) to the Svelte listener and a `class:` prefix scan to the audit's template pass; gate the Astro path on `class` and `class:list` attributes and give the audit the same attribute gate (`class`, `className`, `class:list`, `:class`, bound `class`). Add the three parsers as devDependencies and one contract test per parser that lints a real file through ESLint, replacing the fake-parser tests.
findings.truth_reason: Real parsers: probe.svelte 4 messages, none for class:gap-[13px]; probe.astro 5:84 title FIX p-3; Vue/Svelte skip title. Audit reports title in probe.vue:2:87, probe.svelte:5:82, probe.astro:5:85 and misses the directive. Tests import only fake-template-parsers.js; grep astro in test/ empty; vue/svelte/astro parsers absent from devDependencies and node_modules; README:91. Note: Astro works through the generic Literal visitor, so 'no code path' means no Astro-specific one.
findings.materiality_reason: Svelte class: directives carrying arbitrary values are rare, the Astro title= fix is cs-04 under another parser, and fake-parser tests are a maintenance risk rather than a user-facing bounce. Moves a Svelte or Astro solo dev marginally. Keep as hygiene at the lowest priority.
findings.relates_to: #244 (closed, Vue/Svelte class attributes); README Astro claim. Bug fixes inside the freeze.

findings.title: No 'scale you actually use' report for class strings
findings.claim: The audit's Tailwind histogram counts only bracketed values ('13px x71, 14px x2'); bare step classes (`p-3.25`, `gap-4.5`, `p-13`, `p-5`) appear nowhere in the report, so a team cannot see which steps its class strings use or which repeated values its theme never declares. Phase 0's own conclusion was that 73% of off-scale values are undeclared conventions (5px x99, 18px x74) and that the useful product for Tailwind teams is 'you use 5px 99 times; your theme declares neither', the way `audit --scale auto` reads CSS. It was recorded as checkpoint input, not built.
findings.evidence: node src/cli/index.js audit . --ignore node_modules (text): 'TAILWIND CLASS-STRING DRIFT 82 total: 13px 71, -13px 2, 14px 2, 1.25rem 1, 10px 1, 15px 1, 18px 1'; no 3.25, 4.5, 13 or 5 rows although probe-steps.jsx has them. src/audit/contract.js:261 (countByValue over bracketed tailwindFindings only), src/audit/render-text.js:49. benchmarks/tailwind-v4/RESULTS.md ('511 of the 700 (73%) use a value that appears 5 or more times'; 'That points at a different job for Tailwind apps').
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: A design engineer adopting the ratchet first needs to know what scale the apps already follow and which conventions to promote to tokens; without that report the first run is 700 findings and no decision path, and the designer in the ai-assisted loop gets a lint log instead of a list of values to adopt or snap.
findings.proposal: Count every spacing utility in class strings (steps and brackets, variants stripped) into `contracts.scale.classUsage`: `{ px, count, files, declared, token }`. In text and markdown print 'Scale in use (class strings)' with the top undeclared values and a ready `@theme` line per value (`--spacing-5px: 5px`, or 'snap to 4px/8px'); feed the same rows into `--plan` as adopt/snap/allow decisions. Reuse the step parsing from scripts/bench/tailwind-v4/measure.mjs.
findings.truth_reason: contract.js:261-262 countByValue over tailwindFindings.rawValue, and findings exist only for bracketed tokens; render-text.js:49 prints it. Audit text: 'TAILWIND CLASS-STRING DRIFT 82 total: 13px 71, -13px 2, 14px 2, 1.25rem, 10px, 15px, 18px...' with no 3.25, 4.5, 13 or 5 rows though probe-steps.jsx has them. No classUsage in JSON or src. tailwind-v4/RESULTS.md:40-41,49-51 records the 73% finding and the checkpoint-input status.
findings.materiality_reason: Phase 0's own conclusion: 73% of off-scale values are undeclared conventions, and the useful product is 'you use 5px 99 times; your theme declares neither'. Gives ds-team a decision list on the first run and feeds --plan; no competitor does it. Depends on cs-02 step parsing. New feature, ruled out by the freeze.
findings.relates_to: benchmarks/tailwind-v4/RESULTS.md (recorded as 2027-03-31 checkpoint input), #171 (State of Spacing). Conflicts with the freeze (new audit feature).

findings.title: Every literal reported twice; on-scale raw values count as drift
findings.claim: The audit runs use-scale and prefer-token together (src/audit/scan/stylesheets.js:66-89), so each off-scale literal yields two findings at one position, and prefer-token, running with tokenMapFromCssCustomProperties (same-file tokens only), also flags every on-scale raw literal with 'No known token holds this value' even when the audit's own token contract names the token. On the 300-stylesheet fixture: 5,841 CSS findings at 4,265 positions, 1,576 off-scale each twinned, 2,689 on-scale raw literals, totalFindings 5,986 against 1,721 real off-scale plus Tailwind. The contract lists 8px as --space-2 (332 matches) while all 332 prefer-token findings for 8px deny a token exists. Changing 13px to 8px, the fix the message asks for, is new drift and fails --fail-on-new-drift.
findings.evidence: Fixture /tmp/rg-review-ci/project (generated by /tmp/rg-review-ci/gen.mjs). `node <repo>/src/cli/index.js audit ./src --scale auto --format json` then node analysis: 'css 5841 {off-scale:1576, token-opportunity:4265}; token-opportunity at the same position as an off-scale finding: 1576 of 4265; unique CSS positions: 4265; rawValueMatches 8px count 332 tokens --space-2; token-opportunity findings for 8px: 332, text "No known token holds this value"'. After `perl -0pi -e s/13px/8px/ src/components/component-1.css`, `--since-baseline --fail-on-new-drift` printed 'NEW rhythmguard/prefer-token token-opportunity src/components/component-1.css:61' and exit 1. Totals: src/audit/contract.js:280; lock-in: test/cli/audit-cli.test.js:942 ('use-scale and prefer-token each report it').
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: An agent told to 'fix every off-scale finding' (docs/FOR_AGENTS.md:12) gets a list 3.5x too long whose twin cannot name the token; a developer's correct fix fails the gate; a lead cannot approve a gate whose count triples real drift. The fix loop does not converge and the ratchet blocks the right move.
findings.proposal: One finding per literal. Pass the audit's resolved token definitions (contracts.tokens.definedTokens from scanned token files, token sources and packages) to prefer-token as an inline tokenMap so its message names var(--space-2) with its file; fold that into the off-scale finding as a `token` field instead of a second finding; keep on-scale raw literals as `token-opportunity` entries but exclude them from totalFindings, cleanliness, the badge, --max-findings and --fail-on-new-drift unless `--gate token-opportunity` is set. Bump baseline formatVersion to 4 with a reader for 3 so existing baselines keep comparing. Rewrite the assertion at audit-cli.test.js:942.

findings.title: Gate failure, crash and silent pass share one exit code
findings.claim: Every failure exits 1: missing directory, missing baseline, a bad flag combination and a failed gate (process.exit(1) at src/cli/audit.js:30,52; exitCode 1 at :119). A missing --token-source exits 0 and audits against whichever scale comes next. The Action adds --since-baseline and --fail-on-new-drift only when the baseline file exists, so a deleted or renamed baseline switches the gate off without a word. .rhythmguardrc.json is read from process.cwd() only (src/audit/config.js:36), so `audit packages/b` from a monorepo root ignores packages/b/.rhythmguardrc.json and its maxFindings 0. Stylelint distinguishes 1 fatal, 2 lint, 64 usage, 78 config; a CI step cannot tell drift from a broken run here.
findings.evidence: Probes on /tmp/rg-review-ci/project: `audit ./nope` -> 'Directory not found' exit 1; `--max-findings 0` -> 'Audit failed: total findings 5987 exceeds' exit 1; `--since-baseline ./missing.json` -> 'Baseline file not found' exit 1; `--fail-on-new-drift` alone -> usage error exit 1; `--token-source ./nope.json --format badge` -> exit 0. Monorepo /tmp/rg-review-ci/mono: from root `audit packages/b --scale auto --format json` -> command.config null, exit 0; from packages/b `audit ./src --scale auto` -> 'total findings 3 exceeds --max-findings 0' exit 1. rhythmguard-action action.yml: `if [ -n "$INPUT_BASELINE" ] && [ -f "$INPUT_BASELINE" ]; then common+=(--since-baseline ...)`. Stylelint codes: https://stylelint.io/user-guide/cli (Exit codes).
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: A design-system lead approves a blocking gate only when red means drift and green means the gate ran. Today a typo in a token path, a moved baseline or a package-level config all pass, and a crash is indistinguishable from drift in `if:` conditions, alerting and retries.
findings.proposal: Exit codes: 0 pass, 1 gate failed, 2 usage or config error, 3 runtime error; document the table in AUDIT.md and forward it in the Action's Verdict step. A configured token source that is missing or yields no tokens exits 2 unless `--allow-empty-token-source`. Discover .rhythmguardrc.json by walking up from the audited directory to the git top level, nearest wins, and record the file in command.config. In the Action, when `baseline` names a file that is absent, fail with exit 2 instead of skipping the gate; add a `require-baseline` input defaulting to true.
findings.truth_reason: Probes: ./nope, --max-findings 0, missing baseline, --fail-on-new-drift alone all exit 1 (audit.js:30,52,119); --token-source ./nope.json exits 0 with scale source scanned-css and a warning only. config.js:36 resolves from process.cwd(): from the mono root `audit packages/b` gives command.config null and exit 0 despite packages/b's maxFindings 0; from packages/b exit 1. action.yml:100-103 adds the gate only when the file exists. Stylelint constants.mjs: 1/2/64/78.
findings.materiality_reason: Reproduced: missing --token-source exits 0 on the default scale, packages/b/.rhythmguardrc.json with maxFindings 0 is ignored from the root, and the Action skips the gate when the baseline is absent. False greens stay invisible until trust is gone; the ratchet thesis needs green to mean the gate ran. S effort; config walk-up overlaps ci-07.
findings.relates_to: audit-and-cli map gap (missing --token-source exits 0); #174 (per-workspace config); docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:57 'put it in CI'; rhythmguard-action action.yml gate block

findings.title: PR surface buries new drift: annotations capped, comment near the limit
findings.claim: `--format github` emits every finding, not the new ones (src/audit/render-github.js:6,14): with a baseline and one new 7px line the run wrote 5,987 ::warning lines and the new finding was annotation 4,695; with --since HEAD it was 13th of 22. GitHub shows 10 warnings, 10 errors and 10 notices per step and 50 annotations per job and drops the rest silently. The Markdown comment is 64,473 bytes on 300 stylesheets (GitHub rejects bodies over 65,536; the map measured 354 KB on 2,001 files) because Repeated Raw Value Candidates joins every file name into rows of 6,600 to 6,900 characters, and its New finding table sits at line 129 of 150. Above about 100k findings the renderer throws RangeError.
findings.evidence: `audit ./src --scale auto --since-baseline ../out2/baseline.json --fail-on-new-drift --format github`: 'warnings=5987', `grep -n '"7px"'` -> lines 4695 and 4705; with `--since HEAD`: 'warnings=22', 7px at line 13. Markdown: `wc -c` 64473; `awk length` top rows 6614, 6671, 6909 at lines 89-93 (Repeated Raw Value Candidates); New finding table at line 129. Caps: https://github.com/actions/toolkit/blob/457303960f03375db6f033e214b9f90d79c3fe5c/docs/problem-matchers.md and https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/68471; comment limit: https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/27190 ('Body is too long (maximum is 65536 characters)'). Crash: audit-and-cli map, render-github.js:14 spread.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The one thing a developer needs in a PR, the drift they just introduced, is the thing least likely to be shown: a reviewer sees ten old warnings from the alphabetically first files and a comment that opens with histograms or fails to post at all.
findings.proposal: With --since-baseline, annotate only new findings as ::error (one per literal after ci-01), omit baseline findings, put the summary ::notice first, stop at 10 with a notice 'N more in the job summary', and replace the spread with a loop. In Markdown, lead with the new-findings table (limit 25, each with nearest steps and token), cap every file list at 5 plus '+N more', wrap histograms and the token contract in <details>, and keep the body under 20 KB; the Action writes the full report to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY and posts the short form.
findings.truth_reason: render-github.js:6,14 renders getAllFindings with no baseline filter. Baseline plus one appended 7px line: 5,988 ::warning lines, the 7px pair at line 1,211 (index depends on the edited file); --since HEAD: 14 warnings. Markdown 65,040 bytes, rows of 6,909/6,671/6,614 chars from render-markdown.js:246 joining uncapped entry.files (contract.js:72); New finding table at line 129 of 169. Toolkit doc: 10/10/10 per step, 50 per job; discussion quotes the 65,536 error. RangeError per the map.
findings.materiality_reason: render-github emits getAllFindings regardless of baseline, so one new finding sits among thousands under GitHub's 10-per-step cap; markdown joins every file name per candidate row and puts the New finding table last. This is the advertised PR path for solo-dev and ds-team, and it hides the one thing a reviewer needs. S effort; compounds with ci-01 and ci-09.
findings.relates_to: #165 (SARIF is the uncapped channel); audit-and-cli map gap (github format crash); docs/CI_ADOPTION.md:79-97; rhythmguard-action comment step

findings.title: A file rename fails the fail-on-new-drift gate
findings.claim: Baseline keys include the file path (src/audit/baseline.js:256-264), so `git mv src/components/component-7.css card-7.css` with no content change reports 23 new and 23 resolved and exits 1; with --since HEAD, the PR recipe, it is 0 resolved, 23 new, exit 1. Re-indenting the same file reports 0 and 0, so formatting is handled but moves are not. The only way past a rename is to rewrite the baseline, which also accepts any real drift in the same pull request.
findings.evidence: `git mv src/components/component-7.css src/components/card-7.css` then `audit ./src --scale auto --since-baseline ../out2/baseline.json --fail-on-new-drift --format json`: 'Audit failed: new drift found: 23 finding(s)', 'new: 23 resolved: 23 files of new findings: src/components/card-7.css', exit 1; with `--since HEAD`: 'Since baseline 0 resolved, 23 new', exit 1. Reformat probe (`sed 's/^  /    /'` on component-8.css): 'Since baseline 0 resolved, 0 new', exit 0. Key composition: baseline.js:256-264 (findingIdentity includes file).
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: Design-system teams move components between packages and rename files routinely; a ratchet that goes red on a rename is either disabled or reset, and a reset baseline is not a ratchet. 'Stable findings' is the persona's stated requirement.
findings.proposal: Pair findings across files: a new finding whose rule, type, property, value and occurrence index equal those of a resolved finding from a file that no longer exists is reported under baseline.moved, not new. With --since or --staged, read `git diff --name-status -M` (and `--cached -M`) to map old to new paths before comparison, and let --write-baseline carry the mapping forward. Add tests for a full rename, a partial move (half the findings move, half resolve) and a rename plus one new literal (must still fail).
findings.truth_reason: baseline.js:256-264 findingIdentity includes the file path and nothing in baseline.js pairs findings across files. On a copy: `git mv component-7.css card-7.css` then --since-baseline --fail-on-new-drift gives 23 new, 23 resolved, exit 1; with --since HEAD 23 new, 0 resolved, exit 1; re-indenting component-8.css gives 0 new, 0 resolved, exit 0. COUNCIL:41 reads as quoted.
findings.materiality_reason: Reproduced: git mv gave 6 new and 6 resolved on a full run, 6 new and 0 resolved with --since, exit 1 both. A visible false red per rename with an unsafe baseline rewrite as the workaround. Second-order to the silent failures: fewer runs hit it, and ESLint suppressions share the limit, though hand-rolled count ratchets do not.

findings.title: No SARIF and no GitLab Code Quality output
findings.claim: No SARIF or Code Quality renderer exists (grep over src finds nothing); the only CI-native output is GitHub workflow commands, which are capped (ci-03) and reach neither code scanning nor the Security tab. #165 (2026-09-24, 0 comments) already specifies SARIF 2.1.0 with partialFingerprints from the content key; the council moved it to Q2 2027. Code scanning dedupes by partialFingerprints, shows alerts on changed diff lines and takes 25,000 results per run. GitLab's merge-request Changes view needs a CodeClimate JSON array (description, check_name, fingerprint, severity, location.path, location.lines.begin), not SARIF. User docs name no CI provider but GitHub, while 3.17.0 added reading GitLab's own spacing scale.
findings.evidence: `grep -rli sarif src packages docs/*.md README.md` -> only docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md; `grep -n -i -E 'gitlab|bitbucket|azure devops|jenkins|circleci|code ?quality|sarif' README.md docs/CI_ADOPTION.md docs/AUDIT.md packages/rhythmguard/README.md` -> no matches. gh issue view 165: OPEN, created 2026-09-24, 0 comments. https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/code-scanning/integrating-with-code-scanning/sarif-support-for-code-scanning ('Code scanning uses partialFingerprints to accurately identify which results are the same across commits and branches'; results per run 25,000). https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/testing/code_quality/ (required fields; 'Code Quality results display in the merge request Changes view'). CHANGELOG.md:11 (GitLab scale in 3.17.0); docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:88.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: Enterprise design-system teams approve gates that land where they already review: code scanning, Azure DevOps, SonarQube, GitLab merge-request widgets. A capped annotation stream and a comment are not a reviewable artifact for them, so the gate never gets approved.
findings.proposal: Add render-sarif.js (one rule per finding type, message with nearest steps and token, partialFingerprints.primaryLocationLineHash from the content key, properties for value and property) and render-codeclimate.js (fingerprint = hash of the content key, severity major for off-scale, minor for token-opportunity); validate SARIF against the 2.1.0 schema in a contract test and assert the fingerprint survives a line shift; document `github/codeql-action/upload-sarif` and GitLab `artifacts:reports:codequality` in CI_ADOPTION.md; add `upload-sarif: true` to the Action.
findings.correction: GitLab spacing-scale reading landed on main after the 3.17.0 tag (commit 712cd14, #367) and sits under CHANGELOG [Unreleased], not in 3.17.0. Also, GitHub accepts 25,000 results per run but displays only the top 5,000 by severity.
findings.truth_reason: grep for sarif/codeclimate/code quality over src, packages, docs, README hits only COUNCIL; user docs name no CI provider but GitHub. #165 OPEN, 2026-09-24, 0 comments; COUNCIL:88 schedules it Q2 2027. GitHub doc confirms partialFingerprints/primaryLocationLineHash, 25,000 results per run, changed-lines display; GitLab doc confirms the six required fields and the Changes view. Only the GitLab scale reader's version is wrong.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified absent; #165 is open with 0 comments and the council deferred it to Q2 2027, a plan conflict. ds-team only, and the Stylelint rules already reach SARIF through community formatters, so only the audit's baseline view lacks it. Code scanning would also lift ci-03's cap, and GitLab users have no CI output at all.

findings.title: File-level cleanliness saturates; the badge misreports drift
findings.claim: Scale cleanliness is the share of audited files with zero findings (src/audit/contract.js:366-372), and it is the only gated and badged metric. On the fixture 9.5% of spacing declarations are off-scale (1,493 of 15,654; 32% of raw literals), yet cleanliness reads 4%, the badge says 'spacing drift 96%' in orange, 381 of 401 files are 'with issues', and --min-cleanliness 95 is unreachable until nearly every file is perfect. Token-opportunity findings dirty a file too. The map's 2,001-file corpus reads 0%. A number pinned at 0 to 4% cannot be ratcheted and does not match how teams state drift (State of Spacing uses per-100-files).
findings.evidence: Text output: 'Files with issues 381', 'Scale cleanliness 4%'; `--format badge` -> {"label":"spacing drift","message":"96%","color":"orange"}; `--badge-metric findings` -> 1721. Declaration count: `grep -h -E '^\s+(margin|padding|gap|inset|row-gap|column-gap)[a-z-]*:' src/**/*.{css,scss} | wc -l` = 15654, raw literals 4612; off-scale per 1,000 declarations 95.4. Gate reads the same file share: src/audit/baseline.js:307; badge: src/audit/render-badge.js:26-34.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The badge is the public claim and --min-cleanliness is the gate a lead signs off on; both say a codebase that is 90% on scale is 96% broken, so either the number is ignored or the tool is.
findings.proposal: Count checked spacing declarations per file in the audit's own PostCSS pass (collectDeclarations already walks declarations) and report driftDensity: off-scale findings per 1,000 spacing declarations, per file and overall, plus the on-scale share of raw literals. Define a clean file as one without off-scale or Tailwind findings. Add `--max-drift-density <n>` as a gate and `--badge-metric density` (0 to 5 brightgreen, to 20 green, to 50 yellow, else orange); keep cleanliness for compatibility and print both in text, Markdown, HTML and the Action outputs.
findings.correction: The audit reports 1,576 off-scale CSS findings (10.1% of 15,654 spacing declarations, 34% of 4,612 raw literals), not 1,493 (9.5%); the lower figure omits the 83 0.9rem findings. The conclusion that a 4% file-level cleanliness misstates roughly 10% declaration-level drift stands.
findings.truth_reason: Reproduced: Files with issues 381, cleanliness 4%, badge spacing drift 96% orange, findings metric 1,721, 15,654 spacing declarations, 4,612 raw literals. contract.js:366-372 is a file share; issueFiles (265-269) counts token-opportunity findings; the gate reads exactScaleCleanliness; render-badge.js:26-34. STATE_OF_SPACING.md:5,15 uses per 100 CSS files; COUNCIL:158 as quoted. Only the off-scale declaration count is off.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: cleanliness is the share of files with zero findings, the badge is 100 minus it, and it headlines quickstart, text, markdown and the badge. Misleading on every real repo, but the gate teams rely on is --fail-on-new-drift, badge adoption is near zero, and ci-01 first removes token-opportunity from the denominator. Density is a differentiator, not a blocker.
findings.relates_to: audit-and-cli map gap (file-granular cleanliness); docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:158 ('cleanliness is not a number DS leads report upward'); docs/STATE_OF_SPACING.md per-100-files; a new reported number belongs in 4.0 scope (#172)

findings.title: Monorepo: union scale, cwd-only config, baselines overwrite each other
findings.claim: Auditing a monorepo root with two packages whose token files define a 4px and a 5px ladder produced one union scale 0,4,5,8,10,12,15,16,20,24,25,30,32,40 from both files, so 10px passed in the 4px package. .rhythmguardrc.json is found only in process.cwd() (src/audit/config.js:36), so per-package configs are ignored from the root. Writing a baseline from package a and then from package b with full runs left 3 entries, all from b: an unscoped write replaces the file and only --since/--staged writes merge (src/audit/baseline.js:137-153). There is no workspace flag; a team needs N invocations, N config paths and N baselines by hand.
findings.evidence: /tmp/rg-review-ci/mono: from root `audit . --scale auto --format json` -> 'scale: 0,4,5,8,10,12,15,16,20,24,25,30,32,40 source: scanned-css files: packages/a/src/tokens.css;packages/b/src/tokens.css', off-scale only 13px in both packages (10px passes in a). `audit packages/b` from root -> 'config: null'. Two `--write-baseline ../../.rhythmguard-baseline.json` runs (from a, then b) -> 'baseline entries after two full package writes: 3 packages/b/src/card.css x3'. `audit --help | grep -i workspace` -> none.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The ds-team persona has apps in a monorepo with the scale in a token package; the tool silently blends two scales and drops package-level gates, which is the opposite of the stable CI gate they are asked to approve.
findings.proposal: Add `--workspaces` (and `audit.workspaces` globs): discover package roots (package.json or nearest .rhythmguardrc.json), run one audit per root with that root's config, token sources and inferred scale, and merge into one report with per-package contracts.scale and summary blocks; make every baseline write merge entries outside the audited roots instead of replacing the file (entries are already keyed to the git top level). Resolve config by nearest ancestor. Document the per-package matrix job in CI_ADOPTION.md.
findings.truth_reason: On a copy of the mono fixture: root `audit . --scale auto` infers 0,4,5,8,10,12,15,16,20,24,25,30,32,40 from both tokens files and reports only 13px in each package (10px passes in a). `audit packages/b` from root: command.config null (config.js:36). Two unscoped --write-baseline runs: 4 entries from a, then 3 entries all from b (baseline.js:137-153 merges only scoped runs). `--help` has no workspace flag. #174 'only on request' at COUNCIL:88; scale-and-tokens gap 14.
findings.materiality_reason: Reproduced: a root audit built a union scale from both packages and 10px passed in the 4px package; the per-package rc was ignored; an unscoped baseline write replaced the file. Silent false green for the ds-team persona, but only two-scale monorepos hit the union, per-package runs work today, effort is L and #174 says only on request.

findings.title: Editor shows all baseline drift; rules never read the baseline
findings.claim: Nothing under src/rules, src/core or src/eslint reads the baseline, so Stylelint in VS Code reports every pre-existing finding at full severity: component-7.css carries 46 baseline entries that all light up while CI gates only on new ones. The Stylelint VS Code extension offers only 'Fix all auto-fixable Problems' and source.fixAll.stylelint, so the one editor action snaps every old value at once, which docs/FOR_AGENTS.md:14 tells agents not to do. ESLint ships bulk suppressions (eslint-suppressions.json, --suppress-all, --prune-suppressions) for exactly this gap; Stylelint has nothing comparable, so the plugin has to carry it.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn -i baseline src/rules src/core src/eslint` -> no matches. `grep -c 'component-7\.css' ../out2/baseline.json` -> 46. https://github.com/stylelint/vscode-stylelint README ('Fix all auto-fixable Problems', `source.fixAll.stylelint`; no per-diagnostic quick fix). https://eslint.org/docs/latest/use/suppressions ('While the rule will be enforced for new code, the existing violations will not be reported'). docs/FOR_AGENTS.md:14.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: 'No noise' in the editor is the solo developer's first requirement, and an agent in Cursor or Claude Code reads the same diagnostics; forty old warnings per file bury the one new finding and invite a fix-all that moves layout.
findings.proposal: Add a `baseline` option to use-scale, prefer-token and the Tailwind ESLint rule (path, default auto-discovered .rhythmguard-baseline.json at the git top level, false to disable) that demotes baselined findings to severity warning with a '(baselined)' suffix or hides them with `baselineMode: "hide"`, computed with the same content keys the audit uses so editor and CI agree. Add `rhythmguard audit --prune-baseline` to drop resolved entries and exit 1 when stale entries remain, as ESLint does. Write a one-page EDITOR.md covering VS Code, stylelint.validate for SCSS and fix-on-save guidance.
findings.correction: Stylelint does have a comparable feature: bulk suppressions since 16.25.0 (--suppress, --suppress-location, stylelint-suppressions.json; error severity only; applied to file input, skipped for editor `code` input). The gap is therefore confined to editor runs and warning-severity setups. The proposal should document or build on Stylelint's and ESLint's suppressions (per ESLINT_PLAN.md:89) rather than add a `baseline` rule option, and must say that the audit baseline (content keys) and suppressions (file plus rule counts) are different ledgers.
findings.truth_reason: Rules read no baseline (grep over src/rules, src/core, src/eslint empty); baseline.json holds 46 component-7.css entries; vscode-stylelint README offers only fix-all, and its runner lints with code/codeFilename, which Stylelint's standalone.mjs:327 excludes from suppressions. But Stylelint 16.25.0 added experimental bulk suppressions (--suppress, stylelint-suppressions.json, error severity, ported from ESLint), and docs/ESLINT_PLAN.md:89 already chose ESLint's suppressions over a Rhythmguard baseline for ESLint.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: nothing under rules, core or eslint reads a baseline. A real differentiator, since Stylelint has no suppressions file, and old warnings plus fix-all are the editor noise solo-dev and agents hit. But it only bites legacy codebases that chose a baseline, and needs the finding key in core, which 4.0 already plans. Second-order to the gate findings.
findings.relates_to: none tracked; a new rule option conflicts with the freeze (docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:98); ESLint suppressions as precedent

findings.title: The GitHub Action is unpinned, stale and runs the audit four times
findings.claim: rhythmguard-action v1.0.0 was pushed 2026-09-17 and not since; 13 plugin tags (3.8.0 to 3.17.0) shipped after it, and its `version` input defaults to `latest`, so behaviour changes under users without an Action release. action.yml runs `npx --yes --package` four times per job (json, markdown, optional badge, github): four audits, measured 1.71 s against 0.46 s for one on the fixture, 3.7x the work and four exposures to the memory peak on big repos. It never passes --since, so annotations and the comment cover the whole tree, and the comment step posts the full Markdown under `set -euo pipefail`, so an oversized body fails the job for a reason unrelated to drift.
findings.evidence: gh api repos/PetriLahdelma/rhythmguard-action: pushed_at 2026-09-17T20:55:14Z, stargazers 0, tags v1 and v1.0.0; action.yml: `version: default: latest`, four `npx --yes --package "$pkg" rhythmguard` lines, no --since, comment step `set -euo pipefail` + `gh api ... -f body="$body"`. `git tag --sort=creatordate` after 2026-09-17 -> 13 tags. Probe: `time (for f in json markdown badge github; do audit ./src --scale auto --format $f; done)` real 1.71 s vs 0.46 s single. README.md:104; docs/CI_ADOPTION.md:18-34.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: README.md:104 and CI_ADOPTION.md:18 make the Action the shortest path to CI; a lead who inspects it finds an unreleased dependency floating on `latest`, and a developer on a large repo pays four audits per push.
findings.proposal: Add `rhythmguard render <report.json> --format markdown|github|badge|sarif` (pure renderers over the saved JSON) and make the Action audit once with `--format json --output`, then render the rest. Pin the Action's default `version` to the plugin version it was released with and release the Action from release.yml in lockstep (tag vX.Y.Z, move v1). Pass `--since ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}` for the annotation run, keep the full run for the comment and gate, write the full report to the job summary and post the short form (ci-03).
findings.truth_reason: gh api: pushed_at 2026-09-17T20:55:14Z, 0 stars, tags v1 and v1.0.0; 13 plugin tags since (v3.8.0 to v3.17.0). action.yml: version default latest (44), three unconditional npx runs plus optional badge (109-130), no --since, comment step `set -euo pipefail` with `gh api -f body` (146-153). Timing on the fixture: four formats 1.82 s versus 0.43 s for one. README.md:104 and CI_ADOPTION.md:18-34 as cited; no render subcommand in src/cli/index.js.

Add a 'Pre-commit' section to CI_ADOPTION.md with lint-staged (`"*.{css,scss,jsx,tsx}": "rhythmguard audit --since-baseline --fail-on-new-drift"`), husky and pre-commit-framework snippets, and one line explaining that --staged audits index content, not the working copy.
