findings.title: The JSON schema does not describe a finding
findings.claim: `--schema` types findings.css, findings.motion and findings.tailwind as bare `{type: array}` and contracts as `{type: object}` (src/audit/contract.js:447-470); only parseErrors and nonAuthoredFiles have item schemas. docs/FOR_AGENTS.md:44,49 promises that file, line, column, value, type, text and property are stable and typed, yet the `type` enum (off-scale, token-opportunity, tailwind-arbitrary-spacing, motion-*) appears nowhere in the schema, and the shipped examples already broke on a field name. A consumer cannot validate output, generate types, or detect a breaking change before an agent loop or dashboard goes blank.
findings.evidence: `node <repo>/src/cli/index.js audit --schema` parsed: 'findings.css: {"type":"array"} | contracts: {"type":"object"} | required: schemaVersion,command,summary,scanned,contracts,findings'. First css finding in the fixture JSON: {column,file,line,property,rule,text,type:"off-scale",value}; first tailwind finding adds fixedToken, nearest, rawValue, token, utility. docs/FOR_AGENTS.md:44,49; types/audit.d.ts:264,299 per the audit-and-cli map.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: Agents and dashboards key on the finding shape; without an item schema a renamed field is discovered by a failing fix loop or an empty report, not by a test, so 'stable 2.0 contract' is a claim rather than a check.
findings.proposal: Add item schemas for css, tailwind and motion findings with required fields and a `type` enum, schemas for contracts.scale, contracts.tokens (sources, chains, ladders, candidates) and baseline, an `$id` carrying the schema version, and `additionalProperties: true` kept for forward compatibility. Add a contract test that validates the fixture's `--format json` output against the schema (a small validator or ajv as a dev dependency) and fails on a field rename; derive the finding types in types/audit.d.ts from the same schema. Ship the schema file in the npm tarball.
findings.truth_reason: `--schema` prints findings.css/motion/tailwind as {"type":"array"}, contracts as {"type":"object"}, no $id; only parseErrors and nonAuthoredFiles have item schemas (contract.js:440-520). Fixture findings carry column,file,line,property,rule,text,type,value (Tailwind adds fixedToken,nearest,rawValue,token,utility) and no `type` enum appears. FOR_AGENTS.md:44,49 and types/audit.d.ts:264,299 as cited; test/api/audit-api.test.js:55 only asserts schemaVersion; schemas/ ships only community-scale.schema.json.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: css, motion and tailwind findings are bare arrays, contracts a bare object. Nobody validates it today (two external dependents, no known dashboards) and the examples broke from a wrong field, not a rename. A prerequisite that makes ci-01's shape change and a baseline format bump safe, but moves no persona on its own.
findings.relates_to: audit-and-cli map gap (loose schema); docs/FOR_AGENTS.md:44,49; docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:162 ('structured findings' for 4.0)

findings.title: Pack command audits against the built-in default scale, not the project's
findings.claim: agents/*/SKILL.md line 10 and docs/FOR_AGENTS.md:12,44 tell the agent to run `npx rhythmguard audit . --format json` and fix every `off-scale` finding. Without `--scale auto` or an rc `audit.scale`, the audit checks against the built-in [0,4,8,12,16,24,32]; neither `npx rhythmguard` nor `init` writes an rc. Probe on a project whose tokens.css defines --space-10: 40px, --space-12: 48px, --space-16: 64px: the pack command reported 8 findings with 40px, 48px and 64px off-scale (source 'default'); `--scale auto` reported one off-scale value (13px) with the scale read from src/tokens.css. The eval harness runs `--scale auto` (lib.mjs:143), so the pack's own command was never measured.
findings.evidence: agents/claude-code/SKILL.md:10; docs/FOR_AGENTS.md:12,44; src/cli/quickstart.js:134-141 (comment on #287: `audit .` alone uses the default scale); src/audit/shared.js:7; probe in /tmp/rg-review-ai-assisted/scale40: `node src/cli/index.js audit . --format json` -> scale.source default, 8 findings incl. padding 40px/48px and margin-bottom 64px off-scale; `audit . --scale auto --format json` -> source scanned-css, files [src/tokens.css], 5 findings, 1 off-scale; with `.rhythmguardrc.json` {"audit":{"scale":"auto"}} the bare command reports scanned-css.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The agent's first act under the pack is to snap correct 40px, 48px and 64px values down to 32px on any project whose scale is longer than seven steps or not 4px-based. The human watches the agent break good spacing, and the tool, not the pack, takes the blame and gets uninstalled.
findings.proposal: (1) Change the block to `npx rhythmguard audit . --scale auto --format json`, regenerate the packs, update the assertion at test/cli/agent-packs.test.js:23. (2) Make `init` and the quickstart write `.rhythmguardrc.json` with `{"audit":{"scale":"auto","tokenSources":[...detected token files]}}` so the bare command, CI and every pack agree (verified: the rc flips the bare command to scanned-css). (3) In 4.0 make `auto` the audit default and print the scale source on every run.
findings.truth_reason: Reproduced in /tmp/rg-verify-ai-assisted/scale40: bare `audit . --format json` reports source default with 40/48/64px off-scale (nearest 32px); `--scale auto` reads src/tokens.css, one off-scale; rc {"audit":{"scale":"auto"}} flips the bare run. SKILL.md:10, FOR_AGENTS.md:12,44, quickstart.js:133-137 (#287), shared.js:7, agent-packs.test.js:23 as cited; init writes only `extends`. Harness runs `--scale auto` at lib.mjs:126, not 143.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: all packs and FOR_AGENTS omit --scale auto, audit defaults to the seven-step 'default' scale, quickstart uses auto, init writes no rc, the test pins the bare command. The agent's first act snaps correct 40/48/64px on any longer or non-4px scale. One-line fix at the earliest step; compounds with ai-02, ai-05, ai-07.
findings.relates_to: #287 (quickstart next commands), #172 (one default scale in 4.0); audit map gap 'three default scales'; docs map gap 'quickstart writes no rc'

findings.claim: In a project with eslint and eslint-plugin-rhythmguard 3.17.0 installed from the registry, no Stylelint, and the globals.css every Tailwind v4 app has, `npx rhythmguard audit . --format json` exits 1 with 'Auditing stylesheets needs Stylelint' and reports zero Tailwind findings; `npx rhythmguard` (quickstart) exits 1 the same way; `init --agents all` still writes the pack that gives that command; `doctor` prints 'All checks passed'. The class-string scan needs no Stylelint: `--ignore "**/*.css"` returned the 3 Tailwind findings, because Stylelint is only loaded when cssFiles > 0. No pack text or README line gives the ESLint-only agent a command that works.

Add a pack line: 'If the project runs ESLint without Stylelint, run `npx eslint . -f json`; each message names the two utilities and `fix.text` is the replacement.' Largest persona segment (Tailwind plus ESLint), first command, small fix. Distinct from ai-01.

findings.title: Invented var() tokens never become findings, gates or lint errors
findings.claim: Agents invent plausible token names; Knapsack markets '95% fewer invented token names' and design-tokens-mcp's README names the failure. The audit detects `gap: var(--space-7)` as `contracts.tokens.missingTokens` and `summary.missingTokens`, but it is absent from `findings[]`, from `--format github` annotations, from `--max-findings`, and from baselines (`getAllFindings` = css + motion + tailwind), so `--fail-on-new-drift` passes. At lint time the strict config reported 5 problems on hero.css and none for the phantom var(). The pack says 'fix every off-scale finding', so an agent reading findings never sees it. The eval classifier returns `token` for any added `var(--space` with zero findings, so an invented token scores as a win.
findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/rg-review-ai-assisted/scale40: audit JSON findings.css excludes --space-7 while contracts.tokens.missingTokens = [{token:'--space-7', files:['src/hero.css']}]; stylelint strict run on src/hero.css: 5 problems, none on `var(--space-7)`. src/audit/baseline.js:233-239; src/audit/render-github.js (no missingTokens); scripts/bench/agents/lib.mjs:160-167; landscape map: knapsack.cloud claim, github.com/tablesleveldesign/design-tokens-mcp; prior art csstools/stylelint-value-no-unknown-custom-properties.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: On a tokenised codebase the typical agent failure is a token that resolves to nothing, so the browser silently drops the declaration; a scale ratchet that lets that through has its hole exactly where agents fail, and the eval that should expose it counts it as success.
findings.proposal: Emit `type: "missing-token"` findings in `findings.css` (file, line, column, property, value `--space-7`, `suggestions`: the three defined tokens nearest by name plus the token holding the nearest scale step), count them in totals, github annotations and baselines (contract 2.1, additive). Add `reportMissingTokens` to prefer-token, resolving through the token index and scaleSources, default on in 4.0. Make classifyOutcome check added tokens against `contracts.tokens.definedTokens`. Pack line: 'A token you write must appear in contracts.tokens.definedTokens; never invent one.'
findings.truth_reason: scale40 probe: `--space-7` appears only in contracts.tokens.missingTokens and summary.missingTokens, never in findings.css; getAllFindings (baseline.js:233-239) and render-github.js use css+motion+tailwind; --max-findings compares report.totalWarnings (contract.js:280, baseline.js:301). Strict config on hero.css: 6 problems, none on var(--space-7); no rule checks unknown custom properties. classifyOutcome (lib.mjs:160-167) returns 'token' for any added var(--space without consulting definedTokens. External claims match the landscape map.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: getAllFindings is css+motion+tailwind, missingTokens sits only in the contract summary, and the eval classifier counts any added var(--space as a token win. Invented tokens are the canonical agent failure (Knapsack, design-tokens-mcp); the gate, baseline and eval all let it through. Lint-time competitors catch unknown vars but not in a ratchet.
findings.relates_to: #172 (4.0 defaults); feature freeze (new rule option); Stylelint 18 referenceFiles and custom-property rules (landscape map); csstools/stylelint-value-no-unknown-custom-properties

findings.title: CSS findings carry no structured nearest step or token; no agent format
findings.claim: `findings.css[]` has column/file/line/property/rule/text/type/value; the nearest steps exist only inside `text`, and no token is named even when `--space-3: 12px` is defined, because the audit's Stylelint run omits `fixWith: "token"` and prefer-token says 'No known token holds this value' without naming the nearest one. Tailwind findings do carry `nearest` and `fixedToken`. Every CSS literal appears twice (off-scale plus token-opportunity at one position). The JSON for two files and ten tokens is 11 KB of definedTokens, unusedTokens, chains and ladders; 114 MB on 2,000 files. No `--format agent`, `scale` or `explain` command exists; the only structured way to learn the scale is a full audit.
findings.evidence: Probe JSON in /tmp/rg-review-ai-assisted/scale40: css finding text 'Unexpected off-scale value "13px". Use scale values (nearest: 12px or 16px).' with no token field; prefer-token twin 'No known token holds this value'; tailwind finding has nearest/fixedToken; file 11,084 bytes. src/audit/scan/stylesheets.js:66-90 (rule options, no fixWith), 218-234 (finding shape); `node src/cli/index.js --help` (five commands); `audit --plan` prints value/count/properties/nearest only; audit map numbers (114 MB JSON at 288k findings); docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:160 (proposal C).
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: An agent or a Lovable-style retry loop needs one line per finding with the exact replacement and the scale up front; oxlint-tailwindcss already prints 'Closest in your theme: w-50.5 (202px) or w-51 (204px). If none fits, add a token to src/styles.css'. Parsing prose and joining token tables is where agents guess.
findings.proposal: (1) Add `nearest: {lower: {value, token, utility}, upper: {...}}` to CSS findings by passing the token index the core already builds for fixWith token (src/core/token-index.js:80-170); merge the twin into one finding with `tokenOpportunity: true`. (2) `--format agent`: deterministic text, scale header with source, one line per finding such as `src/hero.css:2:26 margin-top 13px -> 12px var(--space-3) | 16px var(--space-4)`, missing tokens, no histograms. (3) `rhythmguard scale [--format json|md]`: values, source, files, token and utility per step, without scanning for findings. (4) `rhythmguard explain <value>`: nearest steps, tokens, utilities, occurrences, decision.
findings.truth_reason: CSS finding keys are column,file,line,property,rule,text,type,value; nearest steps live only in text. prefer-token says 'No known token holds this value' for 13px and even 40px although tokens.css defines --space-3 and --space-10; the audit passes no fixWith (stylesheets.js:66-90, grep empty). Tailwind findings carry nearest and fixedToken. Each literal is reported twice at one position; JSON is 11,041 bytes for two files. Five commands, seven formats, no agent/scale/explain; --plan prints value, count, properties, nearest.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: CSS findings lack nearest and token while Tailwind findings carry both; the audit omits fixWith token; twins double the list. Agents already read the 'nearest: 12px or 16px' prose, so naming the token and merging twins is the material part; --format agent, scale and explain add surface against the freeze. oxlint-tailwindcss already prints nearest steps for classes.
findings.relates_to: docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:160 proposal C (`rhythmguard context`, `--format agent`); audit map gap 'every literal reported twice'; feature freeze (new commands)

findings.title: No file-scoped audit or hook recipe; --since misses files agents just wrote
findings.claim: No doc mentions Claude Code hooks (grep for PostToolUse/hooks across docs and src: nothing). `audit` accepts only a directory ('Not a directory: src/hero.css') and has no `--files`. `--since HEAD` lists ACMR changes, so an untracked file the agent just created is scanned zero times until `git add -N` (probe: 0 files, then 2). Per-file Stylelint takes 0.9 s but infers the scale from the linted file alone: on hero.css it reported 'using preset rhythmic-4' and 'No known token holds 40px' while src/tokens.css defines --space-10: 40px. Claude Code's PostToolUse hook delivers `tool_input.file_path` and shows stderr to Claude on exit 2; skills accept `hooks:` and `paths:`.
findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/rg-review-ai-assisted/scale40: `audit . --since HEAD --scale auto --format json` -> cssFiles 0 with src/new.css untracked, cssFiles 2 after `git add -N`; `audit src/hero.css` -> 'Not a directory'; stylelint per-file run 0.91 s with the rhythmic-4 fallback and 'No known token holds this value' for 40px. src/audit/scan/files.js:143-334; src/audit/args.js:25-77 (no --files); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks (PostToolUse stdin tool_input.file_path, exit 2 shows stderr, matcher 'Edit|Write|MultiEdit', .claude/settings.json); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills (`hooks`, `paths`, `allowed-tools`); scale map gap 'Stylelint rule infers from the linted file only'.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: A fix loop converges only when the check runs on the file just written, within a second, against the project scale. Today the pack's only instruction is 'before finishing, run the whole audit', and the per-file path gives a different answer than the audit.
findings.proposal: Add `rhythmguard audit --files <path...>` (or file arguments) that scans only those files while resolving the scale, token index and rc from the project root (reuse src/audit/report.js:232-311). Ship `init --agents claude --hooks`: writes `.claude/hooks/rhythmguard-after-edit.sh` (reads stdin JSON, runs `audit --files "$file" --scale auto --format agent`, exits 2 with findings on stderr when non-empty) and merges a PostToolUse `Edit|Write|MultiEdit` entry into `.claude/settings.json`; add `paths:` and `allowed-tools: Bash(npx rhythmguard:*)` to SKILL.md. Document Cursor hooks and a lint-staged recipe with the same command.
findings.truth_reason: `audit src/hero.css` -> 'Not a directory' (files.js:26-28); args.js has no --files. Untracked src/new.css: `--since HEAD` scans 0 CSS files, 1 after `git add -N` (ACMR diff, files.js:266). Per-file Stylelint with scale auto on hero.css reports 'using preset "rhythmic-4"' and 'No known token holds' 40px despite src/tokens.css, also with both files in one run. No PostToolUse or hook recipe in docs or src. Claude Code docs confirm exit 2 shows stderr, Edit|Write matcher, skill `paths` and `hooks`.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: audit rejects file paths, --since uses git diff ACMR so untracked new files are skipped, no hook or lint-staged recipe exists, per-file Stylelint infers from the linted file alone. The persona's stated need is a loop that converges on the file just written; nothing runs within a second against the project scale today. Compounds with ai-01 and ai-10.
findings.relates_to: docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:160 (hook recipes); scale map gap 'infers from the linted file only'; #174 (per-workspace scales)

findings.title: Inline styles, .html and bare v4 steps from AI builders go unread
findings.claim: Probe: `style={{ padding: 13, marginTop: '13px' }}` in a .tsx, `style="padding:13px"` and `p-[13px]` in page.html, and `p-13 p-3.25` produced zero findings; only `gap-[13px]` in the .tsx was reported. Lovable's guardrail list names 'One-off values that bypass the design system's tokens or scale' and 'Inline styles that override the design system's defaults' and retries on them; Figma Make's example guideline reads 'All spacing must use design system tokens (gap-xl, p-2xl) — never hardcode pixel values'; neither exports a lint config, and Rhythmguard reads neither `design-system.json`, `v0.json` nor `Guidelines.md`. accreleus/quasar wrote its own lint for about 449 inline style objects. README.md:16 declares inline styles out of scope.
findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/rg-review-ai-assisted/phantom: scanned.templateFiles 1 (Box.tsx only), tailwind findings 1 (gap-[13px]), page.html not scanned, inline styles and p-13/p-3.25 unreported; src/audit/shared.js:38-48 (template extensions, no .html); https://docs.lovable.dev/features/design-systems; https://help.figma.com/hc/articles/43602393097239; https://github.com/accreleus/quasar/issues/370; README.md:16; landscape map gap 'AI builders' guardrail files'.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The AI-assisted designer's code arrives from these builders as inline styles, arbitrary values and canonicalised bare steps; a tool that reports nothing on it is judged wrong, not quiet, and the builder's own retry loop stays the only enforcement.
findings.proposal: (1) Scan `.html`, `style="..."` attributes in HTML/JSX/Vue/Svelte, and `style={{ paddingTop: 13 }}` object literals (bare number = px) through the existing value engine as finding type `inline-style`, with nearest steps and tokens. findings.title: Agents' disable comments vanish from audit, baseline and CI; no sanctioned escape
findings.claim: An agent that adds `/* stylelint-disable-next-line rhythmguard/use-scale, rhythmguard/prefer-token */` removes that line's findings from the audit JSON, hence from baselines, `--fail-on-new-drift`, annotations and the PR comment; nothing counts suppressions (no 'disable' or 'suppress' key in the output; the audit calls stylelint.lint without ignoreDisables or reportNeedlessDisables). Opus 5 did exactly this in edition 1 and the eval counts it as failure, but the pack offers no legitimate alternative: decisions live in `.rhythmguardrc.json`, which the pack never mentions, and there is no inline allow-with-reason comment. accreleus/quasar built `design-lint-allow` with a required reason for this exact need.
findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/rg-review-ai-assisted/scale40: after adding the disable comment to src/hero.css line 2, audit findings dropped from 6 to 5 (both line-2 findings gone) and the JSON contains no suppression count; src/audit/scan/stylesheets.js:107-123 (lint call); docs/FOR_AGENTS.md (no mention of disable comments or decisions); docs/agent-evals/2026-10-10.md:66 (ignore-comment outcome); https://github.com/accreleus/quasar/issues/370; docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:160 (tamper-evident suppressions).
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The ds-team buyer pays in trust that the ratchet cannot be gamed; an agent-written disable comment is invisible to the gate, and the agent has no sanctioned way to say 'this 13px is intentional, here is why', so it takes the invisible one.
findings.proposal: Run the audit's Stylelint pass with `ignoreDisables: true` and report disabled findings as `suppressed: true` with the comment text, counted separately in summary, annotations and the markdown table; baselines ignore the flag so a new suppression counts as new drift under `--fail-on-new-drift`. Add an inline `/* rhythmguard-allow 13px: reason */` recognised by the rules and the audit, recorded under `contracts.decisions.inline[]` with file, value and reason, listed in `--format agent`. Pack line: 'To keep an off-scale value, write a rhythmguard-allow comment with the reason; never a disable comment.'
findings.truth_reason: scale40 probe: the disable-next-line comment dropped findings from 6 to 4, both line findings gone; the JSON carries no disable or suppress key (contracts.decisions null). stylesheets.js:109 calls stylelint.lint without ignoreDisables or reportNeedlessDisables; src and docs/rules have no rhythmguard-allow or disable handling; FOR_AGENTS.md never mentions disable comments, decisions or .rhythmguardrc.json. Nuance: contracts.decisions.suppressed appears only when rc decisions exist and counts adopt/allow matches, not comments (0 here).
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: stylelint.lint runs without ignoreDisables, so disable comments vanish from JSON, baselines and --fail-on-new-drift; the pack never names rc decisions as the sanctioned route, and Opus took the disable in edition 1. A ds-team trust hole plus a missing agent escape hatch; the pack line is cheap, suppressed-finding reporting is medium. Overlaps ai-11 on decisions.
findings.relates_to: docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:160 (tamper-evident suppressions); audit map capability 'Decisions and --plan'; packages/eslint-plugin-rhythmguard/README.md bulk suppressions (ESLint side)

findings.title: Off-scale values reach the designer as a lint log, not a decision sheet
findings.claim: `--plan` is the only designer-facing artifact: one JSON entry per off-scale value with count, properties and the two nearest steps; no token names, no utilities, no file list, no Tailwind entries, and it must be hand-copied into `.rhythmguardrc.json`. The pack tells the agent 'Ask before adding any; do not guess a scale' when the source is fallback, but gives the human nothing to answer with. OpenCRVS wrote 'A size that is not on the scale is a design question. Ask design. Do not round it in silence'; sound-barrier/recall#781 added five scale stops rather than snap 1,874 values.
findings.evidence: `node src/cli/index.js audit . --scale auto --plan` on /tmp/rg-review-ai-assisted/scale40 printed {value:'13px', decision:'undecided', count:1, properties:['margin-top'], nearest:['12px','16px']} and nothing else; src/audit/decisions.js:23-129; agents/claude-code/SKILL.md:16; https://github.com/opencrvs/opencrvs-core/issues/12627; https://github.com/sound-barrier/recall/pull/781; landscape map gap 'off-scale values as a design question'.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The AI-assisted designer is the person who decides adopt versus snap; if the decision cannot be made in a file they can read and edit, the agent either guesses or stalls, and the scale never gains the step the product needed.
findings.proposal: `rhythmguard audit --plan --format markdown` (and `agent`) writes a 'Spacing decisions' sheet: per value, count, files with line references, properties, nearest steps with their tokens and utilities, Tailwind entries, a suggested decision (adopt when the count is high and the value sits on the base grid, snap otherwise) and a checkbox column. `rhythmguard decide --from decisions.md` writes the rc and `fix --decided` applies the snaps. Pack line: when a finding is intentional, add it to the sheet rather than changing the value.
findings.correction: `--plan` already includes Tailwind arbitrary values, grouped under the property name 'class-string' (decisions.js:19-21, report.js:155-163) without the utility name; the missing pieces are token names, utilities, file and line lists, a designer-readable format and a write-back path into .rhythmguardrc.json, not Tailwind coverage.
findings.truth_reason: `--plan` verified: one JSON entry per value with count, properties and nearest; no tokens, utilities, files or markdown; stdout or --output only, no decide command; SKILL.md:16 as cited; OpenCRVS and recall#781 match the landscape map. But Tailwind findings do enter the plan: report.js:155-163 passes collectTailwindFindings, and the phantom probe lists 13px, count 2, properties ["class-string"]. decisions.js:19-21 maps class-string findings deliberately.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: --plan prints JSON only with count, properties and nearest steps, no tokens, utilities, files or Tailwind entries, and the pack never mentions decisions. Phase 0 and OpenCRVS show adopt-versus-snap is the designer's call, so a readable sheet closes that loop; the markdown render is the material piece, while a decide command adds surface under the freeze.

findings.title: Three length rules are 50-75% copies; every fix is a multi-file edit
findings.claim: use-scale (421 lines), prefer-token (348) and no-offscale-transform (285) are variants of one rule. no-offscale-transform shares 107 of its 143 distinct non-trivial lines with use-scale (75%), prefer-token 86 of 173 (50%). The visit/bounds/report scaffold is pasted three times (use-scale 319-407, transform 227-271, prefer-token 296-325); decisions load through a helper in one rule and an inline try/catch in another; the #234 Sass-operand guard reached two of three rules, so --fix still rewrites translateX($n * 13px). Since 2026-06-01, 17 of the 19 commits touching a rule file touched two or more. ARCHITECTURE.md:60 promises an assembly of primitives, not a copy.
findings.evidence: scratchpad dup.js shared-line count: 'no-offscale-transform (143 distinct) vs use-scale: shared 107'; `git log --since=2026-06-01 --name-only -- src/rules/*/index.js` → 17 of 19 commits touch 2+ rule files; src/rules/use-scale/index.js:70-80 (readDecisions) vs src/rules/no-offscale-transform/index.js:74-79 (inline); sassOperandNodes imported at use-scale/index.js:28 and prefer-token/index.js:24 only.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: Trustworthy autofix is the solo-dev's first ask. A guard that lands in two of three rules means --fix rewrites a Sass operand in the third, and one bad diff ends adoption. For a solo maintainer every behaviour fix costs three edits and three chances to miss one.
findings.proposal: Extract one createLengthVisitor({ options, tokenRegex, sassOperands, checkedBounds, onLength }) into core/value-nodes.js (the function/bound/word/keyword/math-argument decisions, about 60 lines in each rule today) and one runLengthRule({ ruleName, messages, validate, buildOptions, selectDeclaration, onLength }) in src/rules/kit.js (validate, options, decisions, resolve scale, token index, walk, write). Each rule keeps its property selection, message texts and checkLengthValue/checkWordNode. Expected: about 250 fewer lines, operand and bounds guards present in all three by construction, no message change. Verify with the 369 rule and core tests and `npm run bench:quiet -- --check` before and after.
findings.truth_reason: Reproduced: wc 421/348/285; shared distinct lines (minLen 12) transform 108 of 144 (75%), prefer-token 86 of 174 (49%); git log since 2026-06-01: 19 commits, 17 touch two or more rule index files; readDecisions helper at use-scale:70-80 versus inline try/catch at transform:74-79; sassOperandNodes imported only at use-scale:28 and prefer-token:24; ARCHITECTURE.md:60 wording present. Probe with postcss-scss: no-offscale-transform --fix rewrote translateX($n * 13px) to $n * 12px with no warning; use-scale reported it unchanged.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: no-offscale-transform lacks the #234 guard, so --fix rewrites Sass operands, but that is a three-line guard reaching few users (SCSS, transforms, arithmetic, --fix). The extraction itself changes nothing a persona sees; its value is one edit per behaviour fix for a solo maintainer and the 4.0 9,000-line budget. Compounds with cq-05.
findings.relates_to: rules-core map gap (operand guard missing in two rules); #234, #272; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:60-68; pure refactor, compatible with the freeze

findings.title: Audit classifies findings by regex over message text with no covering test
findings.claim: src/audit/scan/stylesheets.js:205-216 classifies every Stylelint warning with four regexes over warning.text; anything unmatched becomes type 'off-scale' with value null (lines 335-348). Of the 15 message shapes the four rules can emit, 5 do not match: use-scale rejectedNegative, rejectedPercentage and invalidPreset, no-offscale-transform with a clamp()/min()/max() position, and the invalid-tokenPattern root report. They are unreachable from the audit only because it hard-codes its rule options. Nothing tests either fact: no test imports getCssFindingType or collectCssFindings; ARCHITECTURE.md:70 asks for two-place edits by hand.
findings.evidence: Probe calling each messages.* factory against the four regexes: 'use-scale rejectedNegative NO MATCH -> off-scale, value null', 'transform rejected position NO MATCH', 5 of 15; `grep -rln 'getCssFindingType\|collectCssFindings' test` returns nothing; src/audit/scan/stylesheets.js:205-216, 335-348.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The CI gate and baseline ratchet count whatever the regexes produce. A reworded message makes the audit quieter, not louder, and the gate passes; a design-system lead who discovers that later stops trusting the number. Agents reading findings.css[].value get null.
findings.proposal: Put the parser next to the templates: src/core/finding-messages.js exporting the format helpers and parseFindingText(text) -> { type, value, position } | null, used by all rules and the audit. Add test/contracts/finding-messages.test.js that calls every messages.* factory of every rule with representative arguments (position, note, aside, group, candidates) and asserts parseFindingText returns the expected type and value, or that the message is on an explicit root-level allowlist. Make the audit record an unparsed warning as type 'unclassified' and print it instead of counting it as off-scale with a null value. One day.
findings.truth_reason: stylesheets.js:205-216 holds the four regexes; getCssFindingType (335-348) defaults to off-scale and getCssFindingValue to null. No test names getCssFindingType or collectCssFindings. Calling every messages.* factory: invalidPreset (same text in three rules), use-scale rejectedNegative and rejectedPercentage, transform rejected with a bound position, and the tokenPattern root report miss (7 counting invalidPreset per rule). Unreachable today because the audit hard-codes use-scale options (stylesheets.js:66-90), --scale takes only auto or a list (args.js:248-265), and never runs no-offscale-transform.
findings.materiality_reason: Latent, not live: the five unmatched message shapes are unreachable with the audit's hard-coded options, so no gate is wrong today. Value is insurance for the ds-team's stable-findings gate, which the 4.0 plan already covers (structured findings, COUNCIL:80); the one-day parser test is the right pre-4.0 guard. Compounds with cq-08.
findings.relates_to: quality-engineering map gap (untracked); docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:70; freeze rule 'patches never change messages' (this enforces it)

findings.title: 43 bare catches turn user mistakes into silent fallbacks
findings.claim: `grep -rnE 'catch\s*\{' src` finds 44 catch blocks without a binding (one inside a string), 16 returning null/[]/false. Eight swallow user input: a throwing tailwind.config.js (token-map.js:286), an unreadable tokenMapFile (token-map.js:145), a malformed .rhythmguardrc.json (decisions.js:110), an invalid community preset (presets/scales.js:114), an unparseable package.json (scale-inference.js:55), an invalid property regex (options.js:148), an invalid tokenPattern in inference (scale-inference.js:497), an unreadable audited file (stylesheets.js:148,248). Verified: a truncated rc file lost its adopt decision and use-scale reported 13px with no root problem; a tailwind.config.js that throws made prefer-token say 'No known token holds this value'. Only doctor notices the rc problem.
findings.evidence: scratchpad/silent probe: 'malformed rc + use-scale: 1 warnings; Unexpected off-scale value "13px" ... invalidOption: 0'; 'throwing tailwind config + prefer-token: Unexpected raw scale value "13px". No known token holds this value ... invalidOption: 0'; `rhythmguard doctor` on the same dir: '✗ .rhythmguardrc.json is not valid JSON'.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The design-system persona pays in trust: a typo in a token path or rc file makes the gate pass against the fallback scale, and the agent is told no token exists and writes a literal. Silent fallbacks are the failure mode that makes a team stop believing the tool.
findings.proposal: Extend the warnings channel token sources already have (warnings[] with file and message) to decisions, token map, Tailwind config, presets and discovery: push a warning instead of returning empty. The rule reports them once on the root through reportProblem (exists); the audit lists them under tokenSourceWarnings and makes that field reach the v2 JSON (it does not today). Keep bare catches only where the failure is expected and commented (stat of an absent file). Add `no-restricted-syntax` on CatchClause without a param and without a leading comment to eslint.config.js so new silent catches need a justification. Under a week.
findings.truth_reason: grep finds 44 bare catches, one inside the child-process script string (token-map.js:318); 14 return null/[]/false on the next line. All eight cited sites verified. Probe: truncated .rhythmguardrc.json with use-scale {decisions:true} gave one 13px warning and no root report, because decisions.js:110 swallows the parse error before readDecisions can report it; a throwing tailwind.config.js with prefer-token gave 'No known token holds this value'; doctor printed '.rhythmguardrc.json is not valid JSON', exit 1. v2 JSON keys lack tokenSourceWarnings.
findings.materiality_reason: Reproduced on the Stylelint path: a truncated rc silently dropped an adopt decision with no root problem, and a throwing tailwind config produced 'No known token holds this value'. Correction: the audit CLI exits 1 on an invalid rc, so the silence is editor and stylelint-CI linting, where all three personas live. Setup-stage, trust-defining.
findings.relates_to: quality-engineering map gap; audit-and-cli gap 'missing --token-source is exit 0'; no conflict with the freeze

findings.title: Discovery anchors on process.cwd(), not the linted file
findings.claim: src/core calls process.cwd() in 13 places: rc decisions (decisions.js:100), installed packages and rc token sources (scale-inference.js:84,158,238,487,530), tokenMapFile and tailwindConfigPath (token-map.js:137,369); fs-cache keys are 'rc <cwd rc path>' and 'packages <cwd>'. Only token-map.js:214 reads root.source.input.file, for display. Verified in a workspace fixture: with the editor or CLI cwd at the monorepo root, use-scale ignored packages/app/.rhythmguardrc.json (its adopt decision and its token source), fell back to rhythmic-4 and reported 13px; from packages/app it honoured both. One cwd means one scale and one decision file per process.
findings.evidence: scratchpad/mono/probe.js: 'cwd=<root>  Unexpected off-scale value "13px" ... No spacing tokens were found for scale "auto"; using preset "rhythmic-4"' vs 'cwd=packages/app  Unexpected off-scale value "7px" ... (nearest: 5px or 10px)'; `grep -rn 'process.cwd()' src/core src/rules | wc -l` = 13; src/core/scale-inference.js:85,384 cache keys.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The design-system persona works in a monorepo with apps and a token package and opens the root in the editor. Anchoring on cwd means decisions and scales silently stop applying from the root; this is #174's per-workspace problem at its root cause.
findings.proposal: Resolve discovery from the file: projectRootFor(file) walks up from path.dirname(root.source.input.file) to the nearest .rhythmguardrc.json or package.json, cached per directory through cachedByFiles (already supports arbitrary keys), falling back to cwd only when the file has no path (stdin). Route loadRcDecisions, rcTokenSources, discoverTokenPackages and token-map path resolution through it; the audit passes each file through the same function so a monorepo audit gets one scale per package. Behaviour change, so 4.0; under a month with the existing fixture style.
findings.truth_reason: 13 process.cwd() calls in src/core and src/rules at the cited lines; cache keys packages:<cwd> (scale-inference.js:85) and rc:<rcPath> (:384); token-map.js:214 reads root.source.input.file only for displayOrigin; cachedByFiles accepts any key. Monorepo fixture reproduced exactly: from the root, use-scale reported 13px with 'No spacing tokens were found for scale auto; using preset rhythmic-4' and 7px nearest 4px or 8px; from packages/app the adopt decision suppressed 13px and 7px got nearest 5px or 10px.
findings.materiality_reason: Reproduced: from the workspace root, use-scale ignored packages/app/.rhythmguardrc.json (decisions and token source) and fell back to rhythmic-4; from the package it resolved the 7px ladder. The reference ds-team opens the monorepo root in the editor. Conflicts with the plan of record's timing (#174 'only on request', Q2 2027); behaviour change, so 4.0.
findings.relates_to: #174 (per-workspace scales); docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:158; conflicts with the freeze (behaviour change), fits the 4.0 scope

findings.title: Audit retains every AST and every finding; output is unbounded
findings.claim: runStylelintAudit passes the whole file list to one stylelint.lint() per syntax (stylesheets.js:112,119); each result keeps _postcssResult, so every file's PostCSS AST lives until the last file is linted. On 300 files / 120k declarations: one call 484 MB RSS, 241 MB heap; the same lint in chunks of 25 keeping only {source, warnings} 301 MB RSS, 79 MB heap. Every declaration yields two finding objects (240,000 findings for 120k declarations), JSON is 85 MB (355 bytes per finding), render-html.js:48 embeds the full JSON in a <pre>, and the baseline records every finding. The previous stage measured 1.1 GB RSS and 161 MB HTML at 2,001 files.
findings.evidence: scratchpad/mem/api.js with `node --expose-gc`: 'single warnings 240000 rss 484 MB heapUsed 241 MB' vs '25 warnings 240000 rss 301 MB heapUsed 79 MB'; 'retains _postcssResult: true'; `/usr/bin/time -l node src/cli/index.js audit ./src --format json`: 767 MB max RSS, 85,140,964 bytes.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: Monorepos are where a drift audit earns its place in CI, and CI boxes have 2-4 GB. A 1 GB process and a 100 MB baseline that cannot be committed make the ratchet unusable at exactly the size the 4.0 thesis targets.
findings.proposal: (1) Lint in chunks of 50 files per stylelint.lint() call and copy out only {source, warnings, invalidOptionWarnings} so ASTs are released (stylesheets.js:107-123); measured 3x heap reduction. (2) Stream renderers: json, markdown and html write findings through a writable instead of building one string; HTML gets a findings table capped at 1,000 rows plus a link to the JSON file, not an embedded dump. (3) Baseline formatVersion 4 stores content keys only (rule, type, file, property, value, occurrence), which is all the comparison uses. Expected on the 2,001-file corpus: under 400 MB, HTML under 1 MB, baseline a third of today.
findings.truth_reason: stylesheets.js:112,119 call stylelint.lint once per syntax; results[0]._postcssResult is retained (true). 300 files x 400 declarations: one call rss 577 MB, heap 333 MB; chunks of 25 keeping {source, warnings} rss 374 MB, heap 89 MB (3.7x). CLI audit --format json: 926 MB max RSS, 78.8 MB JSON, 365 bytes per finding, 216,000 findings for 120,000 declarations (two per off-scale declaration). render-html.js:48 embeds the full JSON; writeBaseline records every finding; audit-cli.test.js:942 locks the double report.
findings.materiality_reason: Monorepo CI is the 4.0 target, and the previous stage measured 1.1 GB RSS, 114 MB JSON and a 138 MB baseline at 2,001 files; an uncommittable baseline disables the ratchet outright. The double report (use-scale plus prefer-token twins, audit map) halves every number here and should ship with it.
findings.relates_to: audit-and-cli map gaps (memory, HTML dump, double reporting locked by test/cli/audit-cli.test.js:942); #165 (SARIF would be one more streamed renderer)

findings.title: Runtime source is untyped; the hand-written d.ts drifts silently
findings.claim: tsconfig.typecheck.json includes only types/, three fixtures, src/configs and examples; 0 of 60 src files carry @ts-check. Running tsc with the repo's own settings over src/**/*.js reports 148 errors in 27 files (63 in 13 files with strict off); 33 files are already clean. They are real shape mismatches (report.js:45 reads readSource off a union that lacks it; codemod.js:37 indexes an untyped []), plus 5 TS2309 from the `module.exports = fn; module.exports.x =` pattern in src/index.js and the four rules. types/audit.d.ts has 17 unknowns (tokenContract is Record<string, unknown>, findings unknown), and both shipped examples read finding.message, a field that does not exist.
findings.evidence: scratchpad/checkjs/out.txt (tsconfig extends the repo's tsconfig.typecheck.json, include src/**/*.js): 'errors: 148', 27 files; out2.txt with strict false: 63; `grep -cE '\bunknown\b' types/audit.d.ts` = 17; examples/audit-dashboard.mjs:77, examples/audit-figma-export.mjs:64.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: Agents and dashboard authors learn the finding shape from the d.ts; today it says unknown, and the only published API examples use a field that does not exist. The persona building with Claude Code or v0 gets a wrong contract from the one place that should be exact.
findings.proposal: Inside the freeze: (1) add src/**/*.js to tsconfig.typecheck.json include and `// @ts-nocheck` to the 27 failing files, gating the 33 clean files today; (2) burn down the 63 strict-off errors, then strict (about a week); (3) declare Finding, TokenContract and AuditContractReport as JSDoc typedefs in src/audit/contract.js, generate the audit section of types/audit.d.ts with `tsc --declaration --emitDeclarationOnly` into a scratch dir, and add a contract test that diffs it against the committed file so drift fails the gate. Fix both examples to finding.text.
findings.correction: 148 strict errors fall in 25 files, leaving 35 of 60 src files clean (not 27 files and 33 clean); every other number, the five TS2309 sites and both example errors reproduce exactly.
findings.truth_reason: Ran tsc 7.0.2 with a tsconfig extending the repo's and including src/**/*.js: 148 errors in 25 files (not 27; 35 of 60 clean); strict off: 63 errors in 13 files; 5 TS2309 in src/index.js and the four rules; report.js(45) readSource missing on the union; codemod.js(37) 'length' on never. 0 of 60 src files carry @ts-check; 17 unknown in types/audit.d.ts; examples/audit-dashboard.mjs:77 and audit-figma-export.mjs:64 read finding.message. The include list is as stated.
findings.materiality_reason: Both shipped API examples read a field findings never carry and the d.ts types findings as unknown, so dashboard authors and agents get a wrong contract from the one exact place. Fixing the examples is minutes; the checkJs burn-down is maintainer insurance with no visible change. Compounds with cq-08.
findings.relates_to: #280, #281, #284; quality-engineering map gap; audit-and-cli map (examples read finding.message)

findings.title: --format github crashes above ~100k findings
findings.claim: render-github.js:11 and :14 spread the whole findings array into Array.prototype.push. Node throws RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded past V8's argument limit: a synthetic report renders at 100,000 findings and crashes at 150,000; the previous stage reproduced it at 114,758 real findings. A CI step ends with a stack trace instead of annotations or a gate verdict. The same pattern sits at stylesheets.js:112,119,152 over per-file results, far from the limit today.
findings.evidence: `node -e` synthetic report through renderGithub: '100000 ok 6500105 chars', '150000 ERR RangeError Maximum call stack size exceeded'; src/audit/render-github.js:11,14.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The GitHub-annotation path is the documented CI recipe (docs/CI_ADOPTION.md); the first large repository that tries it sees a crash, which is the opposite of 'put it in CI'.
findings.proposal: Replace both spreads with for...of pushes (two lines). Because GitHub displays at most 10 warnings and 10 errors per step, emit the first 10 annotations per type plus one ::notice carrying the total and a pointer to the markdown or JSON output; everything beyond is discarded by GitHub anyway. Add a unit test that renders 200,000 findings. An hour.
findings.truth_reason: render-github.js:11 and :14 spread parseErrors and findings into Array.prototype.push. A synthetic report through renderGithub rendered 100,000 findings (14.4 MB) and threw RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded at 150,000, with the default stack and with --stack-size=984. stylesheets.js:112,119,152 use the same spread over per-file result arrays, bounded by file count. The audit-and-cli map records the identical crash at 114,758 real findings as an untracked gap; no fix exists in src.
findings.materiality_reason: Both spreads confirmed. The crash needs over 100k findings, which a large unmigrated monorepo reaches on its first --format github run because every literal is counted twice. A documented CI recipe dying with a stack trace is a bounce, and the fix is an hour; few users get there, and cq-03's streaming subsumes it.
findings.relates_to: audit-and-cli map (found, untracked); #165 SARIF; no conflict with the freeze

findings.title: Child-process Tailwind loader is untested and dead on Node 22
findings.claim: token-map.js:291-345 spawns `node -e <script> <config>` with a 5 s timeout to import an ESM tailwind.config when require() fails. No test executes it (the only spawnSync in src; no test references it). On Node 22.22.3 require() already loads tailwind.config.mjs and a "type": "module" .js config (verified), so the path is reachable only on Node 20, EOL since 2026-04-30, while Stylelint 18 needs Node >= 22.22. It is 55 lines of code-execution surface: the user's config runs at lint time, undocumented, with a possible 5 s stall per file.
findings.evidence: scratchpad/twesm probe: 'require(esm) .mjs OK: {"theme":{"spacing":{"1":"4px","2":"8px"}...}}', 'require(esm) .js type=module OK'; `grep -rn 'DynamicImport' test` empty; src/core/token-map.js:291-345; package.json engines node >=20.19.0.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: An untested code-execution path in a linter that runs inside editors is what a security-minded design-system team greps for before adopting; keeping it buys nothing on any supported Node.
findings.proposal: Delete loadTailwindSpacingFromDynamicImport and the child_process import when the Node floor moves to 22.12 (4.0; Stylelint 18 forces >= 22.22). Until then add one test with an ESM fixture config so the fallback is executed on the Node 20 CI rows. Add one sentence to docs/rules/prefer-token.md and SECURITY.md stating that tailwindConfigPath executes the config file. Half a day.
findings.correction: The fallback is not reachable only on Node 20: require(esm) is on by default from Node 20.19.0, the engines floor, so on every supported Node the child process runs only for a Tailwind config that uses top-level await (or on Node below 20.19, outside engines). The spawn result is cached per config path, so at most one 5 s stall per process, never per file. Untested and undocumented hold; the loader can be deleted now rather than at 4.0, at the cost of top-level-await configs.
findings.truth_reason: token-map.js:291-345 spawns node -e with timeout 5000; it is the only spawnSync in src and no test references it. require() of tailwind.config.mjs and a type:module .js config succeeded on Node 22.22.3 and on Node 20.19.2, the engines floor; only a top-level-await config failed (ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE); Node 20.16.0, below the floor, failed with ERR_REQUIRE_ESM. tailwindSpacingCache (token-map.js:250,350-356) memoises per path, null included. stylelint@18.0.0 engines ^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0.0. Neither prefer-token.md nor SECURITY.md mentions execution.
findings.materiality_reason: Probed on Node 22.22: an .mjs config loads through require with no spawn, so the fallback is dead for ESM, yet a throwing config did spawn the child (one spawnSync logged); it is an untested error path, not dead code. No persona sees a difference; the SECURITY.md sentence is the only trust item.
findings.relates_to: quality-engineering map gap; ecosystem-signals (Stylelint 18, Node 20 EOL); 4.0 scope in docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md

findings.title: doctor keeps module-level state, exits the process, scrapes config by regex
findings.claim: cli/doctor.js captures cwd at require time (line 23) and counts issues and warnings in module scope (24, 42); checks write straight to process.stdout and run() ends in process.exit (469). It cannot run twice, with another cwd, or from quickstart, whose last line tells the user to run it as a separate command; it is testable only by spawning and is the least-covered file (71.4% lines). The config checks are regex scrapes of the config text (checkTokenPattern 182-208, checkTailwindConfig 209-235, checkCustomSyntax 236-262), and types/cli.d.ts exposes only HELP and main.
findings.evidence: src/cli/doctor.js:23-24,42,431-470 (`const cwd = process.cwd(); let issues = 0; ... process.exit(stylelintOk && issues === 0 ? 0 : 1)`); types/cli.d.ts (9 lines); coverage figure from the quality-engineering map.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: An agent repairing a setup wants doctor() as a function to call after each edit, and quickstart wants to run the checks before printing a config. A process-global checker with no return value blocks both and keeps the setup path the least-tested code in the package.
findings.proposal: runDoctor({ cwd, write }) -> { ok, issues, warnings, checks: [{ name, status, message, fix }] } with no module state; cli/doctor.js becomes a 20-line wrapper that prints and sets process.exitCode. Load the config through stylelint.resolveConfig instead of regex scrapes (it already knows the cosmiconfig order). Export runDoctor from stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard/cli and type it; quickstart calls it before printing the config. Unit tests replace most of the spawn tests. Under a week.
findings.truth_reason: doctor.js:23 const cwd = process.cwd(), :24 let issues, :42 let warnings; every check calls process.stdout.write; run() ends in process.exit at :469 (and :439 for an unknown option). checkTokenPattern 182-207, checkTailwindConfig 210-234 and checkCustomSyntax 237-261 regex-scrape the config text. types/cli.d.ts is 9 lines exporting HELP and main. quickstart.js:145 lists 'npx rhythmguard doctor' as the last next command. coverage/lcov.info: LF 476, LH 340 (71.4%). test/cli/doctor-cli.test.js spawns the CLI. Both maps list this as untracked.
findings.materiality_reason: Structural only; no wrong doctor verdict is shown. Agents call the CLI fine, and quickstart running doctor checks is a mild first-run gain for solo-dev. The doctor gap that would move ds-team (it never resolves the scale the config implies, audit map) needs this refactor only as a prerequisite.
findings.relates_to: audit-and-cli map gap (doctor cannot say which scale); quality-engineering map gap (module-level state); no conflict with the freeze

findings.title: Report object has two shapes; renderers read the legacy one
findings.claim: buildReport (contract.js:227-358, 132 lines) builds a formatVersion-5 object with legacy top-level keys and their duplicates (scaleCleanliness and summary.scaleCleanliness, totalWarnings and summary.totalFindings, cssFilesScanned and scanned.cssFiles); toAuditContractReport (contract.js:410-520) projects it to JSON 2.0. Every renderer reads the legacy keys (render-github.js:18,21 filesWithIssues and scaleCleanliness; render-text and render-markdown totalWarnings, scanned, tokenContract), so both shapes must be maintained; baselineWritten and tokenSourceWarnings never reach v2, and --schema types findings.css as {type: array}.
findings.evidence: `grep -rnoE 'report\.(filesWithIssues|scaleCleanliness|totalWarnings|cssFilesScanned)' src/audit/render-*.js src/cli/*.js` → 9 reads across four renderers and quickstart; src/audit/contract.js:227-358, 410-520; types/audit.d.ts:264 (Record<string, unknown>).
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The 'stable JSON 2.0 contract' is what dashboards, the Action and agents key on. While it is a projection of an older shape, new fields land in one and not the other (tokenSourceWarnings already did). A contract that quietly lacks fields is not a contract.
findings.proposal: Make v2 the only in-memory report: buildReport returns the v2 object (summary, scanned, contracts, findings, baseline) plus a legacy() reverse projection used solely by --format json-v1; renderers take v2. Tighten --schema to the real finding shape and validate the fixture output against it in a test (ajv as a devDependency). Do it in 4.0, where json-v1 can be dropped; the renderer switch is mechanical and covered by the 145 CLI tests.
findings.correction: Renderers read the legacy keys 22 times across five renderers (text 6, markdown 5, html 3, github 3, badge 2) plus quickstart (3), not 9 reads across four renderers; toAuditContractReport spans contract.js:410-438 and 440-520 is the JSON schema. The two-shape claim and the two fields missing from v2 hold as stated.
findings.truth_reason: acorn: buildReport is contract.js:227-358 (132 lines), sets formatVersion 5 and carries cssFilesScanned/scanned.cssFiles, scaleCleanliness/summary.scaleCleanliness, totalWarnings/summary.totalFindings side by side. toAuditContractReport is 410-438 (440-520 is AUDIT_JSON_SCHEMA) and omits tokenSourceWarnings and baselineWritten; the CLI's v2 JSON has neither key. --schema: findings.css {type:'array'}; audit.d.ts:264 Record<string, unknown>. The cited grep returns 22 legacy-key reads across five renderers plus quickstart, not 9 across four.
findings.materiality_reason: Confirmed: --schema types findings.css as a bare array and tokenSourceWarnings never reaches the v2 projection. Agents and dashboards cannot validate the shape FOR_AGENTS calls stable, and cq-05's warnings channel is invisible until this lands. Mechanical in 4.0 where json-v1 can go; compounds with cq-07 and cq-02.
findings.relates_to: audit-and-cli map (loose schema, duplicated keys); #172; 4.0 scope; json-v1 removal is a documented break

findings.title: Stylelint 18 install is refused although the code already passes on it
findings.claim: Stylelint 18.0.0 shipped 2026-11-03 and stylelint-config-standard 41 peers on ^18, but the peer range is still ^16||^17 in package.json and in packages/rhythmguard's stylelint dependency. npm 10 refuses the install outright (ERESOLVE), not with a warning. The code needs no change: the full suite passes 664/667 on 18.0.0 and lint plus --fix work in a clean project. CI has no 18 row, the smoke scripts hardcode stylelint@16 (so 17 and 18 are never smoke-tested from the registry), README:147, CONTRIBUTING:125 and stylelint-next.yml:4 still say 18.0.0-next.0, and CONTRIBUTING:87 promises a 4.0 'the week Stylelint 18.0.0 is released', which is this week and cannot happen.
findings.evidence: Probe: `npm install --registry https://registry.npmjs.org stylelint@18 /tmp/rg-review-delivery-risk/stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard-3.17.0.tgz` -> `npm error code ERESOLVE ... peerOptional stylelint@"^16.0.0 || ^17.0.0" from stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard@3.17.0`. With --legacy-peer-deps: 10 findings on a.css, --fix wrote `.card { margin: 12px; padding: 8px 16px; }`. Repo copy with stylelint@18.0.0: `# tests 667 # pass 664 # fail 0 # skipped 3`. package.json peerDependencies; packages/rhythmguard/package.json dependencies.stylelint; .github/workflows/ci.yml:27-36; scripts/ci/smoke-checks.mjs:55 (`install(cwd, ['stylelint@16', ...])`); `npm view stylelint-config-standard@41 peerDependencies` -> `{ stylelint: '^18.0.0' }`; dependency dashboard #33 lists 'update dependency stylelint to v18' as rate-limited.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The first thing a solo-dev or a Renovate bot in a ds-team monorepo does this month is bump stylelint or stylelint-config-standard; the install then fails on Rhythmguard alone, and the cheapest fix for them is to remove the plugin. An agent hitting ERESOLVE in a fix loop reaches for --legacy-peer-deps or drops the rule. It also breaks the #168 'same week' promise, the first public test of the stable-ratchet thesis.
findings.proposal: Ship 3.18.0 this week: peer `^16.0.0 || ^17.0.0 || ^18.0.0` in package.json and in packages/rhythmguard (architecture.test.js:162 already forces the pair to match); add rows 22.x/24.x/26.x x '18' to ci.yml and release.yml; make smoke-checks.mjs install the newest supported major in a second pass instead of only stylelint@16; update README:147, CONTRIBUTING:87/125 and the stylelint-next.yml comment; close #168. Leave engines alone (Stylelint 18's own engines gate Node) and decouple 4.0's date from 'the week 18 ships' to 'by 2027-02-28'.
findings.truth_reason: Reproduced: npm 10.9.8 gives ERESOLVE installing stylelint@18 with the 3.17.0 tarball; with --legacy-peer-deps lint reports and --fix writes 12px/8px 16px; a repo copy on 18.0.0 passes 664/667, 0 fail. Peer ^16||^17 in both manifests, ci.yml:27-36 has no 18 row, smoke-checks.mjs:55 pins stylelint@16, README:147, CONTRIBUTING:87/125 and stylelint-next.yml:4 are stale, config-standard@41 peers ^18, #168 open. Extra: stylelint@next now 404s, so the weekly job breaks. ROADMAP:28 already carries the 2027-02-28 fallback; only CONTRIBUTING:87 lacks it.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: npm 10.9.8 throws ERESOLVE installing stylelint@18 beside 3.17.0 (an optional peer is still enforced). Every Renovate bump of stylelint or stylelint-config-standard 41 now fails at install, the earliest bounce for all three personas, while Stylelint 18 core ships a token-requiring rule that needs no plugin. Code already passes; compat work is exempt from the freeze. Fold dr-05 in.
findings.relates_to: #168 (open, promised the widening the week 18.0.0 ships); #172 (4.0 scope lists peer ^17||^18); CONTRIBUTING:94 counts compatibility work as always welcome, so no conflict with the freeze

findings.title: One Mac mini serializes every PR, merge and release; hosted runners are free and proven
findings.claim: A single self-hosted runner is online. Each job takes 2-3 minutes but ten jobs run one after another, so a CI run takes 33-71 minutes and the release verify 30-68. Seven of the last fifteen CI runs were cancelled by the concurrency rules, the quiet benchmark holds the same runner for 6-20 minutes after every merge, and when the farm is down a release waits 24 hours unless the maintainer flips RELEASE_ON_HOSTED by hand (3.7.0 was cancelled that way). Meanwhile GitHub-hosted jobs in this public repository ran and passed ten times in the last week (fork-verify 47 s, publish x4, cancel-closed-pr-runs x5): standard hosted runners are not metered on public repositories.
findings.evidence: `gh api repos/PetriLahdelma/stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard/actions/runners` -> one runner, `stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard-macmini-2544-w0i393 online Linux`. Run 41926076660 (main, 2026-11-04): ten jobs of 2-3 min each, started serially 22:32 to 23:08. `gh run list --workflow ci.yml`: walls 71, 50, 38, 48, 50, 33 min on 2026-11-04/05; 7 cancelled of the last 15. release.yml:15-19 manual fallback; docs/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md:66-75. Hosted successes: run 41054129926 fork-verify success (2026-10-30T19:04:44 to 19:05:31); publish job of v3.17.0 on 'GitHub Actions 1000082298' in 10 min; cancel-closed-pr-runs success x5 on 2026-11-04.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: Every fix for the other findings, including dr-01, queues behind a machine in the maintainer's home; an outside contributor sees a 70-minute check, and a release during a farm outage needs a manual variable flip only the maintainer knows about. Trust in a CI gate product starts with the product's own gate being fast and always available.
findings.proposal: Three YAML edits, no new infrastructure: (1) turn ci.yml's fork-verify into a 'fast gate' for every PR by changing line 140 to `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` (ubuntu-latest, Node 22, lockfile Stylelint, lint+typecheck+test, about 2 min) and treat it as the check to wait for; (2) invert release.yml:19 so the verify matrix runs on ubuntu-latest by default and the farm is the opt-in (`vars.RELEASE_ON_FARM`), turning a 30-68 min release into about 10 and deleting checklist section 7 from the critical path; (3) keep the farm for the post-merge matrix and the quiet benchmark. Keep the fork gating as is.
findings.truth_reason: gh api runners: one online (macmini, Linux ARM64). Run 41926076660: ten 2-3 min jobs started one at a time 22:32 to 23:08. ci.yml walls 71/50/39/49/50/33 min, 8 of the last 15 cancelled. Release verify 30-69 min; quiet benchmark 7-21 min per merge. Hosted successes verified: fork-verify job 47 s on 2026-10-30, four publish jobs (3.17.0: 10 min), cancel-closed-pr-runs x8. PR #141 confirms the whole 3.7.0 verify matrix passed on ubuntu-latest and moved back 'as before', not for quota. ci.yml:140 and release.yml:19 are the right lines.
findings.materiality_reason: No persona sees runner topology, and fork PRs already get a two-minute hosted job. The value is compounding: every fix here, dr-01 first, waits 33-71 minutes on one Mac mini (7 of the last 15 runs cancelled), and a farm outage stalls releases. Hosted jobs passed ten times this week; the edits restore what the 3.7.0 changelog promised.
findings.relates_to: Conflicts with the maintainer's recorded belief that hosted Actions are quota-dead (user CLAUDE.md; #174: 'Actions quota is not available for a standing job'); the evidence here is ten successful ubuntu-latest jobs in this public repo in the last week. Touches docs/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md section 7, #164 (matrix size), quality map gap 'one self-hosted runner online'

findings.title: Bus factor one with no second key and no away-runbook
findings.claim: One GitHub admin, one npm maintainer on all three packages, no branch protection or rulesets, zero watchers, CODEOWNERS with one name, and a farm that needs the maintainer's own machines up (Colima after a reboot). If the maintainer is away for a month: dr-01 stays unfixed, nobody can merge or publish, SECURITY.md's 72-hour acknowledgment is missed, Renovate PRs pile up two a day, and no human other than the maintainer even receives issue notifications. Nothing in the repository says who to contact or what to do.
findings.evidence: `gh api repos/.../collaborators` -> `PetriLahdelma admin` only; `npm view <pkg> maintainers` -> `petritapanilahdelma` for all three packages; `gh api .../branches/main/protection` -> 404 'Branch not protected'; `gh api .../rulesets` -> []; repo subscribers_count 0; .github/CODEOWNERS:2; SECURITY.md:29-30 (72 h / 7 d targets); release.yml:15-19 (manual RELEASE_ON_HOSTED); maintainer memory 'CI farm needs Colima after reboot'.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: A design-system lead approving a blocking CI gate asks 'what happens if the maintainer disappears'; today the honest answer is 'nothing ships and nothing is answered'. A single unlucky month would also leave dr-01 blocking every Stylelint 18 upgrade with no one able to cut the one-line fix.
findings.proposal: Half a day: (1) invite one trusted person as a GitHub collaborator with write access; because publishing is OIDC bound to repo plus workflow, creating a GitHub release is enough for them to ship a fix with no npm secret shared; (2) add that person as a second npm maintainer so a broken version can be deprecated; (3) write docs/MAINTAINER_AWAY.md: who can cut a release, how RELEASE_ON_HOSTED works, where the runner lives and how to restart it, what to do with Renovate, and the security contact fallback; (4) add a ruleset requiring the dr-02 fast gate on main with admin bypass kept; (5) say in README's support section that the project has one maintainer and what the response times are.
findings.truth_reason: Verified live: collaborators = PetriLahdelma admin only; npm maintainers petritapanilahdelma on all three packages; branch protection 404; rulesets []; subscribers_count 0; CODEOWNERS:2 one owner; SECURITY.md:29-30 72 h/7 d targets; release.yml:15-19 manual RELEASE_ON_HOSTED. No MAINTAINER_AWAY, governance or single-maintainer text in README's support section or docs/. Only ROADMAP:129 plans 'invite a second maintainer' for 2027 Q1, which relates_to should cite; nothing of it is done.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: one admin collaborator, no rulesets, no branch protection, zero watchers. A ds-team lead approving a blocking gate asks, but rival Stylelint plugins are equally solo-maintained, so it is rarely decisive; Stylelint core's new rule needs no such answer. The runbook and an honest README line are an hour; the second maintainer depends on a person existing. Compounds with dr-01.
findings.relates_to: Quality map gap 'bus factor one'; SECURITY.md response targets; COUNCIL:65 buyer 'pays in trust'

findings.title: Releases are hand-edited in four files and shipped in bursts
findings.claim: A release means `npm version` in three manifests, editing two ^ranges by hand, renaming the CHANGELOG heading and writing notes, with only a contract test as the net. The record shows the cost: four releases in eight hours on 2026-10-14/15 (3.9.0, 3.10.0, 3.10.1, 3.10.2), three in three hours on 2026-10-18, 3.16.0 shipped with a broken CLI and 3.16.1 followed 4 h 37 min later, and 7 of the last 12 release runs failed (2026-10-15 to 10-23). The council's own stop list forbids more than one release a day. release.yml's verify also skips the typecheck that ci.yml runs, and the release PR's CI run is cancelled on merge, so the tag's gate is the one without types.
findings.evidence: docs/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md:13-22; `npm view stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard time`: 3.9.0 2026-10-14T22:36, 3.10.0 22:52, 3.10.1 23:15, 3.10.2 2026-10-15T06:50; 3.11.0 09:22, 3.12.0 10:14, 3.13.0 12:24 on 2026-10-18; 3.16.0 2026-11-01T17:01, 3.16.1 21:38; `gh run list --workflow release.yml --limit 12`: 7 failure, 5 success. `grep -n typecheck .github/workflows/release.yml` -> nothing; ci.yml:71-72 has the step; cancel-closed-pr-runs.yml cancelled the 'release: v3.17.0' PR run at 2026-11-04T16:10:34. docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:98 ('more than one release a day' on the stop list).
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: A team that pins a version and reads the changelog sees seven versions in four days and a same-day broken-then-fixed pair; that reads as churn, the opposite of the 'stable ratchet' the plan sells, and Renovate noise in their monorepo multiplies with every release.
findings.proposal: One day: add scripts/release/prepare.mjs <version> that bumps the three manifests and both ^ranges, moves [Unreleased] under a dated heading, writes notes.md from that section, runs the five-command local gate, and refuses when a tag was created in the last 24 hours (the stop-list rule becomes executable). Add `npm run typecheck` to release.yml's verify. Record in RELEASE_CHECKLIST that patch releases batch for a day unless a published version is broken.
findings.correction: The tagged commit is typechecked by ci.yml's push-to-main run (3.17.0: run 41864724904, success, 16:10 to 16:59) and by the local gate in RELEASE_CHECKLIST section 3. What holds is narrower: release.yml's verify, the only job that blocks publish, has no typecheck step, so a type failure cannot stop a publish. Everything else in the claim and evidence holds.
findings.truth_reason: Checklist:13-22 (three npm version runs, two hand-edited ranges, CHANGELOG rename), npm publish times (four releases in 8 h 14 min on 10-14/15, three in 3 h on 10-18, 3.16.1 4 h 37 min after 3.16.0), exactly 7 failures in the last 12 release runs, COUNCIL:98 stop-list entry and no typecheck step in release.yml all verified. But the cancelled release-PR run is not the only type gate: ci.yml's push-to-main run typechecked the tagged 3.17.0 merge commit and passed (run 41864724904).
findings.materiality_reason: Tags confirm the bursts (four releases in eight hours on 10-15, 3.16.0 broken and 3.16.1 4h38m later) and release.yml's verify really has no typecheck step. Churn and Renovate noise are what the ds-team persona avoids, and the stop list already forbids more than one release a day; a prepare script makes it executable. Not a bounce by itself.
findings.relates_to: COUNCIL:98 (one release a day), #172 (the 4.0 cut touches all four files), docs/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md, quality map gap 'release mechanics are manual'

findings.title: SECURITY.md does not say what the package does on your machine
findings.claim: The buyer the plan names pays in trust, and #174 says the first procurement question is 'does it phone home'. SECURITY.md only covers reporting. It does not state that the package makes no network requests and collects no telemetry (true: src has zero network code), that `scale: "auto"` with a Tailwind config requires or spawns node to import the project's tailwind.config.js, that the audit runs `git` for --since/--staged, that --fix writes files, or how to verify the provenance it already ships. The CI result collector (report-ci.sh) is also undocumented, so a reader who finds it assumes telemetry.
findings.evidence: SECURITY.md:1-31 (no 'network' or 'telemetry' text); `grep -rn "fetch(\|node:http\|require('https\|telemetry" src` -> no matches; src/core/token-map.js:324 `spawnSync(process.execPath, ['-e', script, resolvedPath])`; src/audit/scan/files.js:347,361 `execFileSync('git', ...)`; .github/scripts/report-ci.sh posts job results to CI_COLLECTOR_URL in CI only; #174 body: 'state in SECURITY.md that the package makes no network requests and collects no telemetry ... the first question procurement asks'; docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:65.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: A platform team cannot put a linter in a blocking CI gate without a written answer on network, telemetry and code execution; today they have to read the source. Agent platforms (Claude Code hooks, Cursor rules) likewise prefer tools with a declared no-network contract.
findings.proposal: Half a day: add a 'What this package does on your machine' section to SECURITY.md: no network requests, no telemetry; writes only the files --fix or `fix` targets; executes your tailwind.config.js only when `tailwindConfigPath` or Tailwind inference is configured (in-process require or a 5-second child process); runs `git` only for --since/--staged; provenance verifiable with `npm audit signatures`; 2.x security fixes come from the release/v2.x branches until 2027-03-01; CI telemetry is the project's own and never ships. Add a contract test that fails if src ever imports a network module, so the statement stays true.
findings.correction: SECURITY.md and the main README lack any no-network or no-telemetry statement, but packages/rhythmguard/README.md:50 already states 'Makes no network requests' for the CLI package. The project's tailwind.config.* is executed (in-process require, then a 5 s child process) only when `tailwindConfigPath` is configured by hand or by `rhythmguard init`; `scale: "auto"` with a Tailwind config present but no option set never loads it. report-ci.sh ships in the repository only, not in the npm package.
findings.truth_reason: SECURITY.md:1-31 has no network, telemetry, --fix, git or code-execution text; src has no network module; token-map.js:278-345 require()s then spawnSync()s the Tailwind config; files.js:347/361 run git; #174 asks for the statement. Three corrections: packages/rhythmguard/README.md:50 already says 'Makes no network requests' (CLI package only, no telemetry wording anywhere); the Tailwind config executes only when tailwindConfigPath is set (scale-inference.js:513, token-map.js:436), never from scale:'auto' alone; report-ci.sh is not in the tarball (package.json files excludes .github).
findings.materiality_reason: SECURITY.md has no network, telemetry or code-execution statement and src imports no network module, so the statement is true and cheap. It answers the plan's own buyer ('pays in trust, no telemetry', #174) at the late approval stage for ds-team and agent platforms; most solo-devs never read it. A contract test keeps it true. Half a day.
findings.relates_to: #174 (enterprise basics, open); strategy map gap 'no-network or no-telemetry statement absent'; quality map gap on the untested child-process loader (token-map.js:291-345)

findings.title: Node 20 EOL is still carried in engines, CI rows and two workflows
findings.claim: Node 20 reached end of life on 2026-04-30. All three manifests still declare >=20.19.0, three of eight matrix rows run Node 20 (and the coverage and pack-smoke reference row is one of them), and two workflows pin Node 20 outright, so after dr-01 the post-publish smoke cannot even run Stylelint 18. The planned 4.0 floor, Node 22.22, is itself in maintenance and ends 2027-04-30, two months after the latest 4.0 date, so 4.0 would ship on a floor that expires almost immediately.
findings.evidence: package.json:201, packages/rhythmguard/package.json:32, packages/eslint-plugin-rhythmguard/package.json:42 (`"node": ">=20.19.0"`); .github/workflows/ci.yml:27 ('20.x'), :83 and :87 (reference row gated on node 20.x); post-publish-smoke.yml:32 (`node-version: '20'`); community-scales.yml:28 (`node-version: 20`); README.md:147 ('Node 20 itself is end of life'); nodejs/Release schedule.json: v20 end 2026-04-30, v22 end 2027-04-30; `npm view stylelint@18 engines` -> `^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0.0`.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: A 'small, stable tool teams put in CI' that tests an EOL runtime in three of eight rows spends a quarter of its only runner on nobody, and a 4.0 whose floor expires in two months forces a 5.0 engines change within the year, which is exactly the churn the ds-team persona avoids.
findings.proposal: Now, no semver impact: move post-publish-smoke.yml and community-scales.yml to Node 22; move the coverage and pack-smoke reference row to 22.x x 17; keep one Node 20 row (20.x x 16.0.0) as the floor proof and drop the other two, cutting farm time by about a quarter. At 4.0: engines `^22.22.0 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0.0` mirroring Stylelint 18 so no impossible Node/Stylelint pair exists, and write the 2027-04-30 end of Node 22 into MIGRATING_TO_4.md as a minor-release engines bump, not a major.
findings.correction: The pre-4.0 proposal (move two workflows and the coverage/pack-smoke reference row to Node 22, keep one 20.x floor row) is new. The 4.0 engines `^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0 || >=26` mirroring Stylelint 18 is already written at ROADMAP:28 and COUNCIL:76, so the only 4.0-side addition is recording Node 22's 2027-04-30 end in MIGRATING_TO_4.md as a minor-release bump.
findings.truth_reason: Verified: engines >=20.19.0 at package.json:201, packages/rhythmguard:32, packages/eslint-plugin:42; ci.yml:27 gives 3 of 8 rows to Node 20 with the reference row gated on 20.x at :83/:87; post-publish-smoke.yml:32 and community-scales.yml:28 pin Node 20; README:147; Node schedule v20 end 2026-04-30, v22 end 2027-04-30; stylelint@18 engines ^22.22.2. But the 4.0 engines item is already the plan of record: ROADMAP:28 and COUNCIL:75-76 set 4.0 to Stylelint 18's floor, drop Node 20, no later than 2027-02-28.
findings.materiality_reason: Confirmed: three Node 20 matrix rows, the reference row among them, and two workflows pinned to 20. No persona bounces over an EOL floor being supported; the material parts are internal: farm time (dr-02) and the smoke workflow that cannot run Stylelint 18 after dr-01. The 4.0 engines wording is a sentence in MIGRATING_TO_4. Fold into dr-01's PR.
findings.relates_to: #172 (4.0 Node floor), #164 (matrix size), ecosystem map gap 'Node 20 reached end-of-life'
