findings.claim: 2,016 of last week's 3,389 downloads (59.5%) are version 3.6.0, locked by doctor-school/ds-platform's pnpm lockfile at stylelint 17.15.0; their package.json already declares Node ^22.22.2 and they also install oxlint-tailwindcss. The one outreach issue to them has zero comments. Every download-based checkpoint (ROADMAP 2027-03-31, the ESLint demand test) moves if that team upgrades, forks or leaves. Nothing tests what 3.6.0 to 3.17.0 does to such a user: the #172 comment records that the 3.7.0 message rewording turned 645 baseline warnings into resolved-plus-new pairs for a baseline keyed on message text.
findings.evidence: https://api.npmjs.org/versions/stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard/last-week: 3.6.0 2016 (59.5%), 3.17.0 179 (5.3%), total 3389. `gh api repos/doctor-school/ds-platform/contents/package.json`: `stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard ^3.6.0`, `stylelint ^17.15.0`, `oxlint-tailwindcss ^1.11.0`, engines `^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0.0`; pnpm-lock.yaml line 7697 `stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard@3.6.0`. doctor-school/ds-platform#3591 open, 0 comments (2026-11-05). #172 comment 2026-10-14 (645 'new' warnings after the 3.7.0 rewording). docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:17 ('consistent, not proven').
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The reference user for the whole thesis has taken none of eleven minor releases; if their first upgrade churns their baselines the plan's one real design-system team walks, and the download line that justifies continuing drops by sixty percent in a week with no product change.
findings.proposal: (1) Report an 'aged downloads excluding the single largest pinned version' figure for the main package next to raw downloads in ROADMAP and the council indicators, so one lockfile cannot move a checkpoint. (2) Add docs/UPGRADING.md with a 'from 3.6.0' section: the 3.7.0 prefer-token message change, the 3.15.0 default noise paths, and a baseline re-key recipe keyed on file, rule and value. (3) Add test/compat/upgrade-oldest-in-range.test.js: install 3.6.0 from npm into a temp project, run both versions on the pack-smoke fixture, diff findings keyed on file/rule/value, and fail on any difference not listed in UPGRADING.md. Two to three days.
findings.truth_reason: api.npmjs.org today: 3.6.0 = 2,016 of 3,389 (59.5%), 3.17.0 179. doctor-school package.json: rhythmguard ^3.6.0, stylelint ^17.15.0, oxlint-tailwindcss ^1.11.0, engines ^22.22.2||^24.15.0||>=26. #3591 open, 0 comments. #172 comment 2026-10-14 records 645 resolved-plus-new pairs from the 3.7.0 rewording (on the maintainer's own site). COUNCIL:17 'consistent, not proven'. test/compat holds only floor-compat.test.js; no UPGRADING.md; ROADMAP:159 checkpoint is download-based. Nuance: doctor-school runs the rules, not the audit, so the 3.7.0 tailwind-class message change matters to them, the 3.15.0 audit paths do not.

The metric correction is planning hygiene, not persona-facing. UPGRADING.md helps a pinned ds-team a little; the M-effort compat test guards one known user.
findings.relates_to: #172 (structured findings so messages leave the contract), COUNCIL:17 and docs/ESLINT_PLAN.md:66 (the 73% attribution), strategy map gap 'download signal rests on one unreplied pin'; the no-re-contact rule (memory) means the test, not a message, is the mitigation

findings.title: No Windows run while a hosted Windows job would cost nothing
findings.claim: All runners are Linux ARM64 and neither workflow has an OS matrix, so path normalisation in fourteen places (formatPath's backslash replace, git-scoped scans, sparse checkouts, baseline keys) has never executed on Windows. #174 lists Windows as an enterprise basic and the maintainer's own note says a hosted run is unaffordable, but GitHub-hosted jobs in this repository ran and passed ten times last week and public repositories are not metered.
findings.evidence: `gh api .../actions/runners` labels: self-hosted,Linux,ARM64,macmini; ci.yml and release.yml have no `os:` axis; src/core/token-sources.js:1417 (backslash replace); #174 body item 2 ('Run the suite on Windows ... a hosted runner once, since Actions quota is not available'); hosted job successes listed in dr-02; audit map gap 'paths are normalised in 14 places but nothing exercises them'.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: Design-system teams in large organisations have Windows developers and Windows CI agents; the first `rhythmguard audit` that reports wrong paths or a baseline that never matches on Windows ends the evaluation, and nobody on the project would see it coming.
findings.proposal: Add a `windows-latest` job to ci.yml on push to main only (Node 22, npm ci, lint, npm test), `continue-on-error: true` for the first month while path bugs are fixed, then required; then add Windows to README's compatibility line. One hour of YAML plus whatever the first run reveals.
findings.truth_reason: Runner labels self-hosted,Linux,ARM64,macmini; ci.yml and release.yml have no os axis; token-sources.js:1417 backslash replace; #174 item 2 reads 'a hosted runner once, since Actions quota is not available for a standing job'. Hosted ubuntu-latest jobs passed ten-plus times this week (dr-02), the same free standard-runner class as windows-latest on a public repo. 'Fourteen places' is approximate: five backslash replaces plus toPosix/path.sep helpers in files.js, baseline.js, quickstart.js, shared.js, non-authored.js; none exercised on Windows.
findings.materiality_reason: Confirmed: no OS matrix anywhere and five backslash-normalising sites in src never ran on Windows. Baseline keys and git-scoped scans failing silently at first use would end a ds-team evaluation in a Windows-heavy enterprise, and #174 already calls Windows a basic. One hour of hosted YAML, free on a public repo; the larger rivals test Windows in CI.
findings.relates_to: #174 (Windows item); same hosted-runner belief conflict as dr-02; quality map gap 'No Windows or macOS CI rows'

findings.title: Renovate cannot write the benchmark lockfile, so the maintainer does
findings.claim: Hosted Renovate refuses to fetch the @tailwindcss/oxide wasm tarball (EALLOWREMOTE) when it updates benchmarks/tailwind-compare/package.json, so every such PR arrives with a stale package-lock.json and a 'you probably do not want to merge this PR as-is' warning. Three PRs this week (#357, #362, #364) each needed the maintainer to merge main, regenerate the lock and rerun the comparison by hand. The manifest itself says its pins are meant to be bumped deliberately, yet Renovate bumps them on its own schedule. No renovate.json exists in the repo, so the policy cannot be fixed in a PR.
findings.evidence: PR #364 comment by agentic-renovate 2026-11-04T02:33: 'Artifact update problem ... File name: benchmarks/tailwind-compare/package-lock.json ... npm error code EALLOWREMOTE ... Refusing to fetch https://registry.npmjs.org/@tailwindcss/oxide-'; maintainer comment 2026-11-04T22:17: 'pushed the lockfile Renovate could not write (EALLOWREMOTE on the oxide wasm tarball) and reran node scripts/bench/tailwind-compare.mjs'; same on #362 and #357. benchmarks/tailwind-compare/package.json description: 'Pinned tools ... Bump a version deliberately and rerun.' `ls renovate.json .renovaterc* .github/renovate.json` -> none. Dependency dashboard #33: 'WARN: Cannot access vulnerability alerts'.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: Each occurrence costs the maintainer an hour and a 50-70 minute farm run; the competitor comparison that the ESLint positioning rests on silently changes its pins whenever a bot decides, which undermines 'rerun 2026-11-04 on ESLint 10.14.0' style claims.
findings.proposal: Two hours: commit renovate.json with `extends: ["config:recommended", "helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests"]` and `packageRules: [{ matchFileNames: ["benchmarks/**"], enabled: false }]`, so the comparison's pins change only when the maintainer reruns the script (what its manifest already says); grant the Renovate app the vulnerability-alerts permission the dashboard warns about; keep the root lockfile under Renovate as today.
findings.truth_reason: Renovate comments on #357, #362 and #364 all read 'File name: benchmarks/tailwind-compare/package-lock.json ... EALLOWREMOTE ... Refusing to fetch .../@tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi-4.3.3.tgz'; maintainer comments on all three say the lock was pushed by hand and tailwind-compare.mjs rerun (#364 also 'Merged main'). The manifest description says 'Bump a version deliberately and rerun.' No renovate.json in the tree or in git history. #33 shows 'WARN: Cannot access vulnerability alerts'. Those Renovate PR CI runs took 33-71 min on the farm.
findings.materiality_reason: Confirmed: #357, #362 and #364 each rewrote benchmarks/tailwind-compare's lockfile and RESULTS.md by hand, and no renovate.json exists. No persona sees this; it buys back a few maintainer hours a week and keeps the comparison's pins deliberate, a minor credibility point. Same renovate.json edit as dr-08, so do them together.
findings.relates_to: #33 (dependency dashboard), quality map gap 'Renovate configuration lives outside the repository', benchmarks/tailwind-compare/RESULTS.md

findings.title: Actions pinned to mutable tags run on the maintainer's own hardware
findings.claim: All 22 `uses:` lines pin actions/checkout and actions/setup-node to the moving tag @v7, the publish job installs an unpinned npm@latest at publish time, and most workflows have no top-level permissions block (safe today only because the repository default is read). Same-repo PRs, including those opened by the Renovate app, run `npm ci` and the test suite on the maintainer's Mac mini with persisted checkout credentials. A compromised action tag or npm release would execute on that machine with the repository token.
findings.evidence: `grep -rhn "uses:" .github/workflows/*.yml` -> 22 lines, all `@v7`; release.yml:100-103 (`npm install -g npm@latest`); `grep -n permissions: .github/workflows/*.yml` -> only cancel-closed-pr-runs.yml and release.yml's publish job; `gh api .../actions/permissions/workflow` -> default_workflow_permissions read; ci.yml:22-23 (same-repo PRs on self-hosted); PRs #368/#369 by app/agentic-renovate run on the farm.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: A design-system team's security review reads the workflows; tag pins plus self-hosted runners is the pattern their own policies forbid, and it is the one supply-chain gap that the otherwise strong provenance story leaves open.
findings.proposal: One hour: pin every action by commit digest (the renovate.json preset in dr-06 keeps them updated), pin npm to an exact version in the publish job, add `permissions: contents: read` at the top of every workflow, and set `persist-credentials: false` on checkouts in farm jobs. Mention the pinning in SECURITY.md's new section (dr-07).
findings.truth_reason: grep: 22 uses: lines, every one actions/checkout@v7 or actions/setup-node@v7; release.yml:100-103 runs npm install -g npm@latest; permissions: appears only in cancel-closed-pr-runs.yml:13 and release.yml:86 (publish job); default_workflow_permissions is read; no persist-credentials override anywhere; ci.yml:22-23 runs same-repo PRs on the farm, and #368/#369 by app/agentic-renovate ran there (runs 41956004396, 41955986474). The quality map lists tag pins as a gap tracked only by #33; nothing in the repo pins digests.
findings.materiality_reason: Confirmed: 22 tag pins, npm@latest in the publish job with id-token: write, permissions on only two jobs, no persist-credentials: false. A compromised tag could publish, which is the one gap in an otherwise strong provenance story, though the exposure is shared by most of npm. Scorecard-style reviews notice it, rarely decisively. One hour; cite in dr-07.
findings.relates_to: Quality map gap 'actions are tag-pinned'; dr-06 and dr-07

findings.title: Tailwind first run fails at the quickstart's own next step
findings.claim: The quickstart knows the stack but never prints an install line. On a Tailwind v4 project it prints a config extending `configs/tailwind`, an ESLint snippet importing `stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard/eslint` at `warn`, and `Next: npx stylelint "**/*.css"`. Following that plus the README's install line, Stylelint exits 78 with `Could not find "stylelint-config-tailwindcss"` (an optional peer since 3.0), while `rhythmguard doctor` says `All checks passed`. README.md:44-50 has the same omission, and README.md:57-62 installs a different package (`eslint-plugin-rhythmguard`, at `error`). On a Sass-only project the registry `rhythmguard` wrapper brings no postcss-scss, so the first run reports `CSS files 0`, `Skipped 2 (SCSS without postcss-scss)` and `Cleanliness 100%` over three off-scale values.
findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/rg-review-docs-and-site/tw (Tailwind v4, src/app.css with @theme): `node <worktree>/src/cli/index.js` printed the tailwind config, `import rhythmguard from 'stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard/eslint'` at 'warn' and `npx stylelint "**/*.css"` with no install line (src/cli/quickstart.js:115-123, 138-146, 258-262; `grep -n 'npm install' src/cli/quickstart.js src/cli/init.js` = none). After `npm install --save-dev stylelint stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard --registry https://registry.npmjs.org` (3.17.0, stylelint 17.16.0) and pasting the config: `npx stylelint "**/*.css"` -> `ConfigurationError: Could not find "stylelint-config-tailwindcss". Do you need to install the package or use the "configBasedir" option?`, exit=78; `npx rhythmguard doctor` -> `All checks passed.`, exit=0; after installing stylelint-config-tailwindcss, 5 findings, exit 2. src/configs/tailwind.js:5-6 extends it; package.json peerDependenciesMeta marks it optional. README.md:44-50, :57, :62. SCSS probe /tmp/rg-review-docs-and-site/scss with registry `rhythmguard` (118 packages, no node_modules/postcss-scss): quickstart printed `CSS files 0`, `Skipped 2 not audited (2 SCSS without postcss-scss)`, `Off-scale 0`, `Cleanliness 100%`; packages/rhythmguard/package.json dependencies = stylelint and the plugin only; README.md:16 'It reads CSS and SCSS'.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The first ten minutes are the whole pitch ('no install, no config'). The largest persona by market, Tailwind, gets a configuration error as its first result; the Sass teams the Bootstrap GIF is aimed at get a clean bill of health on dirty code. Both read as the tool being broken rather than misconfigured, and an agent following the same printed output loops on the error.
findings.proposal: Make the quickstart print, above 'Paste this', one install line built from what it detected: `npm install --save-dev stylelint stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard`, plus `stylelint-config-tailwindcss` on Tailwind, `postcss-scss` when it skipped SCSS, and `eslint eslint-plugin-rhythmguard` when it prints the ESLint snippet; have that snippet import `eslint-plugin-rhythmguard` at the README's severity. findings.title: No page tells the solo developer how findings appear in the editor
findings.claim: Across the README, both package READMEs, the 14 user guides and the 6 rule pages there is no mention of VS Code, an editor extension, codeActionsOnSave or a language server (grep returns only the 'editorial' presets). The solo-dev persona wants editor feedback and trustworthy autofix on save; the Stylelint and ESLint extensions deliver both once configured, but `stylelint.validate` must list scss, vue and astro and `source.fixAll.stylelint` must be enabled, or SCSS and Vue files show nothing. eslint-plugin-better-tailwindcss, the 6.1M-download neighbour, has an 'Editor configuration' section with auto-fix on save for ESLint and Oxlint.

WebFetch github.com/schoero/eslint-plugin-better-tailwindcss README: 'Editor configuration' > 'VSCode' > 'Auto-fix on save' > 'ESLint' and 'Oxlint' (editor.codeActionsOnSave).
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: A developer judges a linter by the squiggle, not the CI log. Without the page, a solo developer who installs the plugin sees nothing in the editor for SCSS or Vue files, assumes the rules do not work, and uninstalls before the first commit.

findings.title: Re-base the @eslint/css trigger on agent surfaces, not download share
findings.claim: The stop list defers the @eslint/css port until @eslint/css reaches 25% of Stylelint's weekly downloads. Share went from 2.28% (Nov 2025) to 5.36% (Oct 2026): 64 months at the linear rate, 18 at the geometric one, so the gate trips in 2028 at the earliest. Share measures 'replace Stylelint', which is not the value. ESLint is where agent surfaces live: the ESLint CLI ships an MCP server that loads the project's config and plugins, Copilot code review runs ESLint (preview) and not Stylelint, and Stylelint's maintainers closed their MCP request by 'staying focused on ... humans'. The stalled variable tracking (#160) is no blocker: use-scale checks raw lengths and loads tokens itself.
findings.evidence: Monthly table from api.npmjs.org/downloads/range (probe /tmp/rg-review-ecosystem-bets/range-*.json): share 2.28% 2025-11, 3.32% 2026-05, 4.78% 2026-09, 5.36% 2026-10; slope 0.32 pts/month → 64 months; geometric 9.5%/month → 18 months. docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:98; docs/ESLINT_PLAN.md:72 ('around 2028'). https://eslint.org/docs/latest/use/mcp ('The ESLint CLI contains an MCP server', loads eslint.config.* and resolves modules from the project's node_modules). https://github.blog/changelog/2025-11-20-linter-integration-with-copilot-code-review-now-in-public-preview/ (ESLint listed, Stylelint absent). stylelint/stylelint#8676 closed 2026-03-11, jeddy3: 'staying focused on creating interfaces, codebases and documentation that work best for humans'. eslint/css#160 open, accepted, 18 comments. Rule shape for the port: raw.githubusercontent.com/eslint/css/main/src/rules/relative-font-units.js (`Declaration` visitor, node.property, node.value.children, loc).
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: A solo developer on Next.js or Vite has ESLint or Oxlint, never Stylelint; an agent in Cursor or VS Code reaches rules through ESLint's MCP. Without an ESLint-hosted CSS rule, Rhythmguard's CSS checks are invisible to both personas, and the share gate keeps it that way until 2028.
findings.proposal: Build `rhythmguard/use-scale` for @eslint/css inside the ESLint package: a `Declaration` visitor hands property and value text to src/core (length, value-nodes, scale-inference, token-sources), reports the same message text, fixes with `fixer.replaceText`. CSS only (`tolerant` plus tailwind-csstree for v4 `@theme`); SCSS stays on Stylelint. A contract test requires identical findings to the Stylelint rule on shared fixtures, as ROADMAP.md:119 already specifies. Replace the 25% trigger with two facts that already hold: ESLint-hosted agent surfaces exist, and no scaffold installs Stylelint. Flip back to defer only if ESLint's MCP server stops loading project plugins.
findings.truth_reason: Share recomputed from npm range data: 2.28% 2025-11, 3.32% 2026-05, 4.78% 2026-09, 5.36% 2026-10 (exact). Endpoint rates 0.28 pts/month (70 months) and 8.1%/month (20 months), slightly below the finding's; conclusion unchanged. eslint.org: 'The ESLint CLI contains an MCP server' (project-config loading implied, not quoted). Copilot changelog: ESLint, PMD, CodeQL; no Stylelint. stylelint#8676 closed 2026-03-11 with the jeddy3 quote; eslint/css#160 open, accepted, 18 comments; relative-font-units.js shape matches; COUNCIL:98, ESLINT_PLAN:72, ROADMAP:71,119 hold.
findings.materiality_reason: Conflicts with the stop list's 25% share gate, which trips in 2028 at the earliest. A Vite or Next solo-dev never has Stylelint; ESLint hosts the MCP and Copilot review surfaces the ai-assisted persona uses; @eslint/css has no scale rule, so the slot is open. Effort L, but no other path gets CSS checks to those personas.

findings.title: Settle the core-rule split with Stylelint in Q1 2027, not Q3
findings.claim: Stylelint 18 core ships `value-type-custom-property-required-list` and `declaration-property-custom-property-allowed-list` with `referenceFiles`. The kill criterion says deprecate use-scale 'if Stylelint core ships a nearest-scale-step rule', and the council plans to open that discussion upstream in Q3 2027. On the same CSS the core rules flag on-scale 16px and 1px hairlines, flag `calc(var(--space-4) + 1px)` wholesale, name no nearest step and fix nothing; use-scale names 12px/16px and fixes. The maintainer who would decide keeps scales in a plugin (stylelint-scales) and the new core rules are type-based by design. Asking in Q3 leaves 4.0 positioned against a guess and COMPARISON.md has no core row.

Use scale values (nearest: 12px or 16px)' and fixed 13px→12px, 0.8125rem→0.75rem. docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:89 (Q3 discussion), :113 (kill clause). https://github.com/jeddy3/stylelint-scales (6.0.0, 2026-11-04, no tokens, no nearest step). docs/COMPARISON.md:7-13.

Ship a `configs/stylelint-18` recipe: core `value-type-custom-property-required-list: ["length"]` for 'use a token', `use-scale` with `fixWith: "token"` for nearest and fix, and accept Stylelint's `referenceFiles` paths as `scaleSources` so token files are configured once. findings.title: Keep Stylelint 16 in 4.0; drop it on a share number
findings.claim: The council's 4.0 scope says peer `^17 || ^18`, drop Stylelint 16; issue #172 says 'Stylelint 16 and 17 stay supported'. Nobody has resolved the contradiction. Last week v16 was 29.25% of Stylelint downloads (4.11M of 14.06M), v17 46.1% ten months after release, v18 0.22%. The design-system teams the thesis targets sit on the slow side of that curve. Dropping 16 in a major sold as stable removes a third of the reachable base, and none of the listed 4.0 items (fixWith token default, one default scale, structured findings, Node 22 floor) is shown to need an API Stylelint 16 lacks; a 16.0.0 compat-floor test already exists.
findings.evidence: api.npmjs.org/versions/stylelint/last-week (2026-11-05): v17 6,481,807 (46.09%), v16 4,113,365 (29.25%), v18 30,358 (0.22%); registry: 17.0.0 published 2026-01-15. docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:78 ('peer ^17 || ^18; drop Stylelint 16 and Node 20') vs `gh issue view 172` body ('Stylelint 16 and 17 stay supported'). test/compat/floor-compat.test.js; CONTRIBUTING.md:122.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: A design-system lead on Stylelint 16 who sees 4.0 drop their major will not adopt a gate that forces a Stylelint upgrade across a monorepo; the kill criterion counts exactly those organisations.
findings.proposal: Write the rule into #172 and the council text: 4.0 keeps `^16 || ^17 || ^18` with the Node floor at 22.22 independent of the Stylelint major; if any 4.0 item needs an API that 16 lacks, name the API and the minimum 16.x in #172 instead of dropping the major. Drop 16 only in 5.0, and only when v16 is under 10% of weekly Stylelint downloads for two consecutive months, a figure recorded in the release checklist. Number that flips it: v16 under 10% before 4.0 ships.
findings.truth_reason: COUNCIL:78: 'peer ^17 || ^18; drop Stylelint 16 and Node 20'; `gh issue view 172` body: 'Stylelint 16 and 17 stay supported', naming no API that 16 lacks; ROADMAP:28 repeats the council. api.npmjs.org versions/stylelint/last-week: v17 6,481,807 (46.09%), v16 4,113,365 (29.25%) of 14,062,144; 17.0.0 published 2026-01-15. test/compat/floor-compat.test.js exists; CONTRIBUTING:122 documents the 16.0.0 floor. No document resolves the contradiction.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified contradiction: council 4.0 scope drops Stylelint 16, #172 says 16 stays. v16 is 29% of Stylelint downloads and design-system monorepos sit there; dropping it in a major sold as stable costs ds-team adoption for no named API need. findings.title: Add a token-file check so the scale's own input is on base
findings.claim: Design-token tooling is where the ds-team persona lives: Style Dictionary 8.6M/month, Terrazzo +334% with 29 lint rules on token files, none checking a dimension against a spacing base. Rhythmguard's audit already runs on a directory holding only a DTCG file and prints the scale, unused tokens and ladder checks, but it accepted `--space-7: 26px` in a 4px system and reported 'No issues found'. The token repository's CI is where that team would gate, and Rhythmguard has no command for it, no mention of DTCG, Style Dictionary or Tokens Studio on its front page, and no Terrazzo plugin.
findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/rg-review-ecosystem-bets/tokens-only: `rhythmguard audit . --scale auto --token-source tokens/tokens.json` → 'Scale 0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 26, 32 ... Defined but unused 8 ... Token ladders 1 checked (0 collapsed, 0 under 2px apart, 0 inverted steps) ... No issues found'. src/audit/token-ladders.js:7-22 (collapsed, too close, inverted only). https://terrazzo.app/docs/linting/ (29 rules, custom-rule API, no scale rule). api.npmjs.org: style-dictionary 8,628,729/month; @terrazzo/cli 179,006/week. `grep -i dtcg README.md` → nothing.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: A design engineer whose scale lives in a token package wants the gate in that package's CI; a linter that only speaks once CSS exists is a second tool in the app repos, the install they are least likely to approve.
findings.proposal: Add `rhythmguard tokens <file|dir>` (or `audit --tokens-only`): derive the base unit from the token set, report off-base steps (26px on a 4px base), duplicate values, ladder problems and the resulting scale, in text and JSON, with `--fail-on-off-base`; reuse src/audit/contract.js and token-ladders.js. Name DTCG 2025.10, Style Dictionary, Tokens Studio and Figma exports in the README's first screen. If Terrazzo users ask, wrap the same check as a Terrazzo lint plugin over src/core. Number that flips it: one token-package repository adopting it, or Terrazzo passing 1M downloads a month.
findings.correction: Terrazzo ships 27 token-file lint rules (core/valid-dimension checks format and units only; a custom-rule API exists; nothing checks a dimension against a base or scale), not 29. Nothing else in the claim changes.
findings.truth_reason: Audit re-run on the DTCG file with --space-7: 26px printed 'Scale 0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 26, 32', 'Defined but unused 8', ladders '0 collapsed, 0 under 2px apart, 0 inverted' and 'No issues found'. token-ladders.js:7-22 checks only those three; no off-base code in src/audit; the CLI has no tokens command; README never mentions DTCG, Style Dictionary, Tokens Studio or Figma; @terrazzo/cli 179,006 last week. Terrazzo's linting page lists 27 rules, not 29.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: audit with --token-source accepts 26px into a 4px scale (0,4,8,12,16,20,24,26,32), ladder check passes, 'No issues found'; without the flag it ignores tokens.json entirely. Terrazzo's 27 rules check no base either. Gives ds-team a gate in the token package's CI; conflicts with the freeze as a new command.

findings.title: Accept Figma and Tokens Studio exports as scale sources
findings.claim: The council stop-listed 'a Figma bridge', but the designer's scale lives in Figma variables, and every AI builder named in the goal (Figma Make, Claude Design, v0, Lovable) reads it from there. Figma's native export writes a DTCG-aligned JSON per mode, Tokens Studio writes unitless strings, and the REST API (Enterprise only) returns `valuesByMode` floats; Rhythmguard drops all three because spacing values arrive without units and unitless numbers are treated as ratios. OpenCRVS copied 14 steps from a Figma collection by hand on 2026-11-02 and noted the variables had been renamed two days earlier. A reader for exported files is a token-sources change, not a bridge.
findings.evidence: scale-and-tokens map (verified by its probes): 'Figma variables exports ... read as nothing, and the warning wrongly suggests a tokenPattern'; 'Tokens Studio exports (unitless string values like "4") ... read as tokens without lengths'. `grep -i figma src/core/token-sources.js` → no match. https://atomize.tools/blog/figma-variables-export-json/ (collection export, one JSON per mode, $value/$type/$extensions; FLOAT type mapping not shown, hence the lower confidence). https://developers.figma.com/docs/rest-api/variables/ ('you must have a Full seat in an Enterprise org'). https://github.com/opencrvs/opencrvs-core/issues/12627. docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:98 ('A Figma bridge').
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: An AI-assisted designer's only scale is the Figma collection; if the linter cannot read its export, the scale is retyped by hand, drifts on rename, and the designer concludes the tool is for developers only.
findings.proposal: In src/core/token-sources.js add an opt-in `unitless: "px"` per source, auto-enabled for files carrying a Figma `$extensions` key or Tokens Studio `$metadata.json` siblings: a JSON number or numeric string under a group whose name matches the spacing pattern becomes `<n>px`. Add fixtures for a Figma collection export (one mode), a Tokens Studio set and a REST `valuesByMode` dump; let quickstart list exported `*.tokens.json`. Document 'export the collection from Figma, point scaleSources at it'. Number that returns it to the stop list: Figma shipping native DTCG dimension export with units (announced at Schema 2025), which the existing reader would then take as is.
findings.truth_reason: Probe: a Figma-style export (`$type: number`, bare `$value`, `$extensions.com.figma`), a Tokens Studio set (`value: "16"`, `type: spacing`) and a REST valuesByMode dump each returned scale source `fallback`, rejected null, no warning, while bare numbers in flat JSON were read as px. No 'figma' in token-sources.js; unitless values dropped (:524-527, DTCG numbers :1216-1231). opencrvs#12627 body: 14 `space/*` steps read 2026-11-02, renamed 2026-10-31. COUNCIL:98,158 and examples/audit-figma-export.mjs (audit to Figma payload) verified.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: a Figma-style $type number export and a Tokens Studio unitless set both fall to the fallback scale, '0 of 6 resolve'. The designer's scale lives in Figma, so the ai-assisted and ds-team personas retype it by hand. A reader option in token-sources, not the stop-listed bridge; limited to name-matched spacing groups.
findings.relates_to: docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:98 (stop list 'Figma bridge'; this is a file reader, so it sits outside that item but should be said so explicitly), :158 (member B's Figma-variables diff); #163; examples/audit-figma-export.mjs (opposite direction)

findings.title: Write the Biome decision down with a feature trigger
findings.claim: Biome is 25.6M weekly downloads (1.8x Stylelint), ships about 48 CSS rules and a plugin system, and is absent from the council's stop list; ROADMAP says 'revisit when Biome ships JS plugins'. Biome has shipped JS plugins (Developer Preview), so that trigger reads as met, yet the umbrella issue lists 'Rule options' and 'Support other languages, starting from CSS' as unchecked future work, and GritQL CSS plugins take no options and cannot load a token file. A token-aware scale rule still cannot be expressed there, and nobody in the project is subscribed to the issue that will change that.
findings.evidence: api.npmjs.org last-week: @biomejs/biome 25,585,055 vs stylelint 14,062,144. https://biomejs.dev/linter/plugins/ ('JavaScript plugins are in the Developer Preview stage'; GritQL 'supports JavaScript, CSS, and JSON target languages'). biomejs/biome#11420 body ('Future possibilities: Rule options ... Support other languages, starting from CSS', unchecked, 2026-11-05). ROADMAP.md:166 ('Revisit when Biome ships JS plugins or Oxlint lints CSS'); docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:98 (no Biome entry); docs/ESLINT_PLAN.md:94.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: Biome is the one fast host where CSS plugins exist and a scale rule would be first; a vague trigger means the window opens unnoticed, and a competitor with a Rust rule in Biome core would take the solo-dev CSS user for good.
findings.proposal: Add Biome to the stop list with a three-part trigger: JS plugins reach stable with (a) CSS file support, (b) rule options, (c) a fix API. Subscribe the maintainer to biomejs/biome#11420 and check it in the monthly competitor read already listed in ESLINT_PLAN's risks table. When all three hold, the adapter is a wrapper over src/core like src/eslint (25-line entry plus a walker), budget L. Until then, no work. Number that flips it: none; it is a feature gate, and 25.6M a week already justifies watching.
findings.correction: The Biome no is already written down with feature conditions: ESLINT_PLAN:94 ('GritQL plugins take no options and its JS plugins are a developer preview without a fix API, so a scale rule cannot be expressed there today') and ROADMAP:70 ('GritQL, which cannot load a token file'). What is inconsistent is ROADMAP:166's trigger ('Revisit when Biome ships JS plugins'), already satisfied by the Developer Preview, plus the absence of a stop-list line, a CSS-support condition for JS plugins, and a pointer to biomejs/biome#11420. The proposal reduces to aligning those three texts and naming the issue to watch.
findings.truth_reason: biomejs.dev: JavaScript plugins 'Developer Preview', GritQL 'supports JavaScript, CSS, and JSON'; biome#11420 open with unchecked 'Rule options' and 'Support other languages, starting from CSS'; 25,585,055 vs 14,062,144 last week; ROADMAP:166 trigger as quoted; COUNCIL:98 has no Biome line; no doc cites #11420. But the no is already written with feature conditions in ESLINT_PLAN:94 (no options, no fix API) and ROADMAP:70; only the trigger texts disagree.
findings.materiality_reason: Moves no persona today: Biome JS plugins lack CSS options and a fix API, so no rule can ship. Worth one line because ROADMAP:166's 'when Biome ships JS plugins' trigger already reads as met while ESLINT_PLAN:94 says the opposite; a written three-part gate prevents wasted work and a missed window.

findings.title: Keep the Oxlint path; state its limits and track the alpha weekly
findings.claim: The ESLint rules run under Oxlint through its ESLint-compatible JS plugins, contract-tested in CI on a pinned 1.88.0. Oxlint is 43.6M weekly (3.1x Stylelint), grew 304% in six months, is installed by `create-vite`, and the reference user runs it. But its plugin API is 'currently in alpha', custom parsers are unsupported so Vue, Svelte and Astro templates are never linted there, it lints no CSS (request open since September, 7 reactions, no maintainer reply), and 1.91.0 has shipped since the pin. The README claims the Oxlint test without the template caveat, and the weekly early-warning job covers Stylelint only.

Registry: oxlint 1.91.0 (2026-11-03). api.npmjs.org last-week oxlint 43,593,905. https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter/js-plugins.html ('JS plugins are currently in alpha'; 'Custom file formats and parsers' unsupported). oxc-project/oxc#26324 (open, 2 comments, 7 reactions, updated 2026-09-08). README.md:147. doctor-school/ds-platform package.json `lint` script runs oxlint; docs/ESLINT_PLAN.md:30 (create-vite installs Oxlint).

State in README.md and the ESLint package README that Oxlint plugins are alpha and skip Vue, Svelte and Astro templates, pointing those users to the Stylelint `postcss-html` path or ESLint. Bump the pin on each release. Number that flips it to more investment: Oxlint ships CSS linting (#26324) or stable plugins; then build the CSS adapter there before anyone else does.

findings.title: Agent skill lives where no skills CLI or marketplace looks
findings.claim: The only agent-facing artifact, the generated SKILL.md, sits at agents/claude-code/SKILL.md. There is no .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, so `claude plugin marketplace add` fails too. oxlint-tailwindcss (1.19M downloads/month) ships skills/oxlint-tailwindcss/SKILL.md plus .claude-plugin/marketplace.json and is indexed on skills.sh. The README offers only `init --agents` for three runtimes; the skills CLI covers 74 agents. Rhythmguard appears in AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, SKILL.md or .mdc files only in the maintainer's own repositories.
findings.evidence: curl skills.sh/api/search?q=rhythmguard -> count 0; skills.sh/PetriLahdelma/stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard -> 404, skills.sh/sergioazoc/oxlint-tailwindcss -> 200; vercel-labs/skills docs/creating-skills.md lines 49-90 (discovery paths); scripts/build-agents.mjs:28-49 (targets claude-code/SKILL.md, cursor/rhythmguard.mdc, copilot/copilot-instructions.md); gh api repos/sergioazoc/oxlint-tailwindcss/git/trees/main -> skills/oxlint-tailwindcss/SKILL.md and .claude-plugin/marketplace.json; gh api search/code '"rhythmguard" filename:SKILL.md' -> 2 hits, both PetriLahdelma; docs/agents.md in vercel-labs/skills: 74 agent rows

Extend the drift test to the new files. Put `npx skills add PetriLahdelma/stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard` and `claude plugin marketplace add PetriLahdelma/stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard` in the README's agent bullet above `init --agents`. findings.title: No shadcn registry item for the v0, Lovable and shadcn crowd
findings.claim: The shadcn registry is the install path AI builders and shadcn projects share: `npx shadcn add <url>` takes a JSON item that can carry devDependencies, `registry:file` entries with project-root targets such as `~/foo.config.js`, and a `docs` message shown after install. @shadcn/lint reached 845 package.json repositories in nine weeks inside that ecosystem. Rhythmguard publishes nothing in that format, although its GitHub Pages host already serves docs/ and could serve the item with no new infrastructure. Storybook (addon-mcp 10.4M downloads/month, storybook-design-token 456k) is the other place design-system teams install from, but an addon is product work under the freeze; a registry item is packaging.

Document `npx shadcn add https://petrilahdelma.github.io/stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard/r/rhythmguard.json` in README and SETUP.md.
findings.correction: The registry format and hosting facts hold, but @shadcn/lint reached 845 repos through npm install plus SETUP.md, not npx shadcn add, so that number cannot support 'the shadcn registry is the install path AI builders share'; the case for a registry item rests on the format's capabilities alone and lacks an adoption example.

findings.title: Monorepos get one scale per invocation; per-package config is ignored
findings.claim: `.rhythmguardrc.json`, `scaleSources` relative paths and token-package discovery are keyed to `process.cwd()`, never to the linted file's package. From a monorepo root, the audit reports `fallback` for every workspace, the Stylelint rule falls back to `rhythmic-4` with a note although each package has its own rc, and `doctor` says the rc file does not exist. A DS team whose apps live in one repository must run one invocation per package, from inside it, or every package is judged against a guessed scale.
findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/rg-review-ds-team-fit/mono: `node src/cli/index.js audit ./packages --scale auto --format json` from the root gives `source: fallback, files: []` and reports app-b's 20px as off-scale although packages/app-b/.rhythmguardrc.json sets `scale: [0,5,10,20,40]`; from packages/app-a the same audit prints `Scale source token-sources (../tokens/dist/tokens.json)`. Stylelint from the root with `scale: "auto"`: both files end with `No spacing tokens were found for scale "auto"; using preset "rhythmic-4"`. `doctor` from the root: `.rhythmguardrc.json not found`. Code: src/core/scale-inference.js:158,238,487,530 (process.cwd()).
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The council's own user runs a monorepo (COUNCIL:65). A DS lead cannot mandate a gate that reports a different scale depending on which directory CI happens to run from, and cannot explain to five app teams why their editor and the root job disagree.
findings.proposal: Resolve configuration from the linted file outward: walk from the file's directory to the first `package.json` (or `.rhythmguardrc.json`), read that rc, discover token packages from that package.json, and resolve `scaleSources` relative to it; cache per directory with the existing mtime cache. In the audit, group scanned files by nearest package, resolve one scale per package, and add `contracts.packages[]` with `{ name, dir, scale, source, files }`; text output prints a scale table instead of one line. Document the Stylelint `overrides` workaround until then.
findings.truth_reason: Reran the mono probe: the root audit reports source fallback, files [], and flags app-b's 20px although packages/app-b/.rhythmguardrc.json sets [0,5,10,20,40]; from packages/app-a it prints token-sources (../tokens/dist/tokens.json); Stylelint from the root appends the rhythmic-4 fallback note to both files; doctor from the root says the rc is not found. process.cwd() at scale-inference.js:158, 238, 487, 530 verified. #174 open; COUNCIL:88 reads 'Per-workspace scales (#174) only on request'.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: rc, scaleSources and package discovery all key on process.cwd() (scale-inference.js:158,238,487,530). The stated persona (apps in a monorepo, tokens as workspace deps) gets rhythmic-4 from a root run with only a note. Council parks #174 as 'only on request', which conflicts. Shares a root cause with ds-05; fix both together.

findings.title: Findings are keyed on message text, which changes in minors
findings.claim: The audit decides a finding's type and value by regex over Stylelint message text, baselines key on that type, and message wording has changed in eight 'Messages' changelog sections during 3.x. CHANGELOG.md admits teams keying a baseline on text will see resolved-plus-new pairs. There is no message snapshot test, no SURFACE.json budget and no exported findingKey; all three are 4.0 promises. A DS lead who commits a baseline in five repos has no guarantee a minor bump keeps it valid.
findings.evidence: src/audit/scan/stylesheets.js:205-216 (four regexes over `text` decide type and value); CHANGELOG.md:255 'Message text changes are listed here, so teams that key a warning baseline on message text know which warnings will reappear as resolved-plus-new pairs'; `grep -c '^#\+ .*Messages' CHANGELOG.md` → 8; `ls test/contracts/` → 8 files, none a message snapshot; `grep -rn findingKey src types` → only internal baseline helpers (src/audit/baseline.js:52,271,286); docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:80-81,107 ('5 releases since 3.3').
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The buyer pays in trust and 'findings never change within a major' is the thesis. Until the contract is enforced by a test, every minor is a risk to a committed baseline, which is the one artifact the CI gate depends on.
findings.proposal: Do the structural part of 4.0 now, additively: move every message template into one module with a parser beside it, make the audit use that parser, and add a contract test that round-trips each template and snapshots the strings (fails on any change outside a major). Export `findingKey(finding)` from `stylelint-plugin-rhythmguard/audit` and key baselines on it. Commit `SURFACE.json` (rules, options, exports, presets, message ids) with a test that diffs it. None of this changes reports, so it fits the freeze.
findings.truth_reason: stylesheets.js:205-216 derives type and value from four regexes over warning text, and getCssFindingType falls through to 'off-scale' with a null value when nothing matches, so a reworded message silently rekeys findings. CHANGELOG:255 sentence verified verbatim; 8 '### Messages' headings; test/contracts holds 8 files, none a message snapshot; findingKey exists only as baseline.js internals, nothing exported from src or types; COUNCIL:80-81 and :107 confirm snapshot test, SURFACE.json and findingKey as 4.0 promises.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: audit types findings by regex over message text; 8 Messages sections in 3.x; no findingKey export, SURFACE.json or snapshot test. But the audit baseline is already content-keyed, so wording changes only break it when a regex stops matching. Hygiene that underpins the trust thesis and 4.0; no persona bounces on it today.
findings.relates_to: #172 (4.0 scope); docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:80-81; quality-engineering map gap 3

findings.title: A published shared config cannot point at the token package portably
findings.claim: `scaleSources` paths resolve from `process.cwd()`, not from the config that declares them, and bare package specifiers are rejected. A DS team's `@acme/stylelint-config` with `scaleSources: ["node_modules/@acme/tokens/dist/tokens.json"]` works from the repo root and silently falls back to `rhythmic-4` from a workspace directory. `require.resolve()` in a JS config works but no doc mentions it, and JSON configs cannot do it. FOR_CONFIG_AUTHORS.md shows the cwd-relative form as the recommended pattern.
findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/rg-review-ds-team-fit/mono with packages/app-a/.stylelintrc.json extending a hoisted @acme/stylelint-config: from the root the 13px finding has no note; from packages/app-a (rc removed) it ends `Token source not found: node_modules/@acme/tokens/dist/tokens.json` and uses rhythmic-4. `scaleSources: ['@acme/tokens/dist/tokens.json']` → `Token source not found` from anywhere, and `audit --token-source @acme/tokens/dist/tokens.json` → `Scale source fallback`. `scaleSources: [require.resolve('@acme/tokens/dist/tokens.json')]` works. `grep -rn 'require.resolve' docs README.md` → nothing. src/core/scale-inference.js:158; docs/FOR_CONFIG_AUTHORS.md:60-78.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The thing a DS team publishes to its consumers is a config that names the token package. If that config only works when lint runs from the right directory, the team cannot ship it to five repos with confidence, and the fallback is silent in CI.
findings.proposal: Accept package specifiers in `scaleSources`, `audit.tokenSources` and `--token-source`: when an entry is not a path (no leading `.`, `/` or drive), resolve it with `createRequire(<linted file or cwd>/package.json).resolve(spec)`, so hoisted and pnpm layouts both work. Resolve relative entries from the config file's directory when Stylelint exposes it, else from the nearest package.json upward. Make a missing token source an error in `audit` (exit 1), as a missing `--config` is. Document the `require.resolve` pattern for JS configs in FOR_CONFIG_AUTHORS.md.
findings.truth_reason: Reran every variant: from the root the hoisted config resolves (13px finding, no note); from packages/app-a with its rc removed the same config ends 'Token source not found: node_modules/@acme/tokens/dist/tokens.json' and uses rhythmic-4; bare '@acme/tokens/dist/tokens.json' is 'not found' from the root; require.resolve works; audit --token-source with the bare specifier prints 'Scale source fallback'. token-source-entries.js resolves against baseDir = process.cwd() with no specifier branch; FOR_CONFIG_AUTHORS:60-78 recommends the cwd-relative path; no require.resolve in docs or READMEs.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: rule scaleSources resolve from process.cwd() (scale-inference.js:158); a bare specifier becomes a not-found warning and silent fallback; FOR_CONFIG_AUTHORS.md:70 recommends the cwd-relative form; require.resolve is undocumented. This is the persona's exact shape (token package plus shared config) and the failure is silent in CI. S effort, no plan conflict.
findings.relates_to: #174 (same root cause); audit-and-cli map gap on missing --token-source exiting 0; docs/FOR_CONFIG_AUTHORS.md:60-78

findings.title: Token sets, not single files: aliases across files and dirs unread
findings.claim: Token sources must be single files: no directories, globs, YAML or JSON5. Aliases resolve within one file only, so a semantic file alone contributes nothing, silently. Even when both files are listed, the unresolved alias text (`{space.4}`) is kept as a second value, so the chains report says only 7 of 10 tokens resolve. Figma variables exports (arrays of collections) read as nothing and the warning suggests a `tokenPattern` that cannot help. Style Dictionary and Tokens Studio projects, the persona's shape, are multi-file by convention.
findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/rg-review-ds-team-fit/dtcg with `--token-source ./primitive.json --token-source ./semantic.json`: `contracts.tokens.definedTokens` has `--space-inset-md` values `["var(--space-4)","{space.4}"]`, chains summary `on-scale 7, non-length 3`, markdown '7 of 10 spacing tokens resolve to the scale; 3 non-length'. scale-and-tokens map (verified in that stage): semantic.json alone → scale null, no warning (src/core/token-sources.js:1016-1020,1173-1182); glob → 'Token source not found', directory → EISDIR, YAML → JSON parse error (token-sources.js:136-153,240-247); Figma export arrays skipped (token-sources.js:1048-1050). 31 of 57 benchmark repos end on fallback (docs/QUIET_BENCHMARK.md).
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The 4.0 thesis is 'token-file-native'. A DS team's tokens are a directory of DTCG files plus a Figma or Tokens Studio export; today they must hand-enumerate build outputs and still get a misleading chain count. The council named reading these directly as the doctor-school unblocker.
findings.proposal: Treat token sources as one set: accept directories and globs (expand to `.json`, `.tokens.json`, `.css`, `.scss`), parse all files into one token graph, resolve `{alias}` and `$ref` across the set, and store the resolved length as the definition value (drop the alias text) so chains and conflicts are correct. Warn when an alias cannot resolve (`{space.4} in semantic.json: not in the set`) and when a source yields tokens but no lengths. Add a `figma-variables` format for the plugin/REST export shape (collections, modes, variables), reading the default mode. Keep this additive to the current single-file behaviour.
findings.truth_reason: Reran: both files listed gives --space-inset-md values ['var(--space-4)','{space.4}'], chains 7 on-scale 3 non-length, markdown '7 of 10 spacing tokens resolve to the scale; 3 non-length'; glob 'Token source not found', directory EISDIR, YAML 'Unable to parse'; a Figma variables array yields no tokens and the warning recommends tokenPattern although arrays are skipped (token-sources.js:1048-1050); semantic.json alone contributes nothing with warnings []. detectSourceFormat (240-247) and same-file lookupJsonReference (1173-1182) verified; QUIET_BENCHMARK has 31 fallback rows.
findings.materiality_reason: Map-verified: single files only, aliases resolve within one file, a semantic file contributes nothing silently, Figma variable exports are unreadable with a misleading hint. The 4.0 thesis is token-file-native and the persona's tokens are multi-file by convention. Council Q2 2027 covers the alias part; no competitor reads DTCG sets for CSS linting.
findings.relates_to: docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:88 (Q2: read Style Dictionary output and DTCG with aliases directly); #163; scale-and-tokens map gaps 3, 6, 7, 11; Figma bridge is on the stop list (a file reader is not a bridge)

findings.title: Brands, density and modes collapse into one union scale
findings.claim: Two mode files for the same token names merge into a union scale, so a value that is off-scale in every mode passes, and tokens that overlap across modes are reported as 'conflicting'. `$extensions` mode data, Tokens Studio `$themes.json` sets and DTCG resolver documents are ignored. Multi-brand and compact/comfortable density are how multi-product design systems ship; the tool cannot say which mode a value is on-scale for.
findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/rg-review-ds-team-fit/brands with comfortable.json (8,16,24,32) and compact.json (6,12,18,24) as `--token-source`: `contracts.scale.values` [0,6,8,12,16,18,24,32], `source token-sources`, `rejected null`; `padding: 18px; margin: 32px; gap: 6px` yield no off-scale finding; `conflictingTokens [{tokens:['--space-3','--space-4'], value:'24px'}]`. src/core/token-sources.js:1328-1355 (addDefinition unions values), 1033-1071 (only `$value` read).
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: Council member B named the single project-level scale as the one capability gap real design-system practice shows. A DS lead running two brands cannot adopt a gate that accepts the union of both scales and then flags the overlap as a token conflict.
findings.proposal: Introduce a mode dimension without new rule options: a token-source entry may carry `mode` (or a `$themes.json`/resolver file is read for sets), definitions keep values per mode, and the audit resolves one scale per mode. A literal is on-scale when it is on the scale of the mode its declaration context selects (default mode unless a selector or `@media` matches a declared mode selector), otherwise it is reported with the nearest steps of the default mode. Report `contracts.scale.modes[]` and drop the conflict report for tokens whose values differ only across modes. Start with the default mode only (S) and add per-mode checking after.
findings.correction: Two mode files for the same token names merge into one union scale, so a value that is on-scale in only one mode (18px compact, 32px comfortable) passes in any context, one rule can mix modes undetected, and tokens whose values differ only by mode are reported as 'conflicting'; $extensions mode data, Tokens Studio $themes.json sets and DTCG resolver documents are ignored. A value off-scale in every mode is still reported, since the union holds only mode values.
findings.truth_reason: Reran: union scale [0,6,8,12,16,18,24,32], source token-sources, rejected null, no off-scale finding for 18px, 32px or 6px, conflictingTokens [--space-3, --space-4] at 24px; addDefinition (token-sources.js:1328-1355) unions values and no code reads $themes, $extensions or a resolver. But a union cannot pass a value that is off-scale in every mode: each probe value is on one mode's scale. The defect is cross-mode leakage plus the spurious conflict, not the sentence as written.
findings.materiality_reason: The union scale is wrong (accepts values off-scale in every mode), but only multi-brand or density systems hit it, after the single-scale path works. Council B named it and the council asked who the users are beyond one comment. L effort; the default-mode-only first slice is the right start.
findings.relates_to: docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:158 (B critique, no issue); feature freeze (new option) conflicts; scale-and-tokens map gap 4

findings.title: Radius, size and typography scales are second-class in the audit
findings.claim: `audit.scales` checks radius, size and typography per group and the messages name the right nearest steps, but the JSON contract, text and markdown report only the spacing scale's values and source, `--plan` returns `nearest: []` for the other groups although the rule computed them, token chains consider spacing names only, the badge counts spacing, and the ESLint rule covers spacing only. A DS team has five scales; the product reports provenance for one.
findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/rg-review-ds-team-fit/groups (`audit.scales: { radius: 'auto', typography: 'auto' }` over one DTCG file): findings read 'Use radius scale values (nearest: 6px or 10px)' and 'Use typography scale values (nearest: 14px or 16px)', but `Object.keys(contracts.scale)` = cleanliness, files, offScaleProperties, offScaleValues, rejected, source, tokenOpportunities, values (spacing only); text prints only 'Scale 0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24'; `--plan` gives `nearest []` for 15px font-size and 7px border-radius. src/audit/token-chains.js:27 (SPACING_TOKEN_NAME); docs/AUDIT.md:33 documents the empty nearest for auto groups; rules-core map gap 1 (typography group autofixes letter-spacing onto the font-size ladder).
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: A DS lead reports on radius and type ladders as well as spacing. If the report cannot say which radius scale was used or what the nearest radius step is, the other four scales cannot be gated with the same confidence as spacing, and the team keeps a second tool for them.
findings.proposal: Resolve each group's scale once in the audit (already done per stylesheet in the rule) and carry it in the contract as `contracts.scales.<group> = { values, source, files, rejected }`, keeping `contracts.scale` as the spacing alias. Have `--plan` take nearest steps from the resolved group scale. Extend chains to accept a `kind` (radius, typography, size) using the existing `createTokenKindMatcher`, and print one scale line per configured group in text and markdown. Remove letter-spacing and word-spacing from the typography group's autofix. Additive JSON keys keep the 2.0 contract valid.
findings.truth_reason: Reran: findings read 'Use radius scale values (nearest: 6px or 10px)' and 'Use typography scale values (nearest: 14px or 16px)', yet contracts.scale has only cleanliness, files, offScaleProperties, offScaleValues, rejected, source, tokenOpportunities, values and there is no contracts.scales; text prints one Scale line; --plan gives nearest [] for 15px and 7px; AUDIT.md:33 documents it; token-chains.js SPACING_TOKEN_NAME limits chains to spacing names; the ESLint schema is spacing-only. Minor: the badge label says spacing but its number counts all findings.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: one contracts.scale, one scale line in text and markdown, chains match spacing names only, badge counts spacing, ESLint analyses spacing only. DS teams gate radius and type too, but spacing is the entry point and rule-level checks already work; provenance for other groups matters after spacing adoption.
findings.relates_to: docs/AUDIT.md:33; docs/rules/use-scale.md (A scale per property group); rules-core map gap 1; #172 (contract changes land in 4.0)

findings.title: No token-coverage number; unused-token counts ignore alias use
findings.claim: The only headline metric is file-level cleanliness (share of files with zero findings), which saturates on dense repos and is not what a DS lead reports upward; coverage by property is. There is no 'share of spacing declarations that use a token' anywhere. The unused-token list counts `var()` hits only, so when the token build lives outside the audited directory, primitives referenced by the semantic tokens the CSS does use are listed as unused (7 of 10 in the probe), the opposite of what the token package's adoption looks like.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn -i 'coverage' src/audit src/cli` → only a skip-directory name (src/audit/shared.js:32); src/audit/contract.js:366-372 (cleanliness = files without findings). Probe /tmp/rg-review-ds-team-fit/dtcg with the SD build (tokens.css) moved out of ./src and the DTCG files as sources: usedTokens `--space-2 --space-chip-x --space-inset-md`, unusedTokens 7 of 10 including `--space-4` and `--space-6`, which the used `--space-inset-md` and `--space-stack-lg` alias; src/audit/contract.js:66,107-124 (uses are regex hits on `var(` in scanned CSS only). docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:158 ('cleanliness is not a number DS leads report upward, coverage by property is'). Supernova sells 'adoption analytics on which tokens and components teams use' (landscape map).
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: A DS lead justifies the gate with adoption numbers. A tool whose one score is 0% on every real repo and whose unused-token table contradicts the token package cannot be the report they bring to a review.
findings.proposal: Add `summary.tokenCoverage` and `contracts.scale.coverageByProperty`: during the Stylelint pass count every spacing-group declaration (the rule already visits them) and classify each as token (`var()`/`theme()`/`token()`), on-scale literal, or off-scale literal; coverage = token / total, reported overall, per property and per file. Put coverage on the badge (`--badge-metric coverage`) and in `--min-coverage` as a gate. In the token contract, count a token as used when a used token's chain passes through it, and separate 'unused in CSS' from 'unused anywhere'. Keep cleanliness for compatibility.
findings.correction: Evidence: in the probe only --space-4 is wrongly listed as unused (the used --space-inset-md aliases it); --space-6 is aliased by --space-stack-lg, which card.css never references, so it is correctly unused. The claim that unused-token counts ignore alias use holds on --space-4, the 7-of-10 count is accurate, and the absence of any coverage metric is confirmed.
findings.truth_reason: grep -i coverage under src/audit and src/cli hits only the skip-dir name (shared.js:32); summary keys carry no coverage; cleanliness is file-level (contract.js:366-372); uses are regex var( hits in collectTokenUses. Reran with tokens.css moved out: used --space-2, --space-chip-x, --space-inset-md; unused 7 of 10 including --space-4 and --space-6. But --space-stack-lg is itself unused by the CSS, so only --space-4 (aliased by the used --space-inset-md) shows alias blindness; --space-6 is correctly unused.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: cleanliness is file-granular (0% on the corpus, 20% on a five-file fixture) and unused tokens are defined-minus-var()-hits (contract.js:66). The buyer approves the gate on numbers; the only headline number is degenerate and the unused table contradicts the token package. Council B named coverage-by-property as what leads report. Compounds with ds-10.
findings.relates_to: docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:158; audit-and-cli map gap on file-granular cleanliness; docs/STATE_OF_SPACING.md uses drift density already

findings.title: No trend over time; HTML is a JSON dump; API examples broken
findings.claim: A baseline is one snapshot and the badge is one number; nothing stores or renders a series, and nothing rolls up five repositories. `--format html` is four tiles, five tables and the entire JSON in a `<pre>`, poorer than the markdown comment. Both shipped API consumers, the dashboard and the Figma export, read `finding.message`, a field findings never carry, so their message columns are empty. CI_ADOPTION.md has no guidance for more than one repository. A DS lead has nothing to show a quarterly review.
findings.evidence: src/audit/render-html.js:31-48 (tiles, tables, `<pre><code>${JSON.stringify(contractReport)}`); `grep -rn -i 'history|trend' src/audit src/cli` → nothing; examples/audit-figma-export.mjs:64 `message: finding.message || ''` and examples/audit-dashboard.mjs:77 while findings carry `text` (src/audit/scan/stylesheets.js:218-234); package.json `files` ships `examples`; `grep -n -i 'monorepo|fleet|history|trend|repos' docs/CI_ADOPTION.md` → nothing; audit map: 161 MB HTML at 288k findings.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: Mandating across 5+ repos is a management decision that needs a before-and-after. Supernova and Knapsack sell the drift chart; Rhythmguard produces the data and throws the series away, so the lead builds a dashboard by hand or picks the vendor.
findings.proposal: Add `--format summary`: a 1 KB JSON (date, commit, scale source, findings by type, cleanliness, coverage, resolved/new since baseline) that teams commit under `.rhythmguard/history/` or upload as a CI artifact. Add `rhythmguard report <summary files or dirs> --output drift.html`: a static, dependency-free page with one row per repository (latest numbers, scale source, trend sparkline from its summaries) and per-repo detail. Rebuild `--format html` on the same renderer with a findings table and per-file drill-down, not the raw JSON. Fix the two examples to read `text`, and add a contract test that runs them. Static only; no hosted service.
findings.truth_reason: render-html.js:29-48 renders four tiles, five tables and the whole contract JSON inside <pre><code>; grep -i 'history|trend' under src/audit and src/cli finds nothing; examples/audit-figma-export.mjs:64 and audit-dashboard.mjs:77 read finding.message while stylesheet and template findings carry text (stylesheets.js:218-234, templates.js:46,92); package.json files ships examples; no test references examples/. One evidence nit: the CI_ADOPTION.md grep does match 'repos' incidentally at lines 77 and 88, but neither is multi-repository guidance.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: HTML embeds the full JSON in a pre, both examples read finding.message, CI_ADOPTION.md has no multi-repo guidance. A lead already gets resolved/new per run from the baseline, and the council deferred fleet until two teams ask. The static summary plus report slice is plan-compatible but lands after adoption, not before it.
findings.relates_to: docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:160 (A: static dashboards; `fleet` only if two teams ask); stop list: hosted dashboard (a static page is not one); #165 SARIF; audit-and-cli map gaps on html and examples

findings.title: Trust statement missing: telemetry, code execution, Windows
findings.claim: SECURITY.md says nothing about network access or telemetry; the only 'Makes no network requests' line is in the CLI package README. `tailwindConfigPath` executes the project's Tailwind config with `require()` and then a spawned `node -e` dynamic import, and no rule doc says so. CI has no Windows or macOS row and no Windows run is recorded, while the persona runs Windows laptops. An enterprise security reviewer reads SECURITY.md and the rule docs; both are silent on exactly what they check.
findings.evidence: SECURITY.md (31 lines, no network/telemetry text); packages/rhythmguard/README.md:50 'Makes no network requests'; src/core/token-map.js:280 `require(resolvedPath)` and :293 `spawnSync` of `node -e` importing the user's config; `grep -n -i 'execut|child process' docs/rules/use-scale.md docs/rules/prefer-token.md docs/TAILWIND.md` → nothing; `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs-on: three self-hosted Linux rows and ubuntu-latest, no windows; ROADMAP.md:122-123 lists 'A Windows run' and 'A no-network, no-telemetry statement in SECURITY.md' as open; docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:65 (buyer pays in trust, no telemetry).
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: The council says the buyer pays in trust. An org-wide mandate goes through a security review that asks three questions: does it phone home, does it run our code, does it work on our laptops. Today the answers exist only in the maintainer's head and a CLI README line.
findings.proposal: Add a 'What this package does and does not do' section to SECURITY.md: no network requests, no telemetry, no file writes outside `--write`/`--fix`/`--write-baseline`, the one place project code is executed (`tailwindConfigPath`, with the child-process detail) and how to avoid it (`scaleSources` on the built CSS), npm provenance and how to verify it. Say the same in docs/rules/use-scale.md and prefer-token.md next to `tailwindConfigPath`. Add one GitHub-hosted `windows-latest` CI row running the CLI and baseline tests (paths are already normalised in src/audit/shared.js:51 and baseline.js:50) and record the run in README.md:147.
findings.truth_reason: SECURITY.md (31 lines) has no network or telemetry statement; packages/rhythmguard/README.md:50 'Makes no network requests'; token-map.js:280 require(resolvedPath) and a spawnSync of node -e with a 5 s timeout at :324 (the finding's :293 is inside the script builder, not the spawn itself); grep for execut|child process in use-scale.md, prefer-token.md and TAILWIND.md finds nothing; ci.yml runs-on is three self-hosted rows plus ubuntu-latest; ROADMAP:121-123 lists a Windows run and the no-telemetry statement as open; COUNCIL:65 verified.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: SECURITY.md is reporting policy only, the no-network line lives in the CLI README, tailwindConfigPath require()s and spawns node on project code with no doc mention, CI has no Windows row. Gates an org-wide mandate at security review, late in the journey; S effort; ROADMAP already lists all three.
findings.relates_to: ROADMAP.md:122-123; #174 (Windows noted there per the quality map); scale-and-tokens quality note on tailwindConfigPath execution

findings.title: Decisions and token sources cannot be shared across repositories
findings.claim: `.rhythmguardrc.json` has no `extends`: a DS team's `allow 2px on border-*`, `adopt 22px as --space-chip-x` and `tokenSources` must be copied into every repository and kept in sync by hand. The rc is read from the working directory only, the ESLint rule ignores decisions entirely, and the agent pack written by `init --agents` is seven static sentences with no scale or token names. What a DS team can publish to five consumer repos today is a Stylelint config; the decisions, the token source list and the agent context stay per-repo copies.
findings.evidence: `grep -n -i 'extends' src/audit/config.js` → none (the only hit is an error message about presets); src/core/scale-inference.js:382-388 (rc read from cwd); src/audit/config.js:27-247 (one file, no composition); `grep -rn decision src/eslint` → only a message string; docs/AUDIT.md:152-215 (decisions and tokenSources documented as a per-project file); agents/claude-code/SKILL.md:6-18 (static bullets, no project data); src/cli/init.js:247-277 copies files verbatim.
findings.why_it_blocks_number_one: Mandating across 5+ repos means publishing one policy. Five hand-copied rc files diverge within a quarter, the ESLint side never sees the allowances, and each consumer's coding agent gets a pack that does not know the team's scale. The lead ends up policing config drift instead of spacing drift.
findings.proposal: Add `"extends": "@acme/rhythmguard-config"` to `.rhythmguardrc.json` (package or path, resolved with createRequire from the rc's directory), merging `audit.tokenSources`, `audit.scales`, `audit.ignore` and `decisions` with local entries winning by value. Make the ESLint rule read the nearest rc's decisions (ties to ds-03). Have `init --agents` render the pack from a quickstart run: the resolved scale, its source, the token names that hold each step, the team's decisions, and the exact audit command, so a DS team can commit one generated pack per consumer repo. Validate the extended file in `doctor`.
findings.truth_reason: grep -i extends in src/audit/config.js returns no hits at all (the only extends writes are Stylelint configs in init.js, quickstart.js and doctor.js); loadAuditConfig reads one file from process.cwd() with no composition; the lint reads the rc from cwd at scale-inference.js:382-388; src/eslint has no decision reading; agents/claude-code/SKILL.md is seven static bullets with no scale or token names; init.js:247-277 copies packs verbatim; AUDIT.md:152-215 documents decisions and tokenSources per project; COUNCIL:160 records C's 'rhythmguard context' proposal.
findings.materiality_reason: Verified: no extends in config.js, rc read from cwd only, ESLint ignores decisions, agent pack is static prose. Hand-copied rc files drift, but the shared Stylelint config already carries rule options and many decisions are per-repo by nature. Overlaps ds-03 (ESLint decisions) and ds-05 (portability); the agent-pack half is ai-assisted territory.
findings.relates_to: docs/COUNCIL_2027-2028.md:160 (C: `rhythmguard context` into AGENTS.md, no issue); audit-and-cli map gap on static agent packs; feature freeze (config keys, not rule options)
